_No gas means no tears: **no new gas can form in an onion that is being cooked**, so frying onions will not make the cook cry._

questionText: What is the passage mainly about?

options.label: How the tools that people write with have changed since ancient times
What pencil centers are really made of and how they developed
Why lead is dangerous for people who use pencils
How people in England first found graphite

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפטי הנושא עוברים מהטענה **a pencil contains no lead at all**, דרך מקור השם, אל התערובת של גרפיט וחימר, ולכן הקטע עוסק במה שיש באמת במרכז העיפרון ואיך הוא התפתח (הצירוף **how they developed**).

_It begins with **a pencil contains no lead at all**, then explains the old name and the clay mix: what pencil centers are and how they developed._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why did people in the 1500s believe that graphite was lead?

options.label: It was as heavy as the metal called lead.
Scientists of that time told them it was lead.
It made the same kind of marks on paper.
It was found in the same places as lead.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **It left dark marks on paper, just as lead did**, הגרפיט השאיר על הנייר סימנים כהים כמו עופרת, כלומר אותו סוג של סימנים (הצירוף **the same kind of marks**).

_Paragraph 2 says **It left dark marks on paper, just as lead did, so they believed it was a kind of lead**._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, why did people wrap graphite sticks in string?

options.label: The sticks were easy to snap and left marks on fingers.
It made the lines on paper darker and thinner.
There was not yet enough wood in England to cover the sticks.
It kept the graphite from mixing with the clay.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **because graphite breaks easily and makes fingers dirty**, המקלות נשברו בקלות ולכלכו את האצבעות, כלומר היה קל לשבור אותם (הצירוף **easy to snap**).

_Paragraph 3 gives the reason after **because**: **graphite breaks easily and makes fingers dirty**._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "scarce" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי ההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים, הצירוף **only a few places had good supplies of it**, היה גרפיט טהור רק במקומות מעטים, ולכן פירוש המילה **scarce** הוא נדיר, קשה להשיג (הצירוף **hard to find**).

_The words after the colon, **only a few places had good supplies of it**, show that **scarce** means hard to find._

questionText: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about a pencil marked H?

options.label: It probably makes darker lines than a B pencil does.
Its center probably contains more clay than a B pencil's.
It contains a small amount of lead mixed with the graphite.
It was probably made before the late 1700s.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **More clay makes the center harder** והצירוף **H, for hard**, בעיפרון שמסומן באות **H** יש כנראה יותר חימר (הצירוף **more clay**) מאשר בעיפרון שמסומן באות **B**.

_**More clay makes the center harder**, and H stands for **hard**, so an H pencil probably has more clay than a B pencil._

questionText: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: People usually prefer a reversed photograph of their own face.
People's tastes are shaped by many different forces, such as culture, age and personal experience.
Meeting something again and again can make it more appealing, up to a point.
People soon grow bored with the things they see or hear many times.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפטי הנושא עוברים מהאפקט עצמו, הצירוף **the mere-exposure effect**, אל המשפט **The effect has limits, however**, ולכן הרעיון המרכזי הוא שמפגש חוזר מגביר חיבה, אבל רק עד גבול מסוים (הצירוף **up to a point**).

_The text presents **the mere-exposure effect** and then says **The effect has limits, however**, so repeated contact raises liking only up to a point._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, the items that were shown more often

options.label: were easier for the volunteers to recognize and remember
were mostly made-up words rather than shapes
made the volunteers feel bored after a while
were given more favorable scores by the volunteers

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the items shown more often usually receive higher ratings**, הפריטים שהוצגו יותר פעמים קיבלו דירוג גבוה יותר, כלומר ציונים חיוביים יותר (הצירוף **more favorable scores**).

_Paragraph 2 says **the items shown more often usually receive higher ratings**, so the volunteers gave them more favorable scores._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, what is one common explanation for the effect?

options.label: Liking something makes the brain process it more easily.
Familiar things remind people of happy times in their past.
People are taught from an early age to trust familiar things.
People confuse the comfort of easy processing with liking.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **Because this ease feels pleasant, people may mistake it for genuine liking**, אנשים מבלבלים בין הקלוּת הנעימה שבעיבוד של דבר מוכר לבין חיבה (המילה **confuse**, מבלבלים).

_**Because this ease feels pleasant, people may mistake it for genuine liking**: the comfort of easy processing is confused with liking._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "deepen" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט **The effect has limits, however** מסמן שכאן החזרה לא עוזרת, והמילה **only** מראה שהיא רק מוסיפה לסלידה, ולכן פירוש המילה **deepen** הוא להעמיק, לחזק (הצירוף **make stronger**).

_After **The effect has limits, however**, repeated contact with something disliked **may only deepen the dislike**, so **deepen** means make stronger._

questionText: What can be inferred from paragraph 5?

options.label: Photographs show faces less accurately than mirrors do.
Friends tend to judge a person's looks more fairly than the person does.
Each group likes best the view of the face it sees most.
Most people dislike looking at themselves in a mirror.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התמונה ההפוכה דומה לבבואה במראה, לפי הצירוף **like the image in a mirror**, והחברים רואים את הפנים הרגילות, ולכן כל קבוצה מעדיפה את מה שהיא רואה הכי הרבה (הצירוף **sees most**).

_The reversed photo is **like the image in a mirror**, the face people see most, while friends see the normal face, so each prefers the familiar view._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To describe how printing changed the way books were made in England
To explain why English spelling is so irregular and why it stays that way
To argue that English spelling should be made to match pronunciation
To compare the spelling of English with the spelling systems of several other European languages

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפטי הנושא עוברים מהטענה **most of its oddities have historical causes**, דרך הסיבות, אל הצירוף **such plans have rarely succeeded**, ולכן המטרה היא להסביר למה האיות לא סדיר ולמה הוא נשאר כך (הצירוף **stays that way**).

_It moves from **most of its oddities have historical causes** to why reform plans **have rarely succeeded**, so it explains the irregularity and why it stays._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why do many English spellings not match modern pronunciation?

options.label: Printers in the late 1400s did not know how most English words were pronounced.
Vowels changed in spelling but stayed the same in speech.
Teachers chose spellings that were easier for children to learn.
Spelling became fixed while the sounds of the language went on changing.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **settled on fixed spellings** והמשפט **Speech, however, kept changing**, האיות התקבע בזמן שההגייה המשיכה להשתנות (הצירוף **went on changing**).

_Printers and teachers **settled on fixed spellings**, but **Speech, however, kept changing**, so spelling stayed while sounds moved on._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, why did some scholars add a "b" to "debt" and "doubt"?

options.label: They believed the letter was pronounced in those words.
They wanted the words to reflect their Latin origins.
They wanted to make the two words easier to tell apart.
They copied a spelling mistake made by early printers.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **wanted English words to display their Latin roots** והצירוף **because the Latin words contained**, החוקרים רצו שהמילים יציגו את מקורן הלטיני (הצירוף **Latin origins**).

_The scholars **wanted English words to display their Latin roots**, so they added a letter that the Latin words contained._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "obscure" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הדוגמה בצירוף **shows its connection**, האות השקטה מראה את הקשר בין מילים, ולכן כתיבה לפי הצליל הייתה מסתירה אותו, ופירוש המילה **obscure** הוא להסתיר, לטשטש (המילה **hide**).

_The silent letter **shows its connection** to a related word, so spelling by sound would hide that link: **obscure** means hide._

questionText: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about the irregular spelling of English?

options.label: It might become much more regular within a few generations.
It is the main reason that people stop learning English.
It has some benefits that a simpler system might lose.
It matches the pronunciation of one accent better than others.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקה מציגה סיבות לכך שכתיבה לפי הצליל הייתה גרועה יותר, למשל הצירוף **would obscure the links between related words**, ומכאן שלאיות הלא סדיר יש יתרונות (המילה **benefits**).

_Writing by sound **would obscure the links between related words**, so the irregular spelling has benefits that a simpler system might lose._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To describe how furry animals use their hair to protect themselves
To explain how goosebumps form and why humans still get them
To compare the many ways the human body protects itself from cold
To report new findings about how hair grows back in mice

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקאות עוברות מהיווצרות הבליטות, דרך התפקיד שלהן אצל בעלי פרווה, אל הצירוף **a leftover from hairy ancestors**, ולכן המטרה היא להסביר איך נוצר עור ברווז ולמה הוא נשאר אצלנו.

_The paragraphs move from how the bumps form to **a leftover from hairy ancestors**, so the passage explains goosebumps and why we still get them._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why are people unable to produce goosebumps by choice?

options.label: The muscles that cause them are not under a person's conscious control.
The muscles attached to the hairs are too small to be moved on purpose.
The heart must beat faster before these muscles can tighten.
The hairs on the human body are too short and thin to stand up.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **because these muscles are controlled by**, השרירים נשלטים בידי חלק במערכת העצבים שפועל מעצמו (הצירוף **works automatically**), ולכן אין לאדם שליטה מודעת בהם.

_The clue is **because**: the muscles are controlled by the part of the nervous system that **works automatically**, so people cannot control them consciously._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, how do raised hairs help a furry animal stay warm?

options.label: They make the animal look larger to its enemies.
They allow air to move freely over the skin.
They hold more air next to the skin.
They help new hair grow after a cold spell.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **they trap a thicker layer of air close to the skin**, השערות המזדקפות לוכדות שכבת אוויר עבה ליד העור, והאוויר הזה שומר על החום (הצירוף **hold more air**).

_Raised hairs **trap a thicker layer of air close to the skin**, and this air **keeps the body warm**._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "modest" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **though nothing like the important one**, התפקיד אצלנו קטן בהרבה מהתפקיד אצל בעלי פרווה, ולכן המילה **modest** פירושה כאן קטן (המילה **small**).

_**though nothing like the important one** shows that the job is much less important, so **modest** here means **small**._

questionText: What can be inferred from the passage about goosebumps that appear during a frightening film?

options.label: They probably make a frightened person look bigger to others.
They help to keep a person warm during moments of fear.
They are produced by different muscles from the ones that react to cold.
They are probably linked to the way furry animals react to danger.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פחד מעורר עור ברווז, הפרווה המזדקפת מבריחה אויב (הצירוף **may scare away an enemy**), ועור הברווז הוא שארית מאבות שעירים (הצירוף **a leftover from hairy ancestors**), ולכן הוא כנראה קשור לתגובה לסכנה.

_Fear brings goosebumps, raised fur **may scare away an enemy**, and goosebumps are **a leftover from hairy ancestors**, so they probably echo how animals react to danger._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Lichens can live in harsh places because a fungus and an alga each provide something that the other one needs.
Many kinds of living things can be used to measure how clean the air, the water and the soil are in a particular area.
Lichens are hardy partnerships whose way of feeding makes them sensitive to polluted air and useful for judging it.
Pollution from burning coal drove lichens out of cities, and they have not been able to come back since then.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע עובר מהשותפות, דרך העמידות והרגישות לזיהום, אל המשפט **This sensitivity has turned lichens into useful tools**, ולכן הרעיון המרכזי הוא שותפות עמידה (**hardy partnerships**) שרגישה לזיהום ומשמשת למדידתו.

_The topic sentences go from **a partnership** to toughness, to **dirty air**, to **This sensitivity has turned lichens into useful tools**, so the key joins all four._

questionText: According to the passage, what does the fungus provide for the alga?

options.label: Sugars made from sunlight, which the alga then uses as its food
Protection from strong sunlight and wind, along with moisture
Minerals that it draws up from the rock beneath it through its roots
A barrier that filters harmful gases out of the air around it

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **holding water and sheltering the alga from strong light and drying winds**, הפטרייה שומרת על מים ומגינה על האצה מאור חזק ומרוחות, כלומר נותנת לה הגנה (המילה **Protection**) ולחות.

_The fungus is **holding water and sheltering the alga from strong light and drying winds**, so it gives the alga protection and moisture._

questionText: According to the passage, why do lichens take in pollutants?

options.label: They feed straight from rain and air and cannot keep harmful substances out.
They grow so slowly that harmful substances build up in them over many years.
They lose their protective outer layer when they dry out for months at a time.
They need the sulfur in coal smoke to help the alga make sugars from sunlight.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי מילת התוצאה **so** והצירוף **they have no way to filter these out**, החזזיות סופגות הכול ישירות מהגשם ומהאוויר ואינן יכולות לסנן חומרים מזיקים.

_Lichens **absorb water and minerals directly from rain, fog and the air**, and **they have no way to filter these out**._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "exposed" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **no roots and no protective outer layer**, אין לחזזיות הגנה מפני האוויר, ולכן המילה **exposed** פירושה כאן חשופות, בלי הגנה (המילה **unprotected**).

_Lichens have **no roots and no protective outer layer**, so dirty air reaches them freely; **exposed** means **unprotected**._

questionText: It can be inferred from paragraph 4 that a city street with leafy and bushy lichens on its trees

options.label: probably has dirtier air than a street with flat, crusty lichens
has trees that are unusually old
is a place where electronic monitors would cost less than a survey

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **Leafy and bushy types tend to disappear first**, החזזיות האלה נעלמות ראשונות כשיש זיהום, ולכן רחוב שבו הן גדלות כנראה נהנה מאוויר נקי יחסית.

_**Leafy and bushy types tend to disappear first** when air is polluted, so a street where they grow probably has relatively clean air._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To explain why owning something raises its worth in the owner's eyes, and where this effect weakens
To report the results of experiments in which people were handed coffee mugs
To argue that most of the economic decisions people make are driven by their feelings rather than by reason
To warn shoppers that free trials are designed to encourage acquisitive habits

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מגדיר את התופעה, בצירוף **value an object more highly simply because it belongs to them**, מסביר אותה ומגיע לצירוף **The effect is not universal**, ולכן מטרתו להסביר אותה ואת גבולותיה.

_The passage defines the effect (**value an object more highly simply because it belongs to them**), explains it, and then states **The effect is not universal**._

questionText: According to the passage, why do far fewer trades take place in the mug experiments than economists would predict?

options.label: Buyers tend to value the mugs more highly than the owners do.
Sellers demand much more money than buyers will offer.
The mugs are handed out at random, so many people get one they do not want.
Participants are not told how much the mugs cost in a store.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי מילת הניגוד **Yet**, הבעלים דורשים בערך פי שניים ממה שהקונים מוכנים להציע, בצירוף **ask for roughly twice as much**, ולכן מתבצעות מעט עסקאות.

_After **Yet**, owners **ask for roughly twice as much as buyers are willing to offer**, and **as a result** few trades happen._

questionText: According to the passage, what is the most common explanation for the endowment effect?

options.label: Owners know more than buyers about the real value of the object.
People grow attached to objects that they have owned for many years.
Giving up something hurts more than gaining the same thing pleases.
Owners see their goods as things to exchange rather than to keep.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **people feel losses more strongly than gains of the same size**, ויתור על משהו כואב יותר מההנאה שבקבלת אותו הדבר.

_**The most common explanation is that people feel losses more strongly than gains of the same size**, so giving something up hurts more than gaining it pleases._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "outweighs" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **people feel losses more strongly than gains of the same size**, הכאב שבהפסד חזק מההנאה שברווח, ולכן המילה **outweighs** פירושה כאן גובר על (הצירוף **is greater than**).

_**people feel losses more strongly than gains of the same size**, so the pain **outweighs**, or **is greater than**, the pleasure._

questionText: Why does the author mention dealers who buy goods in order to resell them?

options.label: To explain why owners ask for higher prices than buyers will pay
To show how businesses use the effect to increase their sales
To suggest that the mug experiments were not carried out properly
To give an example of people in whom the effect is weaker

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הסוחרים מופיעים אחרי הצירוף **The effect is not universal, however** ובתוך הצירוף **much weaker among experienced traders, such as**, ולכן הם דוגמה לאנשים שאצלם האפקט חלש יותר.

_Right after **The effect is not universal**, the dealers follow **such as** as an example of people in whom the effect **is much weaker**._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Infants appear to locate word boundaries in speech partly by tracking which syllables occur together.
In one experiment, infants listened longer to new combinations of sounds than to made-up words they had heard before.
Children learn their first language largely by copying the words that their parents repeat to them again and again.
Experiments suggest that statistics alone explain how infants discover where words begin and end.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע עובר מהבעיה, המשפט **Speech offers no such help**, אל הרמז, הצירוף **one clue**, ומסייג אותו (**statistics alone**), ולכן תינוקות מאתרים גבולות בין מילים בין השאר (**partly**) לפי הברות שמופיעות יחד.

_The passage moves from the problem (**Speech offers no such help**) to **one clue**, which syllables go together, and then limits it: not **statistics alone**._

questionText: In the phrase "pretty baby," why is "pre" very often followed by "ty"?

options.label: The word "pretty" can come before almost any word.
Speakers usually pause for a moment after saying "pre."
The two syllables make up a single word.
"Ty" is the most common syllable in spoken English.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי מילת הסיבה **because** והצירוף **the two belong to the same word**, שתי ההברות הן חלקים של אותה מילה, ולכן הן מופיעות יחד שוב ושוב.

_The clue is **because the two belong to the same word**: both syllables are parts of one word, so they keep appearing together._

questionText: According to the passage, why did the researchers measure how long the babies listened?

options.label: Infants who listened longer had learned more of the made-up words.
Longer listening shows that a sound seems new to an infant.
The made-up words had been played for about two minutes.
Longer listening showed which sounds the infants probably enjoyed most.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי מילת הסיבה **Because** והצירוף **pay more attention to sounds they have not heard before**, זמן הקשבה ארוך מעיד שצליל נשמע לתינוק חדש.

_**Because infants tend to pay more attention to sounds they have not heard before**, longer listening shows that a sound seems new to them._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "novel" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **sounds they have not heard before**, תינוקות מקשיבים יותר לצלילים חדשים, ולכן המילה **novel** פירושה כאן חדש, לא מוכר (המילה **unfamiliar**), ולא רומן.

_Infants attend to **sounds they have not heard before** and listened longer to these sequences, so **novel** means **unfamiliar** here._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that the ability to notice which syllables go together

options.label: is probably a general learning skill rather than one used for language alone
probably develops after children have learned their first words
is probably enough on its own to explain how young children come to recognize words
is stronger in monkeys than in human infants

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **musical tones rather than syllables** והצירוף **and even in some monkeys**, אותה למידה מופיעה גם בלי מילים וגם אצל קופים, ולכן היא כנראה יכולת למידה כללית.

_Similar learning appears with **musical tones rather than syllables** **and even in some monkeys**, so the skill is probably general, not limited to language._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Dark roofs and roads take in sunlight during the day and give the heat back at night.
Because of how they are built, cities tend to stay warmer than the countryside after dark, causing problems that can be reduced in several ways.
Cities tend to be much hotter than the countryside at midday, when the sun beats down on their dark surfaces.
Air conditioning, which pumps heat out of buildings and into the streets, has become the main reason that temperatures are rising in many parts of the world.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע עובר מהתופעה לסיבות, לנזקים ולפתרונות (**Several remedies have been proposed**), ולכן הרעיון: בגלל אופן בנייתן ערים נשארות חמות מהכפר אחרי החשכה (**stay warmer than the countryside after dark**), ואפשר לצמצם זאת.

_The passage moves from the effect (**It tends to widen after sunset**) to its causes, costs and **remedies**: cities stay warmer after dark, causing problems that can be reduced._

questionText: According to the passage, why does the gap between city and country widen after sunset?

options.label: Open fields keep their warmth for longer than stone, brick and concrete do.
More cars and lights are in use in cities at night than during the day.
Building materials give off the heat they took in during the day little by little.
Air conditioners are switched on in the evening and pump heat out into the streets.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **these materials give it back slowly through the night**, חומרי הבנייה מחזירים את החום לאט, ולכן העיר נשארת חמה בזמן שהשדות כבר מתקררים.

_**Whereas open fields lose their warmth soon after sunset, these materials give it back slowly through the night**, so the city stays warm._

questionText: According to the passage, in what way do plants help to cool a city?

options.label: Moisture from their leaves takes in warmth from the nearby air as it turns into vapor.
Their pale leaves reflect most of the sunlight that reaches them instead of absorbing it.
They store heat in their leaves during the day and then release it slowly through the night.
They block the wind that would otherwise carry warm air into the city.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **as this water evaporates, it takes heat from the surrounding air**, המים שהצמחים משחררים סופגים חום מהאוויר כשהם מתאדים.

_Plants release water, and **as this water evaporates, it takes heat from the surrounding air**._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "compounds" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המזגנים מוציאים חום לרחוב ומוסיפים חום משלהם (הצירוף **while their motors add heat of their own**), ולכן המילה **compounds** פירושה כאן מחמיר (**makes worse**).

_Air conditioners add heat (**while their motors add heat of their own**), so the response **compounds**, or makes worse, the problem._

questionText: What can be inferred from the passage about the heat island on a windy, cloudy night?

options.label: Clouds would keep the city's heat from escaping, so it is likely to be stronger.
It is probably weaker than when the air is still and the sky is clear.
It would probably grow, because tall buildings would block even more of the wind.
It would depend mainly on how many air conditioners were running in the city that night.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפער הגדול מתואר דווקא בצירוף **on calm, clear nights**, והרוח מרחיקה אוויר חם (הצירוף **carry warm air away**), ולכן בלילה עם רוח ועננים הוא כנראה קטן יותר.

_The big gap comes **on calm, clear nights**, and wind would **carry warm air away**, so a windy, cloudy night probably weakens it._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To show that early researchers were wrong to treat the two forms of the locust as separate species
To describe laboratory studies in which locusts' legs were stroked to make them seek company
To argue that spraying swarms from the air is a waste of money and should be replaced by laboratory research
To explain how crowding changes a lone insect into a swarming one, and why this matters for control

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מסביר מה גורם לשינוי (**What sets off the change is crowding**) ומה משמעותו המעשית, ולכן מטרתו: להסביר איך צפיפות הופכת חרק בודד לנחילי ולמה זה חשוב לשליטה בארבה (**why this matters for control**).

_Its purpose is to explain how crowding (**What sets off the change is crowding**) turns a lone insect into a swarming one, and why this matters for control._

questionText: According to the passage, what purpose may the black-and-yellow pattern of young swarming locusts serve?

options.label: It may let predators know that the insects taste bad.
It may help the insects hide among the plants they feed on.
It helps the swarming insects recognize their neighbors and stay together.
It shields the insects from the strong desert sun during the day.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **may warn birds and lizards that the insects are unpleasant to eat**, הדוגמה הצבעונית מזהירה טורפים שהחרקים אינם טעימים.

_The pattern **may warn birds and lizards that the insects are unpleasant to eat**, so it tells predators the insects taste bad._

questionText: What did the laboratory studies mentioned in the passage show?

options.label: Locusts need several generations of crowding before they begin to look for company.
Locusts in which serotonin was blocked changed more quickly than the others did.
A few hours of having their back legs touched made lone locusts sociable.
Touching a locust's hind legs makes it turn black and yellow within a few hours.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **merely stroking these legs for a few hours was enough**, כמה שעות של מגע ברגליים האחוריות הספיקו כדי שארבה בודד יחפש חברה.

_In the lab, **merely stroking these legs for a few hours was enough to make solitary locusts start seeking out company**, so lone locusts became sociable._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "sparse" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **normally sparse** מנוגד לצמיחה הפתאומית אחרי גשמים (הצירוף **the sudden growth that follows unusual rains**), ולכן המילה **sparse** פירושה דליל (**thinly scattered**).

_Plant life that is **normally sparse** contrasts with **the sudden growth that follows unusual rains**, so **sparse** means thinly scattered._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that a locust that has begun to seek out company but is still green or sandy brown

options.label: has probably been crowded together with others for several generations
probably belongs to a different species from the black-and-yellow form
has probably fed on plants that make it taste bad to birds
is probably in the early stages of its change

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההתנהגות משתנה תוך שעות (הצירוף **only a few hours**) והצבע לאורך דורות (הצירוף **over several generations**), ולכן ארבה חברותי שעדיין ירוק נמצא כנראה בתחילת השינוי.

_Behavior changes in **only a few hours**, color **over several generations**, so a sociable but still green locust is probably early in the change._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Modern schooling teaches people to sort things into abstract classes, which is exactly the kind of answer that intelligence tests reward.
Test results rose for decades, apparently because of how people live rather than their genes, and lately the rise has slowed or turned downward in places.
People today score higher than their grandparents did mainly because they have inherited better genes from their parents.
Intelligence test results rose steadily for decades, and they are likely to go on rising as children around the world spend more and more years in school.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מתאר עלייה שהגנים לא מסבירים (**Genes cannot change fast enough**) וירידה בסופו, ולכן הרעיון: הציונים עלו בגלל אורח החיים ולא הגנים, ולאחרונה העלייה נבלמה או התהפכה (**slowed or turned downward**).

_Scores rose although **Genes cannot change fast enough**, and lately **scores have even begun to fall**: a rise driven by how people live, now slowing or reversing._

questionText: According to the passage, how was the rise eventually noticed?

options.label: People who took an older form of a test did far better than the group used to set its average.
Researchers noticed that people were finishing the tests more quickly than before.
Test makers found that each new version of a test had become easier than the version it replaced a few decades earlier.
Scores on vocabulary tests began to climb sharply in many countries.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **people taking an older version of a test scored well above 100 on its original standards**, הנבחנים בגרסה ישנה הצליחו הרבה יותר מקבוצת המקור.

_The pattern became clear when **people taking an older version of a test scored well above 100 on its original standards**._

questionText: According to the passage, why can genetic change not explain the gains?

options.label: Children are now better fed and healthier than their grandparents were.
In several wealthy countries, results have stopped rising or have begun to fall.
They appeared over a period too short for inherited traits to shift.
Tests are regularly restandardized on a new group of people.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **Genes cannot change fast enough**, העלייה הופיעה בתוך שניים או שלושה דורות (הצירוף **within two or three generations**), זמן קצר מדי לשינוי גנטי.

_**Genes cannot change fast enough** to explain gains that **appeared within two or three generations**: the time was too short._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "concentrated" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** מילת הניגוד **whereas** מעמידה עלייה קטנה (הצירוף **rose only a little**) מול המשימות המופשטות, ולכן המילה **concentrated** פירושה כאן נמצא בעיקר (**found mostly**).

_**whereas** contrasts scores that **rose only a little** with abstract tasks, so **concentrated** means found mostly in those tasks._

questionText: What does the author imply about the answer that bees feed on flowers?

options.label: It reflects a different way of thinking, not a lack of intelligence.
It would earn more credit on a modern test than the answer about living things.
It shows that earlier generations were unable to see how two things are alike.
It was probably the most common answer among children in earlier eras.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המחבר מכנה את התשובה הגיונית (הצירוף **quite sensibly**) ומייחס את ההבדל לאימון (הצירוף **trained people to think in a particular way**), ולכן היא דרך חשיבה אחרת ולא חוסר אינטליגנציה.

_The author says it was given **quite sensibly** and that modern life **trained people to think** differently, so it reflects another way of thinking._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: The QWERTY layout was meant to keep the metal arms of early typewriters from colliding, not to slow typists down.
QWERTY survives because early choices locked society into it, even though a far faster layout for typists has been available since the 1930s.
Keyboard layouts make little difference to typing speed, so the choice among them matters little to people who type today.
QWERTY outlived the machines it was made for, and experts disagree about whether its survival shows a weaker design getting locked in.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 1 מציגה מקרה מבחן בוויכוח (**a test case in a debate**) ופסקאות 3–4 את שני הצדדים, ולכן הרעיון: המקלדת שרדה את מכונותיה, ויש מחלוקת אם הישרדותה מעידה על תכנון חלש שננעל (**a weaker design getting locked in**).

_QWERTY outlived its machines and is **a test case in a debate**: economists see a weaker design locked in, but **Critics dismiss this account as a fable**._

questionText: According to the passage, why did the designers of QWERTY keep certain common pairs of letters apart?

options.label: To stop neighboring metal arms from crashing into each other and getting stuck.
To make typists work more slowly, so that they would make fewer mistakes on the page.
To place the most frequently used letters where the fingers rest.
To let the same layout be used later on computers and phones.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **they could collide and jam**, זרועות סמוכות עלולות היו להתנגש ולהיתקע, ולכן הפרידו בין האותיות.

_Neighboring arms used in quick succession **could collide and jam**, so the letters were split up to keep them apart._

questionText: According to the economists mentioned in the passage, why did the 1930s layout fail to replace QWERTY?

options.label: Studies by its inventor had not been checked by independent researchers.
Later comparisons by other researchers found that its speed advantage over the older keyboard was quite small.
Typists, employers and manufacturers were already tied to the older keyboard, and each relied on the others.
Machines built for it jammed more often than older typewriters did.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הכלכלנים קלדנים, מעסיקים ויצרנים כבר היו קשורים למקלדת הישנה, וכל בחירה חיזקה את האחרות (הצירוף **Each of these choices supported the others**).

_Typists had learned it, employers expected it and makers built for it, and **Each of these choices supported the others**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "fable" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבקרים דוחים את ההסבר (הצירוף **dismiss this account as**) ומיד מערערים על הראיות לו, ולכן המילה **fable** פירושה כאן סיפור לא נכון (**an untrue story**).

_Critics **dismiss this account as** a **fable** and then attack its evidence, so the word means an untrue story._

questionText: It can be inferred that the economists and their critics mainly disagree about

options.label: why the designers of QWERTY separated common letter pairs
whether retraining large numbers of typists would be expensive
whether users of the newer layout feel less strain in their fingers
how large the newer layout's speed advantage really is

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הכלכלנים סבורים שהייתה מקלדת טובה יותר (הצירוף **once a better one existed**), והמבקרים מצאו הבדל קטן (הצירוף **the difference in speed to be small**); המחלוקת היא על גודל היתרון.

_The economists think **a better one existed**, while the critics found **the difference in speed to be small**, so they disagree about the size of the advantage._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Bright sunshine early in the day can slow recovery after a long flight to the east.
Jet lag occurs when the body's inner timing falls out of line with local time, and which way one flies affects how readily this is put right.
A small cluster of cells in the brain controls sleep, and light is the signal that keeps this timekeeper accurate.
Jet lag stems from a mismatch between the inner clock and the local day, and the best cure is to get as much bright light as one possibly can.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מגדיר את התופעה כאי-התאמה (**the resulting mismatch**) ומראה שהכיוון משנה, ולכן הרעיון: השעון הפנימי יוצא מהתאמה לשעה המקומית, וכיוון הטיסה קובע כמה קל לתקן זאת (**how readily this is put right**).

_Jet lag is **the resulting mismatch** between the inner clock and local time, and since **direction matters**, which way one flies affects how readily it is put right._

questionText: According to the passage, which of the following can happen before the inner clock has caught up with local time?

options.label: The traveler may sleep soundly at night but feel drowsy during the day.
Morning light may lose its effect on the clock until the traveler has had a full night's rest.
Body temperature may rise and fall at random rather than on a daily cycle.
Food may cause discomfort, as the digestive system still keeps to the hours of home.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הקטע, העיכול נשאר בלוח הזמנים הישן (הצירוף **digestion keeps the old timetable too**), ולכן גם ארוחות עלולות להכביד (הצירוף **meals may sit uneasily**).

_The passage says that **meals may sit uneasily, since digestion keeps the old timetable too**, which the answer paraphrases._

questionText: What reason does the passage give for the difference between eastward and westward travel?

options.label: Without daylight signals, the inner clock tends to run on a cycle longer than a day.
Flights heading east usually cross more time zones than flights heading west.
The inner clock finds it easier to move earlier than to move later.
Sleep on eastbound flights tends to be shorter and lighter than the sleep people get on westbound ones.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההסבר בקטע הוא תכונה של השעון עצמו (הצירוף **a quirk of the clock**): בלי אור יום הוא משלים מחזור בקצת יותר מיממה (הצירוף **a little more than twenty-four hours**).

_The passage places the reason in **a quirk of the clock**: without daylight it runs for **a little more than twenty-four hours**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "advanced" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **advanced** היא ההפך מאיחור (המשפט **Flying east requires the opposite**), והמטייל נעשה ישנוני מוקדם (הצירוף **sleepy hours before the body is ready**); לכן פירושה הוקדם.

_The word **advanced** is **the opposite** of delaying and makes the traveler **sleepy hours before the body is ready**, so it means moved forward, making sleep come sooner._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that a person whose body clock, left without daylight cues, ran a little shorter than twenty-four hours would probably

options.label: recover from westward flights faster than other people do
be largely spared jet lag in both directions
need more morning light than others to keep in step with local time
find flying east less of a strain than most people do

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** טיסה מזרחה קשה כי השעון נוטה ללוח זמנים מאוחר (הצירוף **already leans toward a later schedule**); שעון קצר נוטה לכיוון ההפוך, ולכן קל יותר להקדים אותו.

_East is hard because the clock **already leans toward a later schedule**; a shorter clock leans the other way, so moving it earlier should be easier._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To show that the rush in early films comes largely from how they are screened today
To describe how the coming of sound fixed film speed at twenty-four frames per second
To argue that early filmmakers often sped up their scenes to make audiences laugh
To trace how film technology developed from cameras turned by hand to the equipment in use today

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 1 טוענת שהחיפזון הוא תאונה (**for the most part, an accident**) ושאר הפסקאות מסבירות זאת, ולכן המטרה: להראות שהחיפזון בסרטים הישנים נובע בעיקר מאופן ההקרנה היום (**how they are screened today**).

_The passage states that **The hurry is, for the most part, an accident of the way these films are shown today**, and the other paragraphs explain why._

questionText: Which of the following does the passage state about the showing of films in the silent era?

options.label: Theaters usually slowed films down so that each show would last longer.
Projectionists obeyed guidelines that arrived with each film.
The projection speed sometimes differed from the speed of filming.
Audiences often complained when a film was run too fast.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הקטע, המקרינים לא תמיד התאימו את המהירות לזו שבה צולם הסרט (הצירוף **did not always match the speed at which a film had been shot**).

_The passage says projectionists **did not always match the speed at which a film had been shot**._

questionText: According to the passage, why did the coming of sound lead to a single fixed rate?

options.label: Audiences had started to complain that silent films looked hurried.
Changing the speed would have made voices and music rise or fall in tone.
Sound equipment could not work at speeds below twenty-four frames per second.
The eye notices even slight changes in speed more readily than the ear does.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצליל היה קשור לתמונה, ולכן שינוי מהירות היה משנה את גובה הצליל (הצירוף **would alter the pitch of voices and music**), והאוזן מבחינה בכך.

_Because the sound was tied to the pictures, a speed change **would alter the pitch of voices and music**, which the ear notices._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "forgiving" is closest in meaning to

options.label: willing to excuse the mistakes of others

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** העין מנוגדת לאוזן שמבחינה בכל שינוי קטן (הצירוף **notices even slight changes**), ולכן המילה **forgiving** פירושה כאן סלחנית לשינויים, לא מוטרדת מהבדלים קטנים.

_The eye is contrasted with an ear that **notices even slight changes**, so **forgiving** means not troubled by small differences._

questionText: The author would most likely say that modern viewers who laugh at the hurried figures in a silent film are

options.label: mostly reacting to an effect that its makers did not intend
rightly noticing how crudely such films were made
enjoying a joke that most early filmmakers built in on purpose
largely seeing the film as its first audiences were meant to see it

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הכותב החיפזון הוא ברובו תאונה (הצירוף **for the most part, an accident**), ובקצב הנכון הסצנות חוזרות למצב הרוח המקורי (הצירוף **regain their intended mood**); לכן הצחוק הוא תגובה לאפקט לא מכוון.

_The hurry is **for the most part, an accident**, and at the right pace scenes **regain their intended mood**, so the laughter is mostly at an unintended effect._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Companies bidding for offshore drilling rights have often paid more than the oil they found was worth.
Since auction winners usually pay too much, companies would do better to stay away from items whose worth is uncertain.
The price an auction reaches tends to depend on how many people take part and on how much they know.
Where an item's true worth is much the same for all bidders but uncertain, winning often means having overestimated it.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הניצחון מעיד על הערכת יתר (**victory is evidence of overestimation**) כשהערך משותף ולא ודאי, ולכן הרעיון: במצב כזה הזוכה לרוב העריך יתר על המידה (**winning often means having overestimated it**).

_When value is **shared but uncertain**, **victory is evidence of overestimation**: winning often means having overestimated the item._

questionText: According to the passage, what first led observers to suspect that winning an auction could be costly?

options.label: Classroom auctions in which the winners of coin-filled jars lost money
The weak earnings of companies that had secured undersea drilling rights
Complaints from oil companies that had often lost auctions for drilling rights to their rivals
Evidence that companies usually bid far less than their own estimates of worth

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הקטע, החשד עלה אצל מהנדסים שראו שחברות שזכו בזכויות קידוח הרוויחו מעט (הצירוף **winning companies, they noticed, tended to earn disappointing returns**).

_Engineers studying drilling rights saw that **winning companies, they noticed, tended to earn disappointing returns**._

questionText: According to the passage, why is the highest bidder likely to have overestimated the item?

options.label: Each bidder tends to inflate the estimate on purpose in order to win.
Most estimates of something whose worth is uncertain turn out to lie well above the truth.
The winning offer tends to come from the guess that overshot by the most.
The winner usually has less information than the companies that lose.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** כל מציע מציע לפי הערכתו, ולכן ההצעה הגבוהה ביותר באה ממי שהערכתו חרגה יותר מכולם (הצירוף **the one whose estimate lay furthest above the truth**).

_The highest bidder is, **almost by definition, the one whose estimate lay furthest above the truth**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "shade" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפתרון הוא להציע פחות מההערכה (הצירוף **bid less than one's estimate**), ולכן המילה **shade** פירושה כאן להוריד מעט את ההצעה ככל שמספר המתחרים גדל.

_The cure is to **bid less than one's estimate**, so to **shade** the bid means to trim it somewhat._

questionText: The results of the classroom auctions described in the passage suggest that

options.label: adding more bidders to the room would have raised the average bid above the jar's value
a winner can overpay even when the typical bid is below the item's worth
warning bidders about the curse is enough to prevent it
the winners lost money mainly through overweening confidence in their counting

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההצעה הממוצעת נמוכה מהשווי אך ההצעה הזוכה גבוהה ממנו (הצירוף **the winning bid exceeds it**); מכאן שהזוכה יכול לשלם ביתר גם כשרוב ההצעות נמוכות.

_Since **the average bid often falls below the jar's value while the winning bid exceeds it**, a winner can overpay even when typical bids are low._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To describe the questionnaires that schools and parents buy to sort pupils into types
To argue that teachers should stop taking their students' differences into account
To show why a widely accepted belief about matching lessons to pupils lacks firm support
To show that learning styles are real but that teachers rarely manage to cater to each of them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מציג אמונה נפוצה (**widely held**) ומראה שמחקרים כמעט לא אישרו אותה (**Hardly any of the well-designed studies has borne out the central claim**), ולכן מטרתו: להראות שאין לה ביסוס מוצק (**lacks firm support**).

_The passage presents a **widely held** belief and shows that **Hardly any of the well-designed studies has borne out the central claim**: the belief lacks firm support._

questionText: According to the passage, what would a properly designed study have to find for the theory to be supported?

options.label: That learners of each type gain most from lessons matched to that type
That most people prefer one way of taking in information to the others
That a certain method gives strong results for learners in general
That pupils can name their own style without the help of a questionnaire

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התיאוריה נתמכת רק אם כל סוג לומד מצליח יותר בשיטה שלו (הצירוף **visual learners did better with pictures while auditory learners did better with spoken explanations**).

_Support requires that **visual learners did better with pictures while auditory learners did better with spoken explanations**._

questionText: What does the passage report about learners who described themselves as visual?

options.label: They tended to remember words better than pictures.
They learned noticeably more when lessons were matched to the way they saw themselves.
They were fewer in number than the theory had led reviewers to expect.
Their memory for images was not consistently stronger than their memory for words.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הקטע, הם לא זכרו תמונות טוב יותר ממילים באופן עקבי (הצירוף **did not reliably remember pictures better than words**); השלילה נוגעת ליתרון בלבד.

_Self-described visual learners **did not reliably remember pictures better than words**; the answer restates this without going further._

questionText: As used in the passage, the phrase "borne out" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** רוב המחקרים לא הראו את הדפוס הצפוי (הצירוף **failed to show the predicted pattern**), ולכן הצירוף **borne out** פירושו כאן אושש, אושר (**verified**).

_Since the studies **failed to show the predicted pattern**, **borne out** here means verified._

questionText: Why does the author mention a map and the sound of a language?

options.label: To give examples of the visual and auditory styles of learning that the theory describes
To suggest that visual learners should study geography and auditory learners languages
To support the claim that a subject's nature should shape how it is taught
To show that some subjects are harder to learn than others

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות באות אחרי משפט הנושא **What appears to matter more is the material itself**: מפה וצליל של שפה מראים שהנושא, ולא סוג התלמיד, קובע את דרך ההוראה.

_The examples follow **What appears to matter more is the material itself** and show that the subject should decide the method._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Peahens tend to choose mates whose trains are longer and more elaborate than those of competing males.
An ornament that looks wasteful can be favored because only a fit animal can bear its burden.
Animal signals can be trusted only when they are costly to produce, as the peacock's train illustrates.
Many animals have evolved features that seem to reduce their chances of staying alive.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** העלות היא מקור הערך של האות (**the very source of its value**), ולכן הרעיון: קישוט שנראה בזבזני יכול להיבחר כי רק בעל חיים חזק מסוגל לשאת את הנטל שלו (**only a fit animal can bear its burden**).

_The passage explains a wasteful ornament: **the cost is not a flaw in the signal but the very source of its value**, since only a strong male can bear it._

questionText: According to the passage, which explanation of the peacock's train does no more than shift the puzzle to a new question?

options.label: The view that natural selection removes traits which make survival harder
The idea that the cost of an ornament is the very source of its value
The claim that the long feathers help the bird to escape from predators
The fact that females are drawn to males with bigger, showier tails

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **merely moves the puzzle back a step** (רק מעביר את החידה צעד אחורה), העדפת הנקבות לזנבות גדולים מעוררת שאלה חדשה: מדוע הן מעדיפות קישוט חסר תועלת.

_The females' preference for big trains **merely moves the puzzle back a step**: it raises the new question of why they prefer a useless ornament._

questionText: According to the passage, a peahen that selects a mate by the size of his train is actually assessing

options.label: his general health and strength, which cannot be seen directly
how many months he has spent growing his long feathers
how many times he has managed to escape from predators so far
the beauty of a pretty ornament that serves no practical purpose

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **a quality she cannot observe directly** (תכונה שהיא אינה יכולה לראות ישירות), הנקבה בודקת למעשה את החיוניות של הזכר (**vigor**), כלומר את בריאותו וכוחו.

_The female is **in effect judging a quality she cannot observe directly**: the male's **vigor**, that is, his health and strength._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "taxes" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי ההמשך **would ruin a weak one** (הייתה הורסת בעל חיים חלש), הפועל **taxes** מתאר עומס כבד, כלומר הצירוף **puts heavy demands on** (מעמיס דרישות כבדות, מתיש).

_Since the same display **would ruin a weak one**, **taxes** must mean puts heavy demands on, not anything positive or financial._

questionText: The passage suggests that the idea's early supporters

options.label: overstated the range of cases in which it holds
lost faith in it once mathematical models were built
were themselves incredulous when it was first proposed
believed that a signal could stay honest without being costly

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **under narrower conditions than its supporters had first claimed** (בתנאים צרים יותר ממה שטענו תומכיו בתחילה) מלמד שהתומכים הגזימו בהיקף שבו הרעיון חל.

_Models showed it works **under narrower conditions than its supporters had first claimed**, so the supporters overstated its range._

questionText: The passage is mainly concerned with

options.label: how English makers soon replaced glass bottles with cans of tin-coated iron
how early food makers came to realize that air is what makes food decay
the many different methods that people have used over the centuries to stop food from rotting
a preserving method that worked long before it was understood or made convenient

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הממציא לא ידע להסביר למה השיטה עובדת (**What he could not do was say why**), ולכן הרעיון: שיטת שימור שעבדה הרבה לפני שהובנה או נעשתה נוחה (**worked long before it was understood or made convenient**).

_The method worked before anyone could **say why**, and its convenience **trailed well behind the method itself**: the method worked long before it was understood or made convenient._

questionText: According to the passage, the method succeeded despite a mistaken theory because

options.label: the steps it called for happened to deal with the true cause of decay
the confectioner himself rejected the usual explanation of his day
the heat drove out the air that had been left inside the sealed bottles
experiments in the 1860s showed how long the food needed to be heated

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the heat was killing the microbes** (החום המית את החיידקים) והצירוף **the tight seal kept new ones from entering**, הצעדים עצמם טיפלו בגורם האמיתי למרות ההסבר השגוי.

_The steps worked because **the heat was killing the microbes** and **the tight seal kept new ones from entering**, even though the theory was wrong._

questionText: According to the passage, why were larger containers more likely to fail?

options.label: Their seals let in more of the air than the seals of smaller ones did.
Manufacturers heated them for a shorter time in order to save fuel.
The heat needed more time to penetrate to the middle of the food.
Gas built up inside them more quickly than in smaller ones.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **because heat took longer to reach their centers** (כי לחום לקח יותר זמן להגיע למרכזם) מסביר את הכישלון: מרכז המכל הגדול לא התחמם מספיק.

_Larger containers failed **because heat took longer to reach their centers**, so the middle of the food was not heated enough._

questionText: In the passage, the word "it" in "paid for it" refers to

options.label: the fuel that the manufacturers wanted to save
the choice to cut heating times short
the method of trial and error
the theory that the manufacturers lacked

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בצירוף **those who shortened them to save fuel sometimes paid for it**, מי שנשא במחיר הוא מי שקיצר את החימום, ולכן המילה **it** מציינת את ההחלטה לקצר את זמני החימום.

_In **those who shortened them to save fuel sometimes paid for it**, the price was paid for the shortening, so **it** is the choice to cut heating times._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the last paragraph?

options.label: To explain why English makers soon gave up glass in favor of cans of iron coated in tin
To suggest that the earliest cans were often unsafe to eat from
To show how the discovery of microbes changed the way cans were made
To add a further case in which canning's progress followed a surprising sequence

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקה נפתחת במשפט **The container, too, developed in an unexpected order** (גם המכל התפתח בסדר לא צפוי), והמילה **too** מסמנת מקרה נוסף של אותו פער.

_The paragraph opens with **The container, too, developed in an unexpected order**; **too** marks a second example of the same gap._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Herders who share a pasture tend to add animals until the grass is gone, because each herder pays just part of the cost.
Field studies show that shared resources are best managed by local communities rather than by governments or by private owners of land.
Shared resources need not be ruined, since their overuse tends to reflect a lack of workable rules rather than sharing itself.
How people use land and water tends to vary from one society to another.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט המסכם קורא לתחזית אזהרה ולא חוק טבע (**less a law of nature than a warning**), ולכן הרעיון: משאב משותף אינו חייב להיהרס, כי השימוש המופרז נובע מהיעדר כללים (**a lack of workable rules**) ולא מהשיתוף עצמו.

_The closing sentence calls the prediction **less a law of nature than a warning about what happens when rules are absent**, so shared resources need not be ruined._

questionText: According to the argument described in the passage, why does each herder keep adding animals?

options.label: He fears that unless he acts first, the other herders will take the grass for their own herds.
He reaps the whole benefit of an extra cow but bears only a share of the harm.
The government has set no limit on the number of cattle he may keep.
He fails to notice that the grass is slowly being grazed bare.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **gains the full benefit of it** (מקבל את כל התועלת) והצירוף **is spread among everyone** (מתחלק בין כולם), הרועה מרוויח הכול ונושא רק בחלק מהנזק.

_Each herder **gains the full benefit of it**, while the harm **is spread among everyone**._

questionText: According to the passage, the users of these resources typically

options.label: left the enforcement of their rules to officials who lived far away
admitted outsiders who agreed to respect local customs
punished first offenses as severely as repeated ones
had a hand in drawing up and changing the rules

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **The users themselves usually helped make and revise the rules** (המשתמשים עצמם עזרו בדרך כלל לקבוע ולשנות את הכללים), הם היו שותפים לניסוח הכללים.

_The passage says **The users themselves usually helped make and revise the rules**, so they had a hand in drawing them up and changing them._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "policed" is closest in meaning to

options.label: reported their misdeeds to the authorities

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **policed** באה בניגוד לצירוף **rather than relying on distant officials** (במקום להסתמך על פקידים רחוקים), ולכן פירושה לפקח ולהעניש (**kept watch over and disciplined**).

_Users **policed one another rather than relying on distant officials**: they kept watch over and disciplined each other themselves._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that the original argument

options.label: has been refuted by studies of fisheries and forests
rested on an assumption about people that rarely holds in practice
was intended mainly as a description of mountain meadows
was eventually accepted as sound by most of the researchers who went into the field

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הטיעון הניח אנשים שאינם יכולים לתקשר או לאכוף הסכם (הצירוף **cannot communicate or enforce an agreement**), אבל לפי המשפט **Real herders are seldom so hamstrung** רועים אמיתיים כמעט אינם כבולים כך.

_The argument assumed people who **cannot communicate or enforce an agreement**, yet **Real herders are seldom so hamstrung**._

questionText: Original: Ben went to bed early on Friday because he was very tired.

options.label: Ben went to bed early on Friday, so he was very tired.
On Friday, Ben felt very tired, so he went to bed early.
Ben went to bed early on Friday.
Ben went to bed late on Friday because he was very tired.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי, בגלל ש-) מציגה את הסיבה: בן היה עייף מאוד, ולכן הלך לישון מוקדם, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הקשר הזה בעזרת המילה **so** (לכן).

_**Because** gives the reason: Ben was very tired, so he went to bed early, and the correct answer keeps this link with **so**._

questionText: Original: Our neighbor's dog was found by two children near the river.

options.label: Two children lost our neighbor's dog near the river.
Two children found a dog by the river.
Near the river, our neighbor's dog found two children.
Near the river, two children found our neighbor's dog.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבנה **was found by two children** (נמצא על ידי שני ילדים) אומר שהילדים הם אלה שמצאו את הכלב, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על התפקידים האלה במשפט פעיל, בצירוף **two children found** (שני ילדים מצאו).

_**Was found by two children** means that the children did the finding, and the correct answer keeps this in the active form **two children found**._

questionText: Original: If it rains on Saturday, we will play basketball in the gym.

options.label: If it is rainy on Saturday, we will play basketball in the gym with the other class.
If it does not rain on Saturday, we will play basketball in the gym.
We will watch a basketball game in the gym if it rains on Saturday.
On Saturday, if the weather is rainy, we will play basketball in the gym.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התנאי **If it rains on Saturday** (אם יורד גשם בשבת) קובע מתי משחקים באולם הספורט, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת עליו בצירוף **if the weather is rainy** (אם מזג האוויר גשום).

_The condition **If it rains on Saturday** says when they play in the gym, and the correct answer keeps it as **if the weather is rainy**._

questionText: Original: Most of the students in my class bring lunch from home, but a few buy food at school.

options.label: In my class, most students bring their lunch from home, while a small number buy food at school.
Most of the students in my class bring lunch from home, but a few forget it at school.
A few students in my class buy food at school because it is cheaper, but most bring lunch from home.
In my class, a small number of students bring lunch from home, and most buy food at school.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Most of the students** (רוב התלמידים) והצירוף **a few** (מעטים) קובעים מי מביא אוכל מהבית ומי קונה בבית הספר, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם בצירוף **most students** ובצירוף **a small number** (מספר קטן).

_**Most of the students** and **a few** show who brings lunch and who buys food, and the correct answer keeps both as **most students** and **a small number**._

questionText: Original: Many cities now have bike lanes, and cyclists say that the lanes make them feel safer.

options.label: Cyclists report feeling safer thanks to the bike lanes that many cities now have.
Drivers report that bike lanes make them feel safer, and many cities now have them too.
Cyclists say that the lanes have removed the danger from city streets.
Cyclists in a few cities say that the bike lanes there make them feel safer.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **make them feel safer** (גורמים להם להרגיש בטוחים יותר) מתאר רק תחושה של הרוכבים, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על זה, ואילו האפשרות שמדברת על הסרת הסכנה מגזימה.

_**Make them feel safer** describes only a feeling of the cyclists, and the correct answer keeps it, while the option about removing the danger exaggerates._

questionText: Original: Mia could not hear the teacher because the room was very noisy.

options.label: The room was noisy, but Mia could hear the teacher.
Because the room was very noisy, Mia talked loudly to the teacher.
The room was very noisy because Mia could not hear the teacher.
The room was very noisy, so Mia could not hear the teacher.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי) מסמנת שהרעש הוא הסיבה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הקשר הזה בעזרת המילה **so** (לכן) אחרי הצירוף **the room was very noisy**.

_**Because** makes the noise the reason, and the correct answer keeps this link with **so** after **the room was very noisy**._

questionText: Original: Our school was visited last year by a famous writer, who read stories to the younger children.

options.label: Last year, our school went to see a famous writer, who read stories to the younger children.
A famous writer read stories to the younger children at our school and signed books for their parents last year.
Last year, a famous writer came to our school and read stories to the younger children.
A famous writer visited our school last year, reading stories to the older children.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **was visited last year by a famous writer** (ביקר אצלנו בשנה שעברה סופר מפורסם) אומר שהסופר הגיע לבית הספר, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על התפקידים האלה במשפט פעיל, בצירוף **a famous writer came to our school**.

_**Was visited last year by a famous writer** means the writer came to the school, and the correct answer keeps this in **a famous writer came to our school**._

questionText: Original: Although the ferry ride takes longer than the bridge, many commuters prefer it because the tickets are cheaper and the seats are more comfortable.

options.label: Although the tickets are cheaper and the seats are more comfortable on the ferry, many commuters prefer the bridge because the ferry ride takes longer.
Despite taking longer than the bridge, the ferry is preferred by many commuters for its cheaper tickets and more comfortable seats.
Many commuters choose the ferry over the bridge, since the tickets are cheaper and the seats are more comfortable.
Although the ferry ride takes longer than the bridge, many commuters prefer it because the tickets are cheaper and the seats are more crowded.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** (אף על פי ש-) מציגה ניגוד: המעבורת איטית יותר ובכל זאת נוסעים רבים מעדיפים אותה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הניגוד הזה בצירוף **Despite taking longer** (למרות שהנסיעה בה ארוכה יותר).

_**Although** sets up a contrast: the ferry is slower, yet many commuters prefer it, and the correct answer keeps this with **Despite taking longer**._

questionText: Original: Most of the trees along the street survived the dry summer, but some of the younger ones died.

options.label: Most of the older trees along the street died during the dry summer, while the younger ones survived.
Along the street, most trees failed to survive the dry summer, and some of the young ones lived through it.
More than half of the street's trees lived through the dry summer, though some of the younger ones did not.
In the dry summer, few of the trees along the street survived, and most of the younger ones died.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Most of the trees** (רוב העצים) והצירוף **some of the younger ones** (חלק מהצעירים) קובעים כמה שרדו וכמה מתו, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת עליהם בצירוף **More than half of** (רוב) ובצירוף **some of the younger ones**.

_**Most of the trees** survived and **some of the younger ones** died; the correct answer keeps both amounts as **More than half** and **some of the younger ones**._

questionText: Original: The map of the old harbor was drawn by a sailor who had learned the coastline from a local fisherman.

options.label: A sailor drew the map of the old harbor after he had taught a local fisherman the coastline.
A sailor who had learned the coastline from a local fisherman drew the map of the old harbor and sold it to the city.
A local fisherman who had learned the coastline from a sailor drew the map of the old harbor.
After a local fisherman had taught him the coastline, a sailor drew the map of the old harbor.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **was drawn by a sailor** (צוירה על ידי ימאי) קובע מי צייר, והצירוף **from a local fisherman** (מדייג מקומי) קובע מי לימד, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שני התפקידים במשפט פעיל.

_**Was drawn by a sailor** names the mapmaker and **from a local fisherman** names the teacher, and the correct answer keeps both roles in the active form._

questionText: Original: Glass has been used for windows for many centuries because it is made from sand, which is cheap and easy to find.

options.label: Glass has served as a window material for many centuries, because the sand it is made from is cheap and easy to find.
Windows have been made of glass for many centuries because sand is the cheapest and easiest material in the world to find.
Sand is made from glass, which is cheap and easy to find, so people have used it for windows in many places for many centuries.
Because glass is made from sand, it has been used for windows for many centuries.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הסיבה **made from sand, which is cheap and easy to find** (עשויה מן החול, שהוא זול וקל למצוא) כוללת שלושה חלקים, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שלושתם.

_The reason **made from sand, which is cheap and easy to find** has three parts, and the correct answer keeps all three._

questionText: Original: When the bell rang, the students were already sitting at their desks, so the lesson started on time.

options.label: The students were not sitting at their desks when the bell rang, so the lesson started a little late.
The students had already sat down at their desks before the bell rang, so the lesson began on time.
The students were already sitting at their desks, so the teacher rang the bell early.
The students took their seats when the bell rang, so the lesson started on time.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **were already sitting** (כבר ישבו) מראה שהישיבה קרתה לפני הצלצול, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הסדר הזה בצירוף **had already sat down** (כבר התיישבו) ובצירוף **before the bell rang** (לפני שהפעמון צלצל).

_**Were already sitting** puts the sitting before the bell, and the correct answer keeps that order with **had already sat down** and **before the bell rang**._

questionText: Original: Researchers believe that regular exercise may help older adults remember things more easily, although the evidence is still limited.

options.label: Although the evidence is still limited, researchers believe that regular exercise may help older adults remember things for longer.
Researchers have proved that regular exercise helps older adults remember things more easily.
According to researchers, regular exercise may make remembering easier for older adults, although the evidence is still limited.
Older adults who remember things more easily may exercise regularly, researchers believe, although the evidence is still limited.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **may help** (אולי יעזור) והצירוף **still limited** (עדיין מוגבלות) מראים זהירות, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם, ואילו האפשרות עם הצירוף **have proved** (הוכיחו) מגזימה.

_**May help** and **still limited** show caution, and the correct answer keeps both, while **have proved** exaggerates._

questionText: Original: Even though lightning appears to strike at random, tall and pointed objects are hit far more often than flat ground, which is why many buildings are fitted with metal rods.

options.label: Although lightning looks random, it hits tall, pointed objects so much more often than flat ground that it rarely reaches level land, which is why many buildings are fitted with metal rods.
Many buildings are equipped with metal rods because lightning strikes tall, pointed objects far more frequently than flat ground.
Lightning seems to hit places by chance, yet tall, pointed objects are struck much more frequently than level ground, and this is the reason many buildings have metal rods installed.
Because many buildings are fitted with metal rods, lightning appears to strike at random, even though tall and pointed objects are hit far more often than flat ground.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילים **Even though** (אף על פי ש-) מציגות ויתור, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת עליו בעזרת המילה **yet** (ובכל זאת) ושומרת גם על הסיבה למוטות המתכת בעזרת הצירוף **this is the reason**.

_**Even though** sets up a concession, and the correct answer keeps it with **yet** and keeps the reason for the metal rods with **this is the reason**._

questionText: Original: Few of the office staff in the study walked to work, but those who did took noticeably fewer sick days than colleagues who drove.

options.label: A small proportion of office staff in the study walked to work, but these walkers took noticeably fewer sick days than colleagues who drove.

_**Few** means that only a small group walked, and the correct answer keeps this quantity with **a small proportion of** and the result with **noticeably fewer sick days**._

questionText: Original: Although many people believe that they work better under pressure, a survey of project teams suggests that tight deadlines usually lower the quality of the final product.

options.label: Although many people believe that they work better under pressure, a survey of project teams clearly shows that tight deadlines seriously damage the quality of the final product.

questionText: Original: The first exam was written by the university's lecturers, but its questions were reworded by a testing company, which also marked the answers.

questionText: Original: Although the new battery charges in just ten minutes, it lasts fewer hours than older models and must be replaced after roughly two years of regular use.

_The original has three units, **charges in just ten minutes**, **lasts fewer hours** and **must be replaced**, and the correct answer keeps all three and adds nothing._

questionText: Original: Unless farmers near the lake use less fertilizer, the algae that have spread over its surface in recent summers will probably keep growing.

options.label: As long as farmers near the lake use less fertilizer, the algae that have left its water turbid over the past few summers will probably keep growing.

questionText: Original: By the time the printing press reached the small town in 1520, most of its residents had already been taught to read by monks, who had run a school there for over a century.

questionText: Original: Many economists believe that falling prices for solar panels are partly the result of larger factories, although government subsidies probably played a role as well.

questionText: Original: Although the town council had banned street performers from the main square, it later allowed them back after shopkeepers said that the music was attracting more customers.

questionText: Original: Dug by hand through nearly twenty sweltering summers, the canal lost most of its cargo traffic within a decade of its opening to a railway that a rival company had laid along its banks.

questionText: Original: Popular with city drivers around 1900, early electric cars were gradually pushed aside by gasoline models, not because they were unwieldy to drive but because they could cover only short distances between charges.

Adults who are otherwise inactive appear to do their hearts nearly as much good with several brisk walks spread over a week as with one long walk of the same total length.
Several short spells of fast walking during the day seem to help the hearts of otherwise sedentary adults almost as much as a single long walk.
Adults who take several brief bouts of brisk walking spread across a day are otherwise just as sedentary as those who take one long walk of the same total length.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **nearly as much as** (כמעט באותה מידה כמו) קובע שההליכות הקצרות מועילות כמעט כמו ההליכה הארוכה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הכיוון הזה וגם על התנאי **of equal total length**.

_**nearly as much as** means the short walks help almost as much as the long one, and the correct answer keeps this and the condition **of equal total length**._

questionText: Original: Rarely, if ever, did the masons who laid a medieval cathedral's foundations live to see its towers completed, as work, repeatedly stymied by fires and lack of money, often dragged on for over a century.

options.label: Not infrequently, the masons who laid a medieval cathedral's foundations lived to see its towers completed, though the work, repeatedly held up by fires and lack of money, often dragged on for over a century.

Fires and shortages of funds stymied medieval cathedral projects so badly that building one routinely took several centuries, and the masons who started the work therefore never lived to see the towers finished.

The masons who laid the foundations of a medieval cathedral were rarely, if ever, stymied by fires or by a lack of money, so they often lived long enough to see its towers completed within a single century.

The masons who began building a medieval cathedral almost never survived to see its towers finished, because fires and a lack of funds kept holding up work that frequently lasted more than a hundred years.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Rarely, if ever** פירושו כמעט אף פעם, ולכן התשובה הנכונה אומרת שהבנאים **almost never survived to see** (כמעט אף פעם לא זכו לראות) את המגדלים גמורים.

_**Rarely, if ever** means almost never, so the correct answer says the masons **almost never survived to see** the towers finished._

questionText: Original: Only after a conflagration has swept through the forest do the resin-sealed cones of certain pines open and release their seeds, which then sprout in soil cleared of competing plants.

options.label: Certain pines tend to open their resin-sealed cones and release their seeds after a conflagration has swept through the forest, leaving those seeds to sprout in soil that the fire has cleared of competing plants.
Only once certain pines have released the seeds from their resin-sealed cones is a blaze able to sweep through the forest and burn off competing plants.
Certain pines keep their seeds locked inside resin-sealed cones until a fire has swept through the forest, after which the seeds are released and sprout in soil now free of competing plants.
Only after the competing plants have been cleared from the forest soil do certain pines seal their cones with resin, so that a conflagration does not reach the seeds.

explanation:
