questionText: Original: Unable to write down every word, students who take lecture notes by hand must reduce what they hear to pithy summaries, which may help them remember the material better than classmates who type.

options.label: Students who take lecture notes by hand remember the material better than classmates who type, which might be why they can reduce what they hear to pithy summaries instead of writing down every word.
Students who handwrite their lecture notes cannot record everything that is said, so they have to sum it up briefly, and this might give them an advantage in recall over classmates using a keyboard.
Unable to write down every word, students who take lecture notes by hand must reduce what they hear to pithy summaries, which makes them remember the material far better than classmates who type.
Classmates who type their lecture notes can write down every word, so they remember the material better than students who must boil what they hear down to short summaries by hand.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Unable to write down every word** הוא הסיבה לסיכום והמילה **may** מסייגת את היתרון, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם בצירופים **so they have to sum it up** ו-**might give them an advantage** (עשוי לתת להם יתרון).

_**Unable to write down every word** gives the cause of the summaries and **may** hedges the memory gain, and the correct answer keeps both with **so** and **might**._

questionText: Original: Far fewer onlookers notice a sartorial blunder than the person who made it tends to imagine, though it would be rash to conclude that such a blunder goes entirely unnoticed.

options.label: Those who make a fashion mistake usually think many more people see it than really do, but it would be unwise to assume that nobody sees it.
Usually only a handful of onlookers notice a sartorial blunder, though it would be rash to claim that it passes entirely unnoticed.
Onlookers notice a blunder in someone's clothing far less often than the person who made it tends to fear, and it would be rash to assume that anyone notices it.
People who commit a sartorial blunder tend to imagine that far fewer onlookers notice it than actually do, though it would be rash to say it goes entirely unnoticed.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Far fewer ... than ... tends to imagine** אומר שמי שטעה מגזים בהערכה, והאזהרה **rash to conclude ... entirely unnoticed** אומרת שיש רואים, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם בצירוף **many more ... than really do**.

_**Far fewer ... than ... tends to imagine** means the wearer overestimates, and **rash to conclude ... entirely unnoticed** means some do notice; the correct answer keeps both._

questionText: Ben forgot his keys, so he could not ________ the front door.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **forgot his keys** (שכח את המפתחות) מראה שבן לא יכול היה להיכנס, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **open** (לפתוח).

_**Forgot his keys** is the cause, and **so** gives the result: without keys, Ben could not **open** the front door._

questionText: My sister likes loud music, but I like ________ music.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** (אבל) מסמנת ניגוד ל-**loud music** (מוזיקה רועשת), ולכן הדובר אוהב מוזיקה **quiet** (שקטה).

_**But** signals a contrast with **loud music**, so the speaker likes **quiet** (not loud) music._

questionText: Doctors say we should avoid ________ drinks, such as cola, because they contain a lot of sugar.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמה **such as cola** (כמו קולה) והסיבה **a lot of sugar** (הרבה סוכר) מראות שהרופאים מזהירים ממשקאות **sweet** (מתוקים).

_The example **such as cola** and the reason **a lot of sugar** show that doctors warn against **sweet** drinks._

questionText: Josh broke the window, but he decided to tell his teacher the ________.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** (אבל) מסמנת ניגוד לשבירת החלון (**broke the window**), והצירוף הקבוע **tell the truth** (לומר את האמת) הוא מה שג'וש החליט לעשות.

_**But** contrasts with **broke the window**, and the fixed phrase is to **tell the truth**._

questionText: The market was so ________ on Saturday that it was hard to walk between the tables.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבנה **so ... that** (כל כך ש...) מראה שהתוצאה, **hard to walk between the tables** (קשה ללכת בין השולחנות), נובעת מכך שהשוק היה **crowded** (צפוף).

_The pattern **so ... that** gives a result, **hard to walk between the tables**, that comes from a **crowded** market._

questionText: Although days in the desert are dry and extremely hot, the nights can be surprisingly ________.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** (למרות ש...) מסמנת ניגוד לימים החמים מאוד (**extremely hot**), ולכן הלילות הם באופן מפתיע **chilly** (קרירים).

_**Although** signals a contrast with the **extremely hot** days, so the nights are surprisingly **chilly** (cold)._

questionText: The new teacher was very ________: she explained each idea several times, and she never lost her temper when students asked the same question again.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מסבירים את המילה החסרה: מורה שמסבירה כל רעיון כמה פעמים ואינה כועסת (**never lost her temper**) היא **patient** (סבלנית).

_The colon explains the blank: a teacher who explains ideas several times and **never lost her temper** is **patient**._

questionText: Because the instructions were so ________, many customers could not build the bookshelf and called the shop for help.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Because** (כי) והתוצאה **could not build the bookshelf** (לא הצליחו להרכיב את הכוננית) מראות שההוראות היו **confusing** (מבלבלות).

_**Because** introduces a cause, and the result, **could not build the bookshelf**, shows that the instructions were **confusing**._

questionText: Unless the weather becomes ________ before Friday afternoon, the school festival will take place outdoors as planned.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Unless** (אלא אם כן) מראה שהתוכנית לקיים את הפסטיבל בחוץ (**outdoors as planned**) תשתנה רק אם מזג האוויר יהיה **severe** (קשה, חמור).

_**Unless** means 'if not': the festival stays **outdoors as planned** unless the weather becomes **severe** (very bad)._

questionText: Although the first version of the software was praised for its speed, users soon found it ________: it crashed whenever they opened more than three files at once.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** (למרות ש...) מסמנת ניגוד לשבחים על המהירות, והסבר הקריסות (**it crashed**) מראה שהתוכנה **unreliable** (לא אמינה).

_**Although** contrasts the praise for speed with a problem, and **it crashed** shows the software was **unreliable** (not dependable)._

questionText: Despite being drawn with great care by a skilled artist, the map was ________ in many details: rivers appeared in the wrong places and two of the towns did not exist.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Despite** (למרות) מסמנת ניגוד לציור הקפדני (**with great care**), וההסבר אחרי הנקודתיים (**in the wrong places**) מראה שהמפה הייתה **inaccurate** (לא מדויקת).

_**Despite** contrasts the great care with the errors, and **in the wrong places** shows the map was **inaccurate** (not correct)._

questionText: While her novels sell millions of copies every year, the author herself is famously ________: she rarely gives interviews and avoids public events.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מסבירים את המילה החסרה: מי שכמעט אינה נותנת ראיונות ונמנעת מאירועים ציבוריים (**rarely gives interviews and avoids public events**) היא **reclusive** (מתבודדת).

_The colon explains the blank: someone who **rarely gives interviews and avoids public events** is **reclusive** (keeps away from people)._

questionText: Although the patient looked perfectly healthy, he had to ________ several tests before the doctors allowed him to leave the hospital.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **undergo tests** (לעבור בדיקות) מתאים למטופל שנבדק לפני שהרופאים מתירים לו ללכת (**before the doctors allowed him to leave**).

_The fixed phrase is **undergo tests**: a patient is examined **before the doctors allowed him to leave** the hospital._

questionText: Although news reports tend to focus on sudden disasters, many environmental hazards, such as slow poisoning from polluted water or years of lung damage from dust, are ________ and therefore easy to overlook.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות **slow poisoning** ו-**years of lung damage** מתארות נזק איטי, והמילה **Although** מנגידה אותו לאסונות פתאומיים (**sudden disasters**), ולכן הסכנות הן **gradual** (הדרגתיות).

_The examples **slow poisoning** and **years of lung damage** describe slow harm, which **Although** contrasts with **sudden disasters**, so the hazards are **gradual**._

questionText: Although the manager's speech was ________, listing every complaint in detail, it offered no practical way to solve any of them.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **listing every complaint in detail** (רישום מפורט של כל תלונה) מתאר נאום **thorough** (יסודי), והמילה **Although** מנגידה אותו לחוסר פתרון מעשי.

_**Listing every complaint in detail** describes a **thorough** speech, and **Although** contrasts it with the lack of a practical solution._

questionText: Although donations to the animal shelter rose sharply after its televised appeal, they soon began to ________, and within a year the monthly total was smaller than it had been before the broadcast.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** מסמנת ניגוד לעלייה החדה, והסוף **smaller than it had been before the broadcast** מראה ירידה של ממש, ולכן התשובה היא **dwindle** (להצטמצם, להתמעט).

_**Although** contrasts with the sharp rise, and **smaller than it had been before the broadcast** shows a real decline, so the answer is **dwindle** (shrink gradually)._

questionText: After a decade without a serious flood, residents of the bucolic river valley had grown ________, leaving drainage channels uncleared and sandbags rotting in storage, so last spring's storm caught them almost entirely unprepared.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** עשור בלי שיטפון (**After a decade without a serious flood**) הוביל להזנחה (**leaving drainage channels uncleared**), ולכן התשובה היא **lax** (רשלני, לא מקפיד).

_A decade with no flood led to **drainage channels uncleared** and an unprepared town, so residents had grown **lax** (careless about precautions)._

questionText: Doctors advise against flying, however propitious the timing, until a patient's fever has begun to ________, that is, until the temperature has stayed below 38 degrees Celsius for a full day.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **that is** מסביר שהחום נשאר מתחת ל-38 מעלות יממה שלמה (**stayed below 38 degrees Celsius for a full day**), ולכן התשובה היא **abate** (לשכוך, להיחלש).

_**That is** explains the blank: the temperature **stayed below 38 degrees Celsius for a full day**, so the fever has begun to **abate** (become less strong)._

questionText: Small farmers who grow ________ crops, such as strawberries, lettuce and fresh herbs, must sell them within days of the harvest and therefore have little power to hold out for a better price.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות (**strawberries, lettuce and fresh herbs**) והחובה למכור בתוך ימים (**must sell them within days of the harvest**) מצביעות על יבול שמתקלקל מהר, ולכן התשובה היא **perishable** (מתכלה).

_The examples and **must sell them within days of the harvest** point to crops that spoil fast, so the answer is **perishable** (likely to go bad quickly)._

questionText: When the school trip was canceled, a clause buried in the contract's turgid small print meant that the tour operator, not the parents, had to ________ the bill for the unused hotel rooms.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **foot the bill** (לשאת בתשלום) מתאים לחובה שהסעיף הטיל (**had to**) על צד אחד בלבד (**the tour operator, not the parents**), ולכן התשובה היא **foot**.

_**Foot the bill** means pay it, and the clause made one side pay alone, **the tour operator, not the parents**, so the answer is **foot**._

questionText: Amid the welter of events at the university's open day, three introductory lectures are ________, so visitors must choose between biology, history and economics, all of which begin at ten o'clock.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** החלקים **con** (יחד) ו-**cur** (לרוץ) נותנים 'רצים יחד', כמו בהסבר **all of which begin at ten o'clock**, ולכן התשובה היא **concurrent** (מתקיים בו-זמנית).

_**Con** (together) plus **cur** (run) gives 'running together', which matches **all of which begin at ten o'clock**, so the answer is **concurrent**._

questionText: Heavy snow did not stop the town's intrepid delivery drivers, but it did ________ their progress, so that a route that usually takes an hour took nearly five.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירופים **did not stop** ו-**but it did** אומרים שהשלג לא עצר אבל כן הפריע, והתוצאה **took nearly five** מראה האטה, ולכן התשובה היא **hamper** (לעכב, להכביד).

_The snow **did not stop** the drivers, **but it did** slow them (**took nearly five**), so the answer is **hamper** (make progress slow and difficult)._

questionText: Sailors long regarded a ring around the moon as a ________ of storms: the ring itself does nothing to stir up the wind, but it often appears a day or so before bad weather arrives.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הטבעת אינה גורמת לרוח (**does nothing to stir up the wind**) אבל מופיעה לפני מזג האוויר הרע (**before bad weather arrives**), ולכן התשובה היא **harbinger** (מבשר, סימן מקדים).

_The ring **does nothing to stir up the wind** yet comes **before bad weather arrives**, so it is a **harbinger** (an early sign of something coming)._

questionText: Far from being the ________ genius of later legend, the composer kept meticulous accounts, answered every letter within a week and rarely missed a rehearsal.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבנה **Far from being** דורש את ההפך מן הפרטים שבהמשך, ומי שניהל חשבונות בקפדנות וענה לכל מכתב (**kept meticulous accounts, answered every letter**) היה אחראי, ולכן התשובה היא **feckless** (חסר אחריות).

_**Far from being** demands the opposite of someone who **kept meticulous accounts, answered every letter**, so the answer is **feckless** (irresponsible and disorganized)._

questionText: The popular claim that people use only ten percent of their brains is not a scientific finding but a ________: a baseless story repeated so often that many accept it without question.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים מגדיר את החסר כסיפור חסר בסיס שחוזר שוב ושוב (**a baseless story repeated so often**), ולכן התשובה היא **canard** (שמועת שווא, בדותה).

_The colon defines the blank as **a baseless story repeated so often** that people believe it, so the answer is **canard** (a false, widely spread story)._

questionText: Even Victorian novels praised for their verisimilitude rely heavily on ________: the long-lost heir who turns up in the final chapter, for example, or the letter that arrives at exactly the moment the plot requires.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות, כמו מכתב שמגיע בדיוק כשהעלילה צריכה אותו (**exactly the moment the plot requires**), הן פתרונות מאולצים, ולכן התשובה היא **contrivance** (תחבולה מלאכותית).

_The examples, like a letter arriving at **exactly the moment the plot requires**, are artificial devices, so the answer is **contrivance** (an obviously planned, unnatural device)._

questionText: Plans for a second runway have been in ________ since the airline that was to use it went bankrupt: they remain unchanged and uncanceled, but no work will start until a new tenant is found.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **in abeyance** (מוקפא, מושהה זמנית) מתאים לתוכניות שלא בוטלו (**unchanged and uncanceled**) אבל מחכות (**until a new tenant is found**), ולכן התשובה היא **abeyance**.

_**In abeyance** means suspended for now, matching plans that remain **unchanged and uncanceled** but wait **until a new tenant is found**._

questionText: Teachers once dismissed disruptive pupils as ________, convinced that no amount of discipline or advice would change their conduct, yet later studies found that most embraced real responsibility with alacrity.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** החלקים **in** (לא), **corrig** (לתקן) ו-**ible** (ניתן) נותנים 'שאי אפשר לתקן', כמו בהסבר **no amount of discipline or advice would change their conduct**, ולכן התשובה היא **incorrigible** (חסר תקנה).

_**In** (not) + **corrig** (correct) + **ible** (able) gives 'cannot be corrected', matching **no amount of discipline or advice would change their conduct**, so the answer is **incorrigible**._

questionText: The village's sleepy appearance, all shuttered cottages and torpid cats, ________ its history: for nearly three centuries it was the busiest port on the coast, crowded with ships from a dozen countries.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המראה המנומנם (**sleepy appearance**) סותר את העבר כנמל העמוס ביותר בחוף (**the busiest port on the coast**), ולכן התשובה היא **belies** (נותן רושם כוזב).

_A **sleepy appearance** gives a false picture of **the busiest port on the coast**, so the answer is **belies** (gives a false impression of)._

questionText: The philosopher was ________ rather than ascetic: he drank a single glass of wine with dinner and ate sparingly, but he never denied himself the pleasures of good company, music or travel.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** כוס יין אחת ואכילה במשורה (**a single glass of wine with dinner and ate sparingly**) מראות מתינות ולא התנזרות, ולכן התשובה היא **abstemious** (מתון באכילה ובשתייה).

_Drinking **a single glass of wine** and eating **sparingly** shows moderation, not total refusal, so the answer is **abstemious** (moderate in eating and drinking)._

questionText: It was a very hot day, so we went to the ________ and swam all afternoon.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפועל **swam** (שחינו) מראה שהלכו למקום שבו אפשר לשחות, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **pool** (בריכה).

_The word **swam** shows they went to a place for swimming on a **very hot day**, so the answer is **pool** (a place built for swimming)._

questionText: Our new neighbor is very ________; she smiles and says hello to everyone.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההסבר שאחרי הנקודה-פסיק, **she smiles and says hello to everyone**, מתאר אדם נחמד, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **friendly** (ידידותית).

_What follows the semicolon, **she smiles and says hello to everyone**, explains the blank, so the neighbor is **friendly** (kind and open to people)._

questionText: Rita was ________ for school today because her bus broke down on the way.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי) מסבירה את התוצאה: האוטובוס התקלקל בדרך (**her bus broke down on the way**), ולכן ריטה הגיעה באיחור, **late** (מאחרת), לבית הספר.

_The word **because** links the result to its cause: **her bus broke down on the way**, so Rita was **late** (not on time) for school._

questionText: If you walk in the rain without a coat, you may ________ a cold.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **catch a cold** (להצטנן) הוא היחיד שמתאים לשם העצם **a cold**, וההליכה בגשם בלי מעיל (**walk in the rain without a coat**) מסבירה למה זה קורה.

_The fixed phrase **catch a cold** (to become ill with a cold) fits **a cold**, and walking **in the rain without a coat** explains why it can happen._

questionText: Some chemicals are ________; for example, strong cleaning liquids can burn the skin.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **for example** (למשל) מביא דוגמה: נוזלי ניקוי חזקים יכולים לשרוף את העור (**can burn the skin**), ולכן המילה החסרה היא **harmful** (מזיק).

_**For example** introduces an instance: strong cleaning liquids **can burn the skin**, so some chemicals are **harmful** (able to hurt people)._

questionText: Even though Carlos had studied English for only one year, his speaking was already ________, and many visitors thought he was a native speaker.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Even though** (אף על פי ש) מעמיד את שנת הלימוד היחידה (**only one year**) מול התוצאה, ולכן הדיבור של קרלוס היה כבר **fluent** (שוטף), עד שחשבו שהוא דובר שפת אם.

_**Even though** he had studied for **only one year**, his speaking was already **fluent** (smooth and easy), so visitors thought he was a **native speaker**._

questionText: The rule was ________ because it allowed only some students to enter the competition.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי) מסבירה מה הבעיה בכלל: הוא איפשר רק לחלק מהתלמידים להשתתף (**allowed only some students**), ולכן הוא **unfair** (לא הוגן).

_Because the rule **allowed only some students** to enter, it treated people differently, so it was **unfair**: **un-** means not, and **fair** means equal and just._

questionText: Whereas a cup of strong coffee keeps most people awake, a warm bath in the evening often makes them feel ________.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Whereas** (ואילו) מציבה את הרחצה החמה מול הקפה שמעיר אנשים (**keeps most people awake**), ולכן היא גורמת להם להרגיש **sleepy** (מנומנמים).

_**Whereas** sets the warm bath against coffee that **keeps most people awake**, so the bath makes them feel **sleepy** (ready for sleep)._

questionText: Students who study in a ________ place, such as a quiet library, usually remember more than those who study next to a loud television.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** (כמו) מביא דוגמה, ספרייה שקטה (**a quiet library**), והמשפט מעמיד אותה מול טלוויזיה רועשת, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **peaceful** (שליו, שקט).

_**Such as** gives an example, **a quiet library**, set against a **loud television**, so the blank means **peaceful** (quiet and calm)._

questionText: Although the school committee was ________ to change its old timetable, a flood of complaints from parents finally persuaded its members to try a new one.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Although** (למרות ש) והמילה **finally** (לבסוף) מראים שהוועדה התנגדה בתחילה והתלונות שיכנעו אותה (**finally persuaded**), ולכן המילה החסרה היא **reluctant** (לא ששה, חסרת רצון).

_**Although** and **finally persuaded** show that the committee first resisted change, so it was **reluctant** (unwilling) to change its timetable._

questionText: Although the experiment was carried out with great care, it produced ________ results: when repeated three times, it gave a different answer every time.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מסבירים את החסר: כשחזרו על הניסוי התקבלה בכל פעם תשובה שונה (**a different answer every time**), ולכן התוצאות היו **inconsistent** (לא עקביות), למרות הזהירות הרבה.

_The colon explains the blank: repeating it gave **a different answer every time**, so despite the great care (**Although**) the results were **inconsistent** (not the same)._

questionText: Although the two companies had disagreed about prices for months, they finally ________ an agreement after one last night of talks.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** שם העצם **an agreement** קובע את הצירוף הקבוע **reach an agreement** (להגיע להסכמה), והצירוף **Although** עם **finally** מראה שאחרי חודשי ויכוח (**disagreed about prices for months**) הגיעו להסכמה.

_**Reach an agreement** is a fixed phrase, and **Although** with **finally** shows that after months of disagreement the companies at last **reached** one._

questionText: Although the earliest electric buses could run for only an hour between charges, ________ models, built over the next ten years, managed a full day.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **built over the next ten years** מראה שהדגמים נבנו אחרי הראשונים, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **subsequent** (מאוחרים יותר), והצירוף **Although** מעמיד את הדגמים האלה מול האוטובוסים הראשונים.

_**Built over the next ten years** shows these models came after the earliest ones, so the blank is **subsequent** (coming later), which **Although** contrasts with **the earliest** buses._

questionText: Although many people believe that a large vocabulary makes someone a good writer, great authors often use ________ words, choosing the simplest term that expresses their meaning.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Although** (למרות ש) מציג אמונה נפוצה על אוצר מילים גדול, וההמשך, **choosing the simplest term**, מראה שסופרים גדולים משתמשים במילים פשוטות, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **ordinary** (רגילות).

_**Although** introduces a common belief about a large vocabulary, and **choosing the simplest term** shows that great authors use **ordinary** (everyday) words._

questionText: Although many trees, such as oaks and maples, lose all their leaves each autumn, others, such as pines and firs, are ________.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** (כמו) נותן דוגמאות לעצים שמאבדים את עליהם (**oaks and maples**), והמילה **others** מעמידה מולם עצים אחרים, **pines and firs**, ולכן המילה החסרה היא **evergreen** (ירוקי עד).

_**Such as** gives examples of trees that **lose all their leaves**, and **others** sets different trees against them, so pines and firs are **evergreen** (they keep their leaves)._

questionText: Because the signal from the probe, now far beyond Pluto, was ________, arriving in brief bursts separated by long stretches of silence, the mission's dogged engineers needed weeks to piece together a single image.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף שאחרי החסר מתאר אות שמגיע בפרצים קצרים עם שתיקות ארוכות ביניהם (**brief bursts separated by long stretches of silence**), ולכן התשובה היא **intermittent** (לסירוגין, מקוטע).

_A signal **arriving in brief bursts separated by long stretches of silence** keeps stopping and starting, so it is **intermittent** (on and off)._

questionText: Unlike its predecessor, which fined shops heavily for every peccadillo, the new consumer agency is relatively ________, preferring warnings to fines; yet it is not careless: it inspects every store twice a year.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Unlike** מציבה את הסוכנות מול קודמתה, שקנסה בכבדות, והיא מעדיפה אזהרות (**preferring warnings to fines**) אך אינה רשלנית, ולכן התשובה היא **lenient** (מקל, סלחני).

_**Unlike** a predecessor that fined heavily, the agency prefers **warnings to fines** yet **is not careless**, so it is **lenient** (mild in punishing)._

questionText: For the impoverished mountain village, the sale of a rocky hillside it had long considered worthless was a genuine ________, an unexpected fortune that paid for a new school and a clinic.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף שאחרי החסר מגדיר אותו כהון לא צפוי (**an unexpected fortune**) ממכירת אדמה שנחשבה חסרת ערך, ולכן התשובה היא **windfall** (רווח פתאומי ובלתי צפוי).

_The phrase **an unexpected fortune**, from land the village had **long considered worthless**, defines a **windfall** (a sudden, unexpected gain)._

questionText: Although ________ technologies such as the pager and the fax machine have all but vanished from most offices, many hospitals keep them as stalwart backups for when the network fails.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות **the pager and the fax machine** הן מכשירים ישנים שכמעט נעלמו מן המשרדים (**have all but vanished**), ולכן התשובה היא **obsolete** (מיושן, שעבר זמנו).

_The examples **the pager and the fax machine**, which **have all but vanished from most offices**, are **obsolete** (out of date) technologies._

questionText: Delays of an hour or more are ________ for the course on the island's ramshackle single-track railway, so locals rarely complain and simply bring a book.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילים **for the course** והעובדה שהתושבים כמעט אינם מתלוננים (**locals rarely complain**) מובילות לביטוי **par for the course** (דבר רגיל וצפוי), ולכן התשובה היא **par**.

_**For the course** and **locals rarely complain** point to the idiom **par for the course** (normal and expected), so the answer is **par**._

questionText: The poet won no prizes and sold few books during her lifetime; her fame was entirely ________, arriving only decades after her death, when a scholar found her notebooks moldering in an attic.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התהילה הגיעה רק עשרות שנים אחרי מות המשוררת (**arriving only decades after her death**), ולכן התשובה היא **posthumous** (שלאחר המוות), עם התחילית **post-** (אחרי).

_Fame **arriving only decades after her death** is **posthumous** (coming after death); **post-** means 'after'._

questionText: Rather than banning skateboards outright and facing a deluge of complaints, the town fitted its benches and low walls with small metal studs, which ________ skaters without preventing anyone from sitting down.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הבליטות באות במקום איסור (**Rather than banning**) ואינן מונעות מאיש לשבת (**without preventing anyone from sitting down**), ולכן התשובה היא **deter** (להרתיע).

_The studs work **Rather than banning** and **without preventing anyone from sitting down**, so they **deter** (discourage) skaters._

questionText: In the 1830s the art of photography was still ________: a single portrait demanded minutes of perfect stillness, and few people yet imagined that it might one day rival painting.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילים **still** ו-**yet** וההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים מתארים אמנות בתחילת דרכה, עם חשיפות ארוכות ועתיד שעוד לא נראה, ולכן התשובה היא **nascent** (מתהווה, בראשית דרכו).

_**Still**, **yet** and the details after the colon describe an art just beginning, so photography was **nascent** (newly forming)._

questionText: On the eve of the competition final, the young pianist seemed almost ________ — not reckless, for she had practiced every piece for months, but untroubled, chatting with friends while her rivals paced the corridor.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבנה **not reckless ... but untroubled** מגדיר את החסר כשלווה חסרת דאגה של מי שהתכוננה היטב, ולכן התשובה היא **insouciant** (שליו וחסר דאגה, קליל).

_The frame **not reckless ... but untroubled** describes calm, carefree ease, so she seemed **insouciant** (relaxed and unconcerned)._

questionText: The medieval town's rapacious growth all but ________ its Roman core: its houses were torn down for their stone, and only some paving beneath a few cellars survives.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **all but** פירושו כמעט לגמרי, ורק מעט ריצוף שרד (**only some paving beneath a few cellars survives**), ולכן התשובה היא **obliterated** (נמחה, הושמד כליל).

_The phrase **all but** means almost completely, and **only some paving beneath a few cellars survives**, so the core was almost entirely **obliterated** (destroyed)._

questionText: Though often handsome, with grand town halls, nineteenth-century factory towns were notoriously ________ places to live, with conditions such as coal smoke, open sewers and drinking water drawn from polluted rivers.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות שאחרי הצירוף **such as**, עשן פחם, ביוב פתוח ומי שתייה ממקור מזוהם, הן כולן סכנות לבריאות, ולכן התשובה היא **unwholesome** (לא בריא, מזיק לבריאות).

_The examples after **such as** (**coal smoke, open sewers and drinking water drawn from polluted rivers**) all harm health, so the towns were **unwholesome** (unhealthy)._

questionText: Cheap smartphones brought about a ________ change in how travelers find their way: within a decade, the folding paper map, once a fixture of every glove box, had become a mere curio.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** שינוי שבתוך עשור הפך את מפת הנייר לחפץ נדיר (**had become a mere curio**) הוא **a sea change** (שינוי עמוק ויסודי), ולכן התשובה היא **sea**.

_A change that, **within a decade**, turned the paper map into **a mere curio** is **a sea change** (a deep, complete transformation), so the answer is **sea**._

questionText: Although the novel's narrator is a lugubrious village doctor speaking in the first person, she is curiously ________, reporting the private thoughts of strangers and knowing how each of their lives will end.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** היא מדווחת על מחשבות של זרים ויודעת איך יסתיימו חייהם (**knowing how each of their lives will end**), כלומר יודעת הכול, ולכן התשובה היא **omniscient** (יודע-כל: **omni-** = כל, **sci** = לדעת).

_Reporting **the private thoughts of strangers** and **knowing how each of their lives will end** means knowing everything: **omniscient** (all-knowing)._

questionText: A good referee, however vociferous the home crowd, must be ________: she may care deeply about the sport itself, but she must have no stake in which team wins.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי ההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים, מותר לה לאהוב את הספורט, אבל אסור שיהיה לה אינטרס בתוצאה (**no stake in which team wins**), ולכן התשובה היא **disinterested** (חסר פניות, ללא אינטרס אישי).

_She **may care deeply about the sport itself** but must have **no stake in which team wins**, so she must be **disinterested** (impartial, with no personal interest)._

questionText: Even the historian's most persistent critics offered ________ praise for her new edition of the chronicle: they still disputed her conclusions, but conceded that no one had ever assembled the evidence so carefully.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבקרים עדיין חלקו על מסקנותיה אבל הודו (**still disputed her conclusions, but conceded**) שאיש לא אסף ראיות בקפידה כזאת, ולכן התשובה היא **grudging** (שניתן בחצי פה, בחוסר רצון).

_Critics who **still disputed her conclusions, but conceded** her care give praise unwillingly, so it was **grudging** (given reluctantly)._

questionText: What does the lecturer say about the three hearts of an octopus?

options.label: Two are spares that take over if the main heart fails
The third serves the gills while the two small ones serve the body
The three of them pump blood through the gills to gain oxygen
Each of them moves blood along its own section of the journey

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **Each heart simply handles a different part of the trip** (כל לב פשוט אחראי על חלק אחר של המסלול), כל לב מזרים את הדם בקטע משלו: שני הלבבות הקטנים לזימים, והשלישי לשאר הגוף.

_The two small hearts serve the gills and the third serves the body, so **each heart simply handles a different part of the trip**._

questionText: According to the man, why did the seedlings in the cupboard grow taller?

options.label: They were in better health than the seedlings left on the windowsill
The dark cupboard kept them warmer than the seedlings near the window
They put their growth into height in an attempt to find light
Their stems were already sturdy, which left energy for height

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **Because they're searching for it** (כי הנבטים מחפשים את האור) והצירוף **spends its energy stretching upward** (משקיע את האנרגיה בגדילה כלפי מעלה), הנבטים גבהו כדי להגיע אל האור.

_The seedlings grew tall **because they're searching for** light: each one **spends its energy stretching upward**._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what did Mendeleev do where the pattern broke down?

options.label: He kept a place empty rather than squeeze an element into it
He put the nearest element there and simply marked it as uncertain
He moved those elements to a separate list at the end
He stopped the table at the point where the pattern ended

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **Instead, he left a gap** (במקום זאת, הוא השאיר משבצת ריקה), מנדלייב לא דחק יסוד למקום שאינו מתאים לו, אלא השאיר את המקום פנוי.

_Where the pattern broke down, **he didn't force an element into the wrong place**; **instead, he left a gap**._

questionText: What does the lecturer see as the greatest strength of the table?

options.label: It sorted elements that act alike into neat groups
It foretold elements that had not yet been detected
It corrected mistakes that earlier chemists had made
It gave exact weights for the elements known then

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **They showed that it could predict, not just organize** (הרווחים הראו שהטבלה יכולה לחזות, ולא רק לסדר), כוחה הגדול של הטבלה היה בחיזוי יסודות שהתגלו רק מאוחר יותר.

_The gaps **showed that it could predict, not just organize**: the elements he described were found later._

questionText: According to the professor, what did about half of the people in the study do?

options.label: They stopped giving directions once they saw a new face
They went on helping a new person without realizing it
They noticed the change but were too polite to mention it
They helped the two workers carry the door down the street

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **They kept giving directions to a completely new person** (הנבדקים המשיכו לתת הוראות דרך לאדם חדש לגמרי), כמחצית מהנבדקים המשיכו לעזור בלי לשים לב להחלפה.

_**About half of them didn't** notice: **they kept giving directions to a completely new person**._

questionText: How does the professor explain the result of the study?

options.label: Their eyesight was weaker than they themselves believed
They kept looking away from the stranger while they were giving directions
Their minds kept the general sense of the scene but few details
The first and second strangers looked almost exactly like each other

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **we actually store very little** (בפועל אנחנו שומרים מעט מאוד), המוח שומר רק את מה שנראה חשוב ברגע זה ומשלים את השאר, ולכן הנבדקים זכרו את התמונה הכללית בלבד.

_**We actually store very little**: **our brains keep only what seems important at the moment** and fill in the rest._

questionText: According to the lecturer, how are most limestone caves formed?

options.label: Underground rivers rush through the rock and grind it away over many years
A strong acid stored deep inside the rock burns tunnels through it
Movements of the ground crack the rock open and leave wide empty spaces
Rain that absorbs a gas in the soil slowly eats the rock away

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **the real work was done much more quietly, by rainwater** (העבודה האמיתית נעשתה בשקט רב יותר, בידי מי הגשם), המערות נוצרות ממי גשם שקולטים פחמן דו־חמצני מהקרקע וממיסים את הסלע.

_**But in most limestone caves, the real work was done much more quietly, by rainwater**, which **picks up carbon dioxide** and dissolves the rock._

questionText: According to the lecturer, why does a drop hanging from a cave roof leave mineral behind?

options.label: Some of the gas it carries escapes into the air of the cave
It picks up extra carbon dioxide from the rock of the cave roof
The cold air in the cave turns part of the drop into ice
It meets river water that flows along the floor of the cave

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **loses some of its carbon dioxide into the air** (מאבדת לאוויר חלק מהפחמן הדו־חמצני), הטיפה כבר לא יכולה להחזיק את כל הגיר המומס, ולכן היא משאירה מינרל.

_When a drop **loses some of its carbon dioxide into the air**, it **can no longer hold all of the limestone it dissolved**._

questionText: According to the woman, why did historians doubt the sagas for many years?

options.label: They were written in an old language that few historians could read
They gave dates that clashed with the remains that were found in Canada
They were recorded long after the voyages and blended fact with myth
They spoke of iron tools that the Norse did not yet possess

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההיסטוריונים פקפקו בסאגות כי הן נכתבו מאות שנים אחרי האירועים (**written down centuries after the events**) ומערבבות תיאורי מסע עם אגדה (**they mix travel with legend**).

_After **Not really**, she explains that **the sagas were written down centuries after the events, and they mix travel with legend**._

questionText: What point does the woman make at the end of the discussion?

options.label: The site shows that the sagas are correct down to the last detail
The site confirms the voyage but not each part of the stories
The site dates from a time long after the voyages in the sagas
Historians should trust written records more than finds in the ground

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף **Well, not entirely** (טוב, לא לגמרי) בא המשפט **It doesn't prove that every detail of the sagas is true** (האתר לא מוכיח שכל פרט בסאגות נכון), ולכן האתר מאשר את המסע אך לא כל פרט.

_**The site proves that Norse sailors were there**, but **it doesn't prove that every detail of the sagas is true**._

questionText: According to the lecturer, how does soap help water remove grease?

options.label: It breaks the grease down into parts that dissolve in water
Its water-loving ends sink deep into the grease and hold it in place
It coats the pan with a film that stops grease from sticking
It traps small bits of grease so that water washes them away

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **surround tiny drops of it** (מקיפים טיפות זעירות של השומן) והמשפט **water can then carry those drops away** (המים יכולים לסחוף את הטיפות), הסבון לוכד את טיפות השומן כך שהמים שוטפים אותן.

_Soap does not break grease down; its oily ends **surround tiny drops of it**, so **water can then carry those drops away**._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what is the purpose of these joints?

options.label: To hold the bridge firmly in place when the weather turns hot
To make a regular noise that tells drivers they are crossing a bridge
To let the bridge stretch and contract as temperatures rise and fall
To mark weak spots where the bridge is likely to crack

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **grow slightly longer when they warm up** (הפלדה והבטון מתארכים מעט כשהם מתחממים) והמשפט **They let it move safely** (רצועות המתכת מאפשרות לגשר לזוז בבטחה), המרווחים נותנים לגשר מקום להתארך ולהתקצר.

_Steel and concrete **grow slightly longer when they warm up**, and the joints **let it move safely** instead of letting it crack._

questionText: According to the man, why do planets shine more steadily than stars?

options.label: Their light comes from a small area rather than one point
Their light is too bright for its small changes to be noticed
Their light is made steadier by the moving air above us
Their light travels to us in a narrower beam than a star's

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **A planet shows up as a small disk** (כוכב לכת נראה כדסקה קטנה), האור של כוכב הלכת מגיע משטח קטן ולא מנקודה אחת, ולכן ההבהובים מתקזזים.

_**A planet shows up as a small disk**, so **its light comes from many points at once** and the flickers **average out**._

questionText: What does the lecturer mainly explain?

options.label: How farmers learned to grow clover and wheat side by side
Why the nitrogen in the air is of little use to most plants
How scientists replaced an old farming rule with a much better one
Why wheat grew better in a field that had just grown clover

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **they had no idea why the rule worked** (החקלאים לא ידעו מדוע הכלל עובד) והמשפט **the old rule wasn't luck** (הכלל הישן לא היה מזל), ההרצאה מסבירה מדוע חיטה גדלה טוב יותר אחרי שנה של תלתן.

_The farmers **had no idea why the rule worked**, and the lecture shows that **the old rule wasn't luck**: clover leaves nitrogen for the wheat._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what do the bacteria in the root swellings do?

options.label: They carry nitrogen out of the soil and release it into the air
They change the air's nitrogen into a nutrient plants can use
They help the roots of the wheat reach deeper into the soil
They guard the clover's roots against insects in the ground

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **bacteria that turn nitrogen from the air into a form plants can absorb** (חיידקים שהופכים חנקן מן האוויר לצורה שצמחים יכולים לקלוט), החיידקים ממירים את החנקן שבאוויר לחומר מזין לצמחים.

_The swellings hold **bacteria that turn nitrogen from the air into a form plants can absorb**._

questionText: According to the man, why are distant contacts often useful in a job search?

options.label: They are more willing to help than close friends tend to be
They belong to other social groups and so hear different news
They share a person's circle and so hear the same news first
They have usually spent more years working than close friends have

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **A casual acquaintance moves in different circles** (מישהו שמכירים רק בשטחיות נע בחוגים חברתיים אחרים), אנשי קשר רחוקים שייכים לקבוצות אחרות ולכן מביאים חדשות שחברים קרובים אינם שומעים.

_**A casual acquaintance moves in different circles**, so such contacts bring **news from outside your own group**._

questionText: What does the man say about close friends at the end of the conversation?

options.label: They are of little use, as they seldom hear about new jobs
They usually hear of more openings than distant contacts do
They tend to give poorer job advice than casual acquaintances do
They still matter, as they may be keener to lend a hand

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **I wouldn't go that far** (לא הייתי מרחיק לכת כל כך) והמשפט **Close friends may be more eager to help** (ייתכן שחברים קרובים להוטים יותר לעזור), חברים קרובים עדיין חשובים.

_He answers **I wouldn't go that far** and adds that **Close friends may be more eager to help**._

questionText: According to the lecturer, how do salmon find their way back?

options.label: They depend on one sense far out at sea and on another near home
They use smell to cross the ocean and the magnetic field near the coast
They follow familiar landmarks along the coast until they reach their stream
They are guided mostly by the warmth of the water in their home stream

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **one for each stage of the trip** (חוש אחד לכל שלב במסע) והמשפט **they switch to smell** (הדגים עוברים לחוש הריח), הסלמון נעזר בשדה המגנטי בים הפתוח ובריח ליד נחל הבית.

_The fish uses **two different senses, one for each stage of the trip**: the magnetic field at sea, and then **they switch to smell**._

questionText: What did the experiment with blocked noses show?

options.label: Salmon can reach their own stream by the magnetic field without smell
Salmon that could still smell picked streams almost at random
Salmon rely on smell to pick out their own stream near the end
Salmon learn the smell of their home stream while living out at sea

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **Those fish chose streams almost at random** (הדגים שאפם נחסם בחרו נחלים כמעט באקראי), בלי חוש הריח הסלמון מתקשה למצוא את נחל הבית, ולכן הריח נחוץ לבחירת הנחל בסוף המסע.

_Fish with blocked noses **chose streams almost at random**, while those that **could still smell mostly returned home**._

questionText: What is the woman's concern about the usual explanation?

options.label: Traffic noise may be too high-pitched for higher songs to stand out
The city birds might belong to a different species from the forest birds
Singing more loudly may in fact lower the pitch of a song
The birds' louder singing might itself be pushing the pitch up

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **When birds sing louder, their songs naturally rise in pitch** (כשציפורים שרות חזק יותר, הצליל של שירתן עולה מעצמו), ייתכן שהצליל הגבוה בעיר נובע רק מכך שהציפורים שרות חזק יותר.

_She notes that **When birds sing louder, their songs naturally rise in pitch**, so the change may be **a side effect of shouting**._

questionText: What do the researchers decide they need to do next?

options.label: Check how loud the songs are in addition to their pitch
Drop the pitch data and measure the songs' loudness instead
Record the same species in several more forests for comparison
Find out whether higher songs help the city birds attract mates

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **We'd have to measure loudness as well as pitch** (נצטרך למדוד את עוצמת הקול וגם את גובה הצליל), החוקרים צריכים למדוד את עוצמת השירה ולא רק את גובה הצליל שלה.

_She says **We'd have to measure loudness as well as pitch**, and he agrees that **it's worth doing**._

questionText: Suppose a skeleton's bones match the local trace but its teeth do not. What would this suggest?

options.label: The person grew up in the area but spent later years elsewhere
The person moved to the area at some point after childhood
The person left the area as a child and did not come back
The person's teeth changed after they arrived in the area

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **tooth enamel forms in childhood and never changes afterward** (אמייל השן נוצר בילדות ואינו משתנה אחר כך) והמשפט **it reflects recent years** (העצם משקפת את השנים האחרונות), האדם הגיע לאזור אחרי ילדותו.

_Enamel **forms in childhood and never changes afterward**, while bone **reflects recent years**, so the person arrived after childhood._

questionText: Which of the following fits the lecturer's explanation?

options.label: Seldom-used words tend to hold on to their full length
Rarely heard words get cut down more often than common ones
Short words tend to fall out of use faster than long ones
Common words grow longer as speakers add detail to them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **spend it where a word is rare** (משקיעים את המאמץ במילים נדירות), מילים שמשתמשים בהן לעיתים רחוקות נוטות לשמור על אורכן המלא.

_Speakers save effort on frequent words and **spend it where a word is rare**, so seldom-used words keep their full length._

questionText: According to the man, what chiefly makes ice slippery?

options.label: Water melted by the weight of the people walking on it
A glassy surface too smooth for shoes to grip
Heat from friction, which melts the ice as feet slide over it
A thin wet coating present even when nobody is on the ice

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **ice seems to carry a watery layer of its own, even before anyone steps on it** (נראה שלקרח יש שכבה מימית משלו, עוד לפני שמישהו דורך עליו), הקרח חלקלק בעיקר בגלל ציפוי רטוב שקיים עליו גם כשאיש אינו דורך עליו.

_He says **ice seems to carry a watery layer of its own, even before anyone steps on it**, while friction adds only **a little**._

questionText: Compared with the well at Syene, what did the shadow in Alexandria show?

options.label: The sun was nearer to Alexandria than to Syene
The sun was overhead at Syene but not at Alexandria
The sun's rays were spreading apart over long distances
The sun's light was bent by the air above Alexandria

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **the sun shone straight down a deep well in Syene** (בסיינה השמש האירה ישר לתוך באר עמוקה) והמשפט **a tall column did cast a short shadow** (באלכסנדריה עמוד גבוה הטיל צל קצר), השמש עמדה ישר מעל סיינה בלבד.

_In Syene **the sun shone straight down a deep well**, but in Alexandria **a tall column did cast a short shadow**, so only Syene had the sun overhead._

questionText: What is the lecturer's view of the estimate?

options.label: It came remarkably close, and that is why it is admired
It was too large, since his unit of distance was too long
Its logic was weak, though the figure turned out to be right
Its accuracy is unclear, but its logic is impressive

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **we can't say** (איננו יכולים לומר) והמשפט **What makes the work remarkable is the reasoning, not the final number** (מה שמרשים בעבודה הוא דרך החשיבה ולא המספר הסופי), הדיוק לא ידוע אך ההיגיון מרשים.

_Asked how close he got, the lecturer says **we can't say**, and adds that **What makes the work remarkable is the reasoning, not the final number**._

questionText: What makes the student doubt the idea?

options.label: Signs of habitual fire use come long after the body changed
Brain growth began long after people had learned to cook
The brain uses too little energy for diet to affect its growth
Cooked meals supply the body with less energy than raw food does

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **Brains and teeth changed nearly two million years ago** (המוח והשיניים השתנו לפני כמעט שני מיליון שנה) והצירוף **show up much later** (מופיעים הרבה יותר מאוחר), עדויות האש מאוחרות בהרבה מהשינוי בגוף.

_She notes that **Brains and teeth changed nearly two million years ago**, while signs of regular fire **show up much later**._

questionText: Which statement best sums up the professor's final position?

options.label: The idea has been ruled out by the lack of early fire traces
The idea is supported by the fact that ash rarely survives
The idea is believable, but it still lacks firm confirmation
The idea explains the smaller gut but not the bigger brain

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **that isn't support, either** (גם זו אינה תמיכה) והמשפט **the idea is plausible, not proven** (הרעיון סביר אך לא הוכח), הפרופסור רואה ברעיון אפשרות סבירה שעדיין לא אוששה.

_He says the preservation argument **isn't support, either**, and ends with **the idea is plausible, not proven**._

questionText: What happened to the early reports about trees, according to the lecturer?

options.label: Welcomed at first, the claim later failed in more careful tests
Doubted at first, the claim was finally shown to involve real talking
Ignored at first, the claim came back through studies of wasps
Dismissed at first, the claim has since gained experimental support

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **It sounded like wishful thinking** (זה נשמע כמו משאלת לב) והמשפט **careful experiments have shown** (ניסויים קפדניים הראו), הטענה נדחתה בתחילה אך מאז קיבלה תמיכה ניסויית.

_At first **It sounded like wishful thinking**, but **Since then, though, careful experiments have shown** that undamaged plants do prepare._

questionText: Why is the lecturer cautious about calling this communication?

options.label: The signal may have arisen to alert other parts of the same plant
The chemicals may be too weak to travel as far as nearby plants
The proof that neighbors respond rests on a few small, early studies
Plants that pick up the signal seldom change their own defenses in response

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **the signal evolved to reach the plant's own distant leaves** (האיתות הכימי התפתח כדי להגיע לעלים הרחוקים של הצמח עצמו), השכנים כנראה רק קולטים איתות שנועד לצמח עצמו.

_She suggests that **the signal evolved to reach the plant's own distant leaves**, so **The neighbors ... may simply be listening in**._

questionText: How does the man explain the result for the one-dollar group?

options.label: They felt uneasy about lying and changed their view to ease it
They wanted to please the researcher who had paid them so little
They judged their feelings by noticing what they had just said
They were paid too little to care about describing it honestly

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **the participants simply judged themselves the same way, by looking at what they'd just done** (המשתתפים שפטו את עצמם כמו צופה מהצד, לפי מה שעשו זה עתה), הם הסיקו מה הם מרגישים ממה שאמרו.

_He suggests that **the participants simply judged themselves the same way, by looking at what they'd just done**, as an onlooker would._

questionText: What conclusion does the woman reach at the end?

options.label: The discomfort account has now been shown to be mistaken
The experiment establishes the effect but not its cause
Larger payments do more to change what people come to believe
The observer account works better than the usual one in most cases

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **the study shows that small rewards can shift attitudes, but not, by itself, why** (המחקר מראה שתגמול קטן יכול לשנות עמדות, אך לא מדוע), הניסוי מוכיח את התופעה אך לא את הסיבה לה.

_She concludes that **the study shows that small rewards can shift attitudes, but not, by itself, why**._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what pattern in a set of figures might make an auditor suspicious?

options.label: Leading digits that are ones in close to a third of cases
Leading digits that occur with nearly identical frequency
Leading digits that become steadily rarer from one to nine
Final digits that are spread fairly evenly from zero to nine

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט **people who concoct figures tend to spread those first digits far too evenly** (אנשים שממציאים נתונים נוטים לפזר את הספרות הראשונות באופן שווה מדי), ספרות פותחות בשכיחות כמעט זהה מעוררות חשד.

_Real data favor ones, but **people who concoct figures tend to spread those first digits far too evenly**._

questionText: What is the passage mainly about?

options.label: Why burrs hold on so tightly to the fur of animals
How engineers have copied many different ideas from plants and animals
How a plant's seed cases led to a useful invention
Why the makers of clothing did not want to use nylon at first

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקאות עוברות מהצירוף **covered with burrs**, דרך הרצועות, אל הצירוף **Today it is used on bags**, ולכן הקטע עוסק בתרמילי זרעים של צמח שהובילו להמצאה שימושית (הצירוף **led to a useful invention**).

_The passage moves from **covered with burrs** to the strips and **Today it is used on bags**, so it shows how a plant's seed cases led to a useful invention._

questionText: According to paragraph 1, how do the hooks help the plant?

options.label: They let animals take its seeds to new places.
They keep its seeds close to the parent plant.
They help its seeds take in water from the rain.
They stop birds from finding its seeds.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **animals carry the burrs far away before they fall off, so the seeds can grow in new places**, בעלי חיים לוקחים את הזרעים למקומות חדשים (הצירוף **new places**).

_Paragraph 1 says **animals carry the burrs far away before they fall off, so the seeds can grow in new places**._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, what was the problem with the first strips?

options.label: Their two parts were too hard to pull apart.
Their loops were too small for the hooks to catch.
Their nylon hooks were too soft to hold.
Their hooks soon became too weak to hold.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the cotton hooks soon became soft and weak**, הווים של הרצועות הראשונות נחלשו מהר, ולכן הם היו חלשים מדי כדי להחזיק (הצירוף **too weak to hold**).

_Paragraph 2 says **His first strips were made of cotton, and the cotton hooks soon became soft and weak**._

questionText: In paragraph 2, the word "sturdier" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הנקודתיים בא הסבר, הצירוף **could be opened and closed thousands of times, and the hooks still held**, ולכן המילה **sturdier** פירושה חזק ועמיד יותר (הצירוף **harder to damage**).

_After the colon, **could be opened and closed thousands of times, and the hooks still held** shows that **sturdier** means harder to damage._

questionText: Why does the writer mention astronauts in paragraph 3?

options.label: To show that the fastener was first made for use in space
To explain how the fastener came to be widely used
To explain why clothing makers thought it looked cheap
To explain why the engineer chose nylon over cotton

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האסטרונאוטים באים בין הצירוף **few companies wanted the new fastener** לבין הצירוף **Today it is used on bags**, ולכן הם מסבירים איך ההמצאה הגיעה לשימוש רחב (הצירוף **widely used**).

_The astronauts come between **few companies wanted the new fastener** and **Today it is used on bags**, so they explain how it came to be widely used._

questionText: What is the passage mainly about?

options.label: How crystals in a chameleon's skin reflect light
How and why chameleons really change color
Why chameleons change color to match what they sit on
How different animals use color to send messages

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 1 דוחה רעיון נפוץ בצירוף **it is mostly wrong**, פסקה 2 מסבירה איך הצבע משתנה ופסקה 3 למה, ולכן הקטע עוסק באופן ובסיבה האמיתיים לשינוי הצבע (הצירוף **How and why chameleons really change color**).

_Paragraph 1 calls the popular idea **mostly wrong**, and paragraphs 2 and 3 explain how and why chameleons really change color._

questionText: According to paragraph 1, why do chameleons not need to change color in order to hide?

options.label: They spend most of the day hidden under leaves.
Their skin changes color too slowly to help them hide in time.
Few other animals hunt them in the trees.
Their usual colors already help them hide among plants.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **usual green or brown colors already help it hide among leaves and branches**, הצבעים הרגילים של הזיקית כבר עוזרים לה להסתתר (הצירוף **already help them hide**).

_Paragraph 1 says **usual green or brown colors already help it hide among leaves and branches, so it does not need to change them**._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why does a calm chameleon look green?

options.label: Its crystals move apart and reflect yellow and red light.
Its skin takes in the green color of the leaves around it.
Blue light from its crystals mixes with yellow.
A green top layer of skin hides its other colors.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **This blue mixes with a yellow color in the skin, so the chameleon looks green**, האור הכחול מהגבישים מתערבב עם צבע צהוב (הצירוף **mixes with a yellow color**).

_Paragraph 2 says the calm crystals **reflect blue light**, and **This blue mixes with a yellow color in the skin, so the chameleon looks green**._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "it" in "it is giving up" refers to

options.label: the fight between the two males
the male that does not win

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **it** מתייחסת לנושא של המשפט, הצירוף **The other male**, כלומר לזכר שלא מנצח (הצירוף **the male that does not win**), כי הוא זה שנעשה כהה ומוותר.

_The subject of the sentence is **The other male**, the one that does not win, so **it** refers to that male._

questionText: What can be inferred about a chameleon that suddenly turns bright yellow and red?

options.label: It is probably reacting to another chameleon.
It is probably trying to match a bright flower.
Its crystals have probably moved closer together.
It probably wants to warm its body in the cool morning.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **When two males meet, each may turn bright**, צבע בהיר מופיע במפגש בין זיקיות, ולכן זיקית שנעשית בהירה כנראה מגיבה לזיקית אחרת (הצירוף **reacting to another chameleon**).

_Bright colors come when the animal is **excited**, and **When two males meet, each may turn bright**, so it is probably reacting to another chameleon._

questionText: What is the passage mainly about?

options.label: Why we count time in sixties rather than in tens
How people in ancient Mesopotamia did their counting
How people have measured time throughout history
Why France decided to keep the meter but not decimal time

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקאות עוברות מהצירוף **Time is different**, דרך מקור השיטה וניסיון לשנות אותה, אל הצירוף **time stayed in sixties**, ולכן הקטע מסביר למה סופרים זמן בשישים ולא בעשרות (הצירוף **in sixties rather than in tens**).

_The passage moves from **Time is different** to **time stayed in sixties**, so it explains why we count time in sixties rather than in tens._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why may people in Mesopotamia have counted in sixties?

options.label: Sixty was the number of minutes in their hour.
Ten can be divided by more numbers than sixty can.
Sixty can be divided into many equal parts.
Large numbers were hard to write in groups of ten.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **One possible reason is that sixty is easy to share**, ולפי רשימת המספרים שאחריו, אפשר לחלק את שישים לחלקים שווים רבים (הצירוף **many equal parts**).

_Paragraph 2 says **One possible reason is that sixty is easy to share**, and it lists the many numbers that divide it._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, which of the following is true about the word "minute"?

options.label: It was first used by the people of ancient Mesopotamia.
It was taken from Latin words for a small part.
It was chosen because clocks had sixty marks.
It once meant a part of a second.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **The word "minute" comes from a Latin phrase that means "small part,"**, מקור המילה הוא צירוף לטיני שפירושו חלק קטן (הצירוף **a small part**).

_Paragraph 3 says **The word "minute" comes from a Latin phrase that means "small part,"**._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "discarded" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **most people did not want to change their habits** והצירוף **time stayed in sixties**, התוכנית לא נשארה, ולכן המילה **discarded** פירושה שוויתרו עליה (הצירוף **given up**).

_**most people did not want to change their habits**, and **time stayed in sixties**, so **discarded** means given up._

questionText: What can be inferred from paragraph 4?

options.label: Decimal time may have failed because its clocks were hard to make.
A new system can succeed if special clocks are made for it.
A system that people use every day can be hard to replace.
Most people in France found it hard to count in tens.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התוכנית ננטשה כי רוב האנשים לא רצו לשנות את ההרגלים שלהם (**most people did not want to change their habits**), ומכאן שקשה להחליף שיטה שאנשים משתמשים בה כל יום (**can be hard to replace**).

_The plan failed because **most people did not want to change their habits**, so a system used every day can be hard to replace._

questionText: What is the passage mainly about?

options.label: Why signs and fences often fail to keep walkers off the grass
How cities decide where to build new roads and parks
Why walkers should stay on the paths that planners build
How walkers' shortcuts form and how planners deal with them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקאות עוברות מהצירוף **grows in stages** אל הצירוף **saw these paths as a problem** ואל הצירוף **the opposite approach**, ולכן הקטע עוסק בהיווצרות קיצורי הדרך ובתגובת המתכננים (הצירוף **deal with them**).

_The paragraphs go from **grows in stages** to **saw these paths as a problem** and **the opposite approach**: how shortcuts form and how planners respond._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, why do later walkers tend to use a path that has just begun to form?

options.label: The grass along it has already worn away.
A line that stands out is simpler to walk along.
Signs near the lawn point them toward the new shortcut.
The paved path nearby has been closed for repairs.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **Because a visible line is easier to follow than open grass**, קו בולט קל יותר ללכת בעקבותיו (הצירוף **a line that stands out**), ולכן ההולכים הבאים משתמשים בו.

_Paragraph 2 says **Because a visible line is easier to follow than open grass, the next walkers tend to use it too**._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, what often happens when bushes are planted in a desire path?

options.label: People walk around them, and a new path forms close by.
Walkers return to the paved path after a short time.
The bushes are pulled out by walkers who need the path.
Planners add signs to explain why the bushes are there.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **step around the bushes, and before long a new path appears close by**, אנשים עוקפים את השיחים ושביל חדש נוצר בקרבת מקום (הצירוף **a new path forms close by**).

_Paragraph 3 says walkers **step around the bushes, and before long a new path appears close by**._

questionText: In paragraph 2, the word "inviting" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the next walkers tend to use it too**, כל הולך גורם לשביל למשוך עוד הולכים, ולכן המילה **inviting** פירושה מושך, מפתה (הצירוף **tempting to use**).

_Each walker makes the next one more likely to use the path (**the next walkers tend to use it too**), so **inviting** means tempting to use._

questionText: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about the designers who wait before paving paths?

options.label: They want lawns to stay free of paths for good.
They believe walkers' choices show where paths are needed.
They care more about neat designs than about walkers.
They have found that bushes keep walkers off better than fences do.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **paved where walkers had worn them down**, המעצבים סוללים שבילים במקום שבו ההולכים בחרו ללכת, ולכן הם מאמינים שבחירת ההולכים מראה איפה צריך שבילים (הצירוף **show where paths are needed**).

_They pave the paths **where walkers had worn them down**, so they must believe walkers' choices show where paths are needed._

questionText: Which of the following best describes the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Doctors once checked whether a patient's nerves were working by placing the patient's hands in warm water.
Finger wrinkles form because the skin takes in water, and they probably help people grip wet objects.
Finger wrinkles are produced by the body rather than by water alone, but their purpose is still uncertain.
Wrinkled fingers are a warning sign of nerve damage and should be checked by a doctor as soon as possible.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפטי הנושא עוברים מההסבר הישן אל הצירוף **the body itself produces the wrinkles** ואל הצירוף **the question is still open**, ולכן: הגוף יוצר את הקמטים, אבל מטרתם עדיין לא ברורה (**their purpose is still uncertain**).

_The passage moves from **the body itself produces the wrinkles** to **the question is still open**: the body makes the folds, but their purpose is still uncertain._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, what shows that water alone does not cause the wrinkles?

options.label: A finger whose nerves are damaged stays smooth in water.
Damaged nerves make the skin fold more quickly in water.
Doctors found that the outer layer of skin does not take in water.
Some doctors used warm water to damage the nerves in a finger.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **when the nerves in a finger are damaged, the finger does not wrinkle**, אצבע שהעצבים שלה פגועים נשארת חלקה (המילה **smooth**), ולכן המים לבדם לא יוצרים את הקמטים.

_Paragraph 2 says that **when the nerves in a finger are damaged, the finger does not wrinkle**, so water alone is not the cause._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, what happens when the nerves send their signal?

options.label: The fingertip swells as it fills with water.
The fingertip becomes warmer, and its color grows darker than usual.
The nerves in the fingertip stop working for a short time.
The fingertip becomes smaller, and its skin is pulled into folds.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the fingertip loses some of its volume**, קצה האצבע נעשה קטן יותר, ולפי הצירוף **pulled down into folds** העור שמעליו נמשך לקפלים (הצירוף **becomes smaller**, נעשה קטן יותר).

_After the signal, **the fingertip loses some of its volume, and the skin on top is pulled down into folds**._

questionText: In paragraph 3, the word "constrict" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בעקבות האות קצה האצבע מאבד נפח, לפי הצירוף **loses some of its volume**, ונעשה חיוור יותר, ולכן המילה **constrict** פירושה להתכווץ, להיעשות צר יותר (הצירוף **become narrower**).

_When the vessels **constrict**, the fingertip **loses some of its volume** and looks **paler**, so **constrict** means **become narrower**._

questionText: Why does the writer mention a car tire in paragraph 4?

options.label: To show that the folds on fingers and on tires might form in the same way
To explain why later studies did not find the same effect as the first experiment
To compare how well wet fingers and dry fingers hold small objects
To illustrate one suggested reason why the body might produce finger wrinkles

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצמיג מובא כדי להסביר את הרעיון שבצירוף **One popular idea is that the folds work like the patterns on a car tire**, כלומר כדי להמחיש סיבה אפשרית לקמטים (המילה **illustrate**, להמחיש).

_The tire explains **One popular idea**: the folds may **carry water away** like tire patterns, a possible reason for the wrinkles._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To describe the musical features that make some songs easier to remember than others
To explain what earworms are, what causes them and how people can stop them
To compare the different ways in which music affects people's moods and memories
To warn readers that listening to pop songs and advertisements can harm their memory

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע עובר מהתופעה (**Such tunes are known as earworms**), דרך הגורמים, אל השאלה **How can people get rid of an earworm?**, ולכן מטרתו להסביר מה הן תולעי אוזן, מה גורם להן ואיך להפסיק אותן (**how people can stop them**).

_It defines earworms, gives their causes and asks **How can people get rid of an earworm?**: what they are, their causes, how to stop them._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, when do earworms tend to appear?

options.label: When people are in a busy place, such as a crowded market or station
When people are working on a difficult task
When people see a face that they do not know
When people are doing something that needs little attention

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **when the mind is not busy**, והדוגמאות **walking, showering or doing housework**, תולעי אוזן מופיעות כשעושים דבר שדורש מעט תשומת לב (**needs little attention**).

_Paragraph 2 says earworms appear **when the mind is not busy**, as in **walking, showering or doing housework**: activities that need little attention._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, what is typical of songs that become earworms?

options.label: They are easy to sing but include a few unexpected notes.
They have a slow and steady beat that is easy to remember.
They are long songs that contain many different musical parts.
They are usually songs that people do not like.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **a simple melody that is easy to sing** והצירוף **one or two surprising notes**, השירים האלה קלים לשירה אבל כוללים כמה צלילים לא צפויים (**a few unexpected notes**).

_Such songs have **a simple melody that is easy to sing**, but they also **contain one or two surprising notes**._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "backfires" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **since the effort itself keeps the tune in mind**, המאמץ לא לחשוב על השיר דווקא משאיר אותו בראש, ולכן המילה **backfires** פירושה פועל הפוך מהכוונה (**has the opposite result**).

_The effort **keeps the tune in mind**, the opposite of what people want, so **backfires** means **has the opposite result**._

questionText: Based on paragraphs 2 and 4, why might a word puzzle help to stop an earworm?

options.label: It keeps the mind busy, which makes the song less likely to return.
It probably teaches people to forget songs they have heard many times.
It keeps the jaw moving in the same way that chewing gum does.
It lets people sing the song silently until it finally stops.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **when the mind is not busy** תולעי אוזן מופיעות כשהמוח פנוי, ולכן משימה כמו תשבץ (**a word puzzle**) עוזרת כי היא מעסיקה את המוח (**keeps the mind busy**).

_Earworms appear **when the mind is not busy**, so a task like **a word puzzle** helps because it keeps the mind busy._

questionText: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Early cameras were so slow that people could not hold a smile while their picture was taken.
Photography changed the way people in the 1800s thought about art, about family and about the future.
Advertisements for cheap cameras were the first to show people smiling at the camera.
The serious faces in old photographs had several causes, of which slow cameras were just one.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **it is not the whole story** ההסבר הפופולרי לא מספיק, והקטע מוסיף סיבות של מסורת ומחיר, ולכן: לפרצופים הרציניים היו כמה סיבות, ומצלמות איטיות היו רק אחת מהן (**just one**).

_The slow-camera answer **is not the whole story**; tradition and cost also mattered, so slow cameras were just one of several causes._

questionText: According to paragraph 2, what shows that slow cameras do not fully explain the serious faces?

options.label: Few people could hold a natural smile for many seconds.
Faces stayed unsmiling even after cameras had become much faster.
Early cameras could take a picture in a second or less.
Early photographs often showed people with wide, natural smiles on their faces.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **a photograph could be taken in a second or less, yet most people still did not smile**, הפרצופים נשארו בלי חיוך גם כשהמצלמות נעשו מהירות (**Faces stayed unsmiling**).

_**By the 1880s, a photograph could be taken in a second or less, yet most people still did not smile**._

questionText: According to paragraph 3, why did people want to look serious in their photographs?

options.label: Their cameras were too slow to record a natural smile.
They believed that a smile would probably make the photograph cost more.
They were paying a lot for what was often their only picture.
They were following new rules made by early photographers.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **a photograph was expensive** והצירוף **the only picture of themselves that they would ever have**, תמונה הייתה יקרה ולעתים קרובות התמונה היחידה של האדם (**their only picture**).

_**a photograph was expensive**, and for many it was **the only picture of themselves that they would ever have**, so they wanted to look serious._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "This" in "This began to change" refers to

options.label: the custom of looking serious in photographs
the high cost of painted portraits
the slow speed of early cameras
the use of advertisements to sell new cameras

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **This** מתייחסת למה שתואר עד כה, הרצון להיראות רציניים בצירוף **wanted to look serious**, וסוף הפסקה, הצירוף **the smile became the normal way**, מאשר זאת: המנהג להיראות רציני (**the custom of looking serious**).

_**This** points back to people who **wanted to look serious**; the paragraph ends with **the smile became the normal way to face the camera**._

questionText: What can be inferred from the passage about the spread of smiling in photographs?

options.label: It began as soon as cameras could take a picture in a second or less.
It depended more on how people valued photographs than on camera speed.
It was probably started by painters, who began to paint smiling faces.
It happened because photographs became more expensive than painted portraits.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** החיוך לא הופיע עם המצלמות המהירות (**yet most people still did not smile**) אלא כשתמונה כבר לא נראתה מיוחדת (**no longer seemed so special**), ולכן הוא תלוי ביחס לתמונות (**how people valued photographs**).

_Fast cameras did not bring smiles (**yet most people still did not smile**); smiles came when a photograph **no longer seemed so special**._

questionText: What is the purpose of the passage?

options.label: To explain how horseflies and other biting flies spread disease among the large animals they feed on
To argue that zebras' stripes help them hide from lions in tall grass and at dusk
To describe several explanations for the zebra's stripes and show which one the evidence now favors
To compare the various ways in which African animals protect themselves from their enemies

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקאות 2–4 מציגות שלושה הסברים, ולפי הצירוף **now has the most support** אחד מהם מועדף, ולכן המטרה היא לתאר כמה הסברים לפסים ולהראות איזה מהם מועדף כיום (**which one the evidence now favors**).

_Paragraphs 2-4 give three explanations, and the insect one **now has the most support**, so the purpose is to describe several explanations and show which the evidence favors._

questionText: Why has the idea that the stripes serve as camouflage lost much of its appeal?

options.label: Lions usually hunt when the light may be too dim for them to see the stripes.
Lions often hunt in bright daylight, when the stripes stand out clearly even from far away.
Zebras rarely spend time in tall grass or at the edges of woodlands.
Lions have been found to pick out single animals from running herds quite easily.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האריות צדים בעיקר בשעת בין ערביים ובלילה, לפי הצירוף **Lions hunt mainly at dusk and at night**, ואז הם כמעט לא רואים את הפסים, כי האור חלש מדי (**too dim**).

_**Lions hunt mainly at dusk and at night**, when **they can hardly see the stripes**, so the light is **too dim** for the stripes to matter._

questionText: Which of the following is stated about the idea that the stripes help to cool the zebra?

options.label: It depends on white stripes taking in more sunlight than black ones.
It is the explanation that now has the most support among researchers.
It was put forward after the explanation involving insects had been rejected.
