Tests of it have produced results that do not all agree.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **have produced mixed results**, הניסויים בחביות נתנו תוצאות מעורבות, כלומר תוצאות שאינן מתיישבות זו עם זו (**do not all agree**).

_The barrel tests **have produced mixed results**, that is, results that **do not all agree**._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "thwart" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הזבובים מתקרבים אבל נוחתים הרבה פחות, לפי הצירוף **landed on them far less often**, ולכן המילה **thwart** פירושה לסכל, למנוע (המילה **prevent**).

_Flies approached but **landed on them far less often**, so the stripes **thwart**, that is, **prevent**, a landing._

questionText: What can be inferred about zebras in places with few biting insects?

options.label: They probably rely on their stripes to stay cool more than zebras in other areas do.
They are more easily picked out of a running herd by hunting lions.
They probably have less bold stripes than zebras that live among many flies.
They tend to spend more of their time at the edges of woodlands.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the zebras with the boldest stripes tend to live where biting flies are most active**, היכן שיש מעט זבובים צפויים פסים פחות בולטים (**less bold stripes**).

_Since **the zebras with the boldest stripes tend to live where biting flies are most active**, zebras among few flies probably have **less bold stripes**._

questionText: What is the passage mostly about?

options.label: The reasons why older people find it harder than younger people to remember proper names
A common failure to find a familiar word, and some of the factors behind it
The many different ways in which human memory can let people down in everyday conversation
A simple method that people can use to recall forgotten words more quickly

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע נותן שם לתופעה (**a tip-of-the-tongue state**) ומונה גורמים שמגבירים אותה (**Several factors**), ולכן הוא עוסק בכישלון נפוץ למצוא מילה מוכרת ובכמה מהגורמים שמאחוריו (**some of the factors behind it**).

_The passage defines **a tip-of-the-tongue state** and its causes, so it is about a common failure to find a familiar word and the factors behind it._

questionText: According to the passage, what can people in a tip-of-the-tongue state often do?

options.label: Spell the word correctly even though they are unable to say it aloud
Explain where and when they first learned the missing word
Give a clear definition of the word but not its first letter
Say which letter the word starts with or roughly how long it is

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **can often report the first letter of the missing word, roughly how many syllables it has**, אפשר לומר באיזו אות המילה מתחילה (**the first letter**) ולנחש את אורכה.

_People **can often report the first letter of the missing word, roughly how many syllables it has**, so they can name the first letter or guess its length._

questionText: Why, according to the passage, are proper names a common source of these states?

options.label: A name usually has just one link to its owner, with no special logic.
Ordinary words usually have far fewer links to other words and ideas than names do.
Stress and tiredness affect names more strongly than they affect other words.
Names tend to be longer and harder to pronounce than most ordinary words.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **tied to its owner by a single, arbitrary link**, שם קשור לבעליו בקשר יחיד ושרירותי, כלומר בקשר אחד שאין מאחוריו היגיון מיוחד (**no special logic**).

_A name **is tied to its owner by a single, arbitrary link**, that is, one link with **no special logic**._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "impede" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המאמץ כמעט לא עוזר (הצירוף **trying harder seldom helps**), ומילה שגויה חוסמת את הנכונה, ולכן המילה **impede** פירושה לעכב, להפריע (המילה **delay**).

_Since **trying harder seldom helps** and a wrong word **can block the right one**, **impede** means **delay**._

questionText: What can be inferred about the missing word in a tip-of-the-tongue state?

options.label: It is probably still stored in memory, although it cannot be reached.
It is probably a word whose meaning the speaker has partly forgotten.
It is more likely to be recalled easily the next time it is needed.
It is usually a rare term that the speaker learned long ago and barely knows.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדובר בטוח שהוא מכיר את המילה, ולפי הצירוף **arrives on its own some time later** היא חוזרת מעצמה, ולכן היא כנראה עדיין שמורה בזיכרון (**still stored in memory**).

_The speaker is **sure of knowing it**, and the word **arrives on its own some time later**, so it is probably still **stored in memory**._

questionText: Which of the following best sums up the passage?

options.label: Loading cargo by hand was slow and costly, and goods were often damaged or stolen.
Many inventions of the last century changed the way in which goods are made and sold.
Old ports in narrow city centers gained most of the traffic once containers came into use.
A standard steel box made shipping far cheaper, though not quickly or for everyone.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 3 מראה הוזלה חדה, ופסקה 4 מוסיפה את הצירוף **neither quick nor painless**, ולכן: קופסה תקנית הוזילה מאוד את השילוח, אבל לא מהר ולא לטובת כולם (**not quickly or for everyone**).

_Paragraph 3 shows **handling costs fell sharply**, and paragraph 4 adds **neither quick nor painless**, so a standard box made shipping cheaper, but not quickly or for everyone._

questionText: What does the passage say about loading ships before containers were used?

options.label: It usually cost less than the voyage, although it took a long time.
Each item had to be carried and fitted into the ship's hold separately.
Dockworkers often packed the goods at the factory in order to save time.
Goods were rarely damaged, since workers handled them with great care.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **had to be lifted one by one into a ship's hold**, כל פריט הורם והותאם למקומו לבד, כלומר בנפרד (**separately**).

_Goods **had to be lifted one by one into a ship's hold** and fitted together, that is, each item **separately**._

questionText: According to the passage, why were companies able to make parts in one country and assemble them in another?

options.label: Ships began to travel much faster between distant countries than before.
Factories moved closer to the ports so that goods could be loaded onto ships directly.
Handling costs fell so much that sending goods overseas became very cheap.
Cranes allowed workers to open containers and check the goods in minutes.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **As handling costs fell sharply, shipping goods across an ocean became so cheap**, עלויות הטיפול ירדו עד כדי כך שהשילוח נעשה זול מאוד (**very cheap**).

_**As handling costs fell sharply, shipping goods across an ocean became so cheap** that parts could be made in one country and assembled in another._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "them" refers to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** נמלים שהיססו לבנות משהו איבדו את התנועה שלהם, ולפי הצירוף **the huge cranes and storage yards that containers required** מה שצריך לבנות הם המנופים ומגרשי האחסון (**cranes and storage yards**).

_Ports hesitated to build **the huge cranes and storage yards that containers required**, so **them** means cranes and storage yards._

questionText: What is the role of the last paragraph in the passage?

options.label: It explains how the shipping container was first invented, and by whom.
It gives further examples of the savings that were described in paragraph 3.
It describes how modern ports load and unload their ships so quickly.
It shows that the change came slowly and left some groups worse off.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפסקה נפתחת בצירוף **neither quick nor painless** ומתארת נמלים וסוורים שנפגעו, ולכן תפקידה להראות שהשינוי הגיע לאט והרע את מצבן של קבוצות מסוימות (**left some groups worse off**).

_The paragraph opens with **neither quick nor painless** and describes ports and dockworkers who lost out, so it shows the change was slow and left some groups worse off._

questionText: What is the purpose of the passage?

options.label: To explain how nets can collect water from fog, and what limits their use
To show how desert plants and animals manage to survive for years without rain
To compare the different ways in which dry regions obtain their drinking water
To argue that fog nets could end water shortages in most of the world's dry regions

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי תיאור השיטה מגיעה הסתייגות, הצירוף **is not an answer to drought everywhere**, ולכן המטרה היא להסביר איך רשתות אוספות מים מערפל ומה מגביל את השימוש בהן (**what limits their use**).

_Paragraphs 2-3 explain the method, and paragraph 4 says it **is not an answer to drought everywhere**, so the purpose is to explain how the nets work and their limits._

questionText: How does the water from the fog reach the storage tank?

options.label: A small electric pump draws the water out of the net and into a pipe.
The wind presses the droplets straight through the threads and into the tank.
Droplets gather on the threads until they are heavy enough to flow into a gutter.
The heat of the sun warms the droplets until they slide off the net into the tank.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **they become heavy enough to run down into a gutter**, הטיפות מצטברות על החוטים עד שהן כבדות מספיק כדי לזרום למרזב (**heavy enough to flow into a gutter**).

_When droplets join together, **they become heavy enough to run down into a gutter**, and from there they flow into the tank._

questionText: Which of the following is stated about the water that fog nets collect?

options.label: It is usually sold to towns that lie far away from the coast.
It can supply part of the water used by some small communities.
It is used mostly by factories rather than by people in their homes.
It costs more to collect than water that is delivered by truck.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **now receive at least part of their water from the fog**, יש קהילות שמקבלות מהערפל חלק מהמים שלהן (**part of the water**).

_**Some communities ... now receive at least part of their water from the fog**, so it supplies part of their water._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "clog" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האבק והאצות פוגעים ברשת וגורמים לכך שהיא אוספת פחות, לפי הצירוף **reduce the amount of water collected**, ולכן המילה **clog** פירושה לסתום (המילה **block**).

_Dust or algae **clog the mesh and reduce the amount of water collected**, so **clog** means **block**._

questionText: What can be inferred about a fog net set up in a sheltered valley where the air is usually still?

options.label: It would need more repairs than the nets that stand in windy places.
It would probably collect less water than a net on a windy coast.
It would collect more water, because its mesh would stay cleaner.
It would probably work well as long as the valley had thick fog.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **the wind pushes it steadily through the nets**, הרשת צריכה רוח, ולכן באוויר עומד היא תאסוף כנראה פחות מים (**collect less water**).

_The nets work where **the wind pushes it steadily through the nets**, so in still air a net would probably **collect less water**._

questionText: Which of the following best states the central point of the passage?

options.label: Recording equipment often makes voices sound thinner and higher than they really are.
People hear high tones better through the bones of the head than through the air.
Most people dislike their recorded voice because it is less pleasant than the voices of others.
Our recorded voice sounds strange to us because of how we hear and what we expect.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקאות 2–3 מסבירות שאנו שומעים את עצמנו בשתי דרכים (**in two ways at once**) ופסקה 4 מוסיפה את ההפתעה (**the surprise**), ולכן הקול המוקלט נשמע מוזר בגלל האופן שבו אנו שומעים ומה שאנו מצפים לשמוע (**what we expect**).

_Paragraphs 2-3 explain how we hear ourselves, and paragraph 4 adds **the surprise of hearing something unfamiliar**, so the voice sounds strange because of how we hear and what we expect._

questionText: Why, according to the passage, does our own voice sound deeper to us than to others?

options.label: Sound reaching the inner ear through the skull carries low tones well.
The ears of other people are less able than ours to pick up the low tones of a voice.
The air inside the head makes high tones sound much louder than low ones.
We usually speak in a deeper voice when we are alone than when others are listening.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **Bone tends to carry low tones better than high ones**, הצליל שמגיע לאוזן הפנימית דרך העצמות מעביר היטב צלילים נמוכים (**carries low tones well**).

_**Bone tends to carry low tones better than high ones**, so sound reaching the inner ear through bone **carries low tones well**._

questionText: What happens to the voice when it is recorded?

options.label: The equipment adds high tones that were not part of the original voice.
Its low tones are made louder so that it sounds clearer to listeners.
Only the part of the sound that moves through the air is captured.
The vibrations that pass through the bones of the head are recorded clearly.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הצירוף **A recording captures only the sound that travels through the air**, ההקלטה קולטת רק את החלק של הצליל שעובר באוויר (**moves through the air**).

_**A recording captures only the sound that travels through the air**, so the bone route is lost._

questionText: In paragraph 4, the word "harshly" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** מי שלא זיהו את הקול שלהם דירגו אותו לטובה (הצירוף **rate it quite favorably**), ולכן המילה **harshly** פירושה בחומרה, באופן ביקורתי (המילה **critically**).

_When they did not recognize their voice, people **tended to rate it quite favorably**, so judging it **harshly** means judging it **critically**._

questionText: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about people's dislike of their recorded voice?

options.label: It may depend more on knowing the voice is theirs than on its actual sound.
It usually disappears once they learn why recordings sound different from what they hear.
It is shared by most strangers who listen to the same recording of their voice.
It probably shows that their voice really does sound unpleasant to other people.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אנשים שהאזינו לקולם בלי לזהות אותו (הצירוף **without recognizing their own**) דירגו אותו לטובה, ולכן הדחייה תלויה כנראה בידיעה שזה הקול שלהם (**knowing the voice is theirs**).

_People who heard several voices **without recognizing their own** rated it **quite favorably**, so the dislike may depend on **knowing the voice is theirs**._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Several ways of limiting the influence of birth dates on selection have been suggested, with limited success so far.
Those born in the first months of the selection year are favored in youth sports, an advantage that usually stays with them well into their adult sporting careers.
Older children within an age group tend to be picked for top youth teams, an edge that says more about birth dates than about potential.
Children develop physically at different rates, and this affects how well they perform in many sports.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המבוגרים בקבוצה נבחרים יותר, אך לפי פסקה 4 הביצועים בגיל עשר הם מדד לא ודאי (**an uncertain guide**), ולכן: יתרון שמעיד יותר על תאריך הלידה מאשר על הפוטנציאל (**says more about birth dates than about potential**).

_Early-born children are **overrepresented on elite youth teams**, yet early form is **an uncertain guide**, so their edge says more about birth dates than about potential._

questionText: According to the passage, what happens to the children chosen for advanced squads?

options.label: They build real skill through the extra training and tougher matches they receive.
They learn to rely on technique and judgment because their rivals are bigger.
They are given less practice than the others so that they do not tire out too early.
They tend to leave the sport sooner than children born late in the year.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנבחרים מקבלים אימון טוב יותר, יריבים חזקים יותר ויותר תרגול (**better coaching, stronger opponents and more practice**), וכך היתרון הופך להבדל אמיתי במיומנות (**a genuine difference in skill**).

_Those selected **receive better coaching, stronger opponents and more practice**, so their early edge becomes **a genuine difference in skill**._

questionText: According to the passage, in which situation is the relative age effect likely to be most marked?

options.label: In sports that reward technique, once the players have become adults
In sports for young children, at about the age of nine or ten
In clubs that move their cutoff date each season, once players reach their twenties
In sports that favor size and strength, during the first years of adolescence

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 3 ההשפעה חזקה במיוחד בענפים שמתגמלים גודל וכוח (**sports that reward size and power**) ובשנות ההתבגרות המוקדמות (**the early teenage years**), ולכן התשובה היא ענפי גודל וכוח בתחילת גיל ההתבגרות.

_The effect is strongest **in sports that reward size and power and during the early teenage years**, when bodies differ most._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "attrition" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההצעה הראשונה בפסקה 4 נועדה להשאיר ילדים במשחק (**keep more late-born children in the game**), ולכן המילה **attrition** פירושה נשירה מהענף (**dropping out of the sport**).

_One remedy is **meant to keep more late-born children in the game**, so **attrition** here means dropping out of the sport._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that some of the late-born children who leave the sport early

options.label: usually leave because they prefer sports that reward technique
tend to be less talented than the children who are chosen for the top teams
might have done well as adults if they had stayed in it
are generally weaker in tactical judgment than early-born players

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** מי שנולדו מאוחר ושרדו מצליחים לעתים בצמרת (**long professional careers**), והביצועים בגיל עשר הם מדד לא ודאי (**an uncertain guide**), ולכן חלק מהנושרים היו עשויים להצליח (**might have done well**).

_Late-born survivors may enjoy **long professional careers**, and early form is **an uncertain guide**, so some who left might have done well._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Ants introduced into new regions often eat the food on seeds without carrying the seeds away.
Many plants pay ants in food to move their seeds to favorable spots, a deal that depends on which ants are present.
Ants spread the seeds of many plants over long distances, which in turn keeps the young plants from having to compete with their parents.
Plants have developed a number of different ways of spreading their seeds, relying on wind, birds and insects.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצמח משלם לנמלה במזון (**paid the ant to sow its seed**), התועלת היא במקום שהזרע מגיע אליו (**where it ends up**) ויש נקודת תורפה, ולכן: עסקה שתלויה בנמלים שבסביבה (**depends on which ants are present**).

_The plant has **paid the ant to sow its seed**, the gain lies in **where it ends up**, and the deal depends on which ants are present._

questionText: According to the passage, what happens to a seed once an ant has carried it to the nest?

options.label: It stays in a storeroom until the young ants are old enough to eat it.
It gets broken open so that the colony can feed on the nutrients inside.
It is often eaten by mice that visit the nest in search of food.
It loses its fatty part to the young but is otherwise left undamaged.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התוספת מוסרת ומוגשת לצעירים (**removed and fed to the young**), והזרע קשה מדי לאכילה ולכן נשאר שלם (**left whole**), כלומר הוא מאבד רק את החלק השומני.

_The attachment is **removed and fed to the young**, and the seed, **too difficult to eat**, is **left whole**._

questionText: According to the passage, which of the following has been proposed as a benefit for plants whose seeds are taken by ants?

options.label: Their seeds may be spared the heat of fires by lying under the soil.
Their seeds may be carried farther than the wind would take them.
Their seeds may be guarded by native ants against the newcomers.
Their seeds may be moved on by birds that search the ants' refuse heaps.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בפסקה 3 נאמר שבמקומות שיש בהם שריפות רבות זרע קבור מוגן מהחום (**a buried seed is shielded from the heat**), ולכן אחת התועלות היא שהזרע ניצל מחום השריפה כשהוא מתחת לאדמה.

_Paragraph 3 says that **where fires are frequent, a buried seed is shielded from the heat**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "exclude" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף **need not exclude one another** הכותב מונה שלוש תשובות שיכולות להיות נכונות יחד, ולכן המילה **exclude** כאן פירושה לשלול (**rule out**).

_After **they need not exclude one another**, three answers are listed that can all be true at once, so **exclude** means rule out._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that seeds left on the surface by the introduced ants

options.label: are more likely to be eaten than seeds taken into a nest
usually sprout sooner because they are exposed to light
end up farther from the parent than seeds moved by native ants
probably lose their hard coats once the attachment has been eaten

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** זרעים מתחת לקרקע מוסתרים מעכברים ומציפורים (**hidden from mice and birds**), ולכן זרעים שנשארו על פני הקרקע חשופים יותר לאכילה (**more likely to be eaten**).

_**Seeds taken below ground are hidden from mice and birds**, so seeds left on the surface are more likely to be eaten._

questionText: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: To explain how operators used telescopes and codebooks to pass signals from tower to tower
To argue that the optical telegraph failed because its codes were too hard for operators to learn
To trace the history of long-distance communication from riders on horseback to modern wires
To describe how a chain of signal towers carried messages, and why a newer system replaced it

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקטע מתאר שרשרת מגדלים (**a chain of towers**), את חולשותיה ואת יתרונות החוט החשמלי, ולכן: לתאר איך המגדלים העבירו הודעות ולמה מערכת חדשה החליפה אותם (**why a newer system replaced it**).

_The passage describes **a chain of towers**, its **weaknesses**, and the electric system's **real advantages**: how the towers worked and why a newer system replaced them._

questionText: According to the passage, why could a message travel so quickly along the line?

options.label: Codebooks let operators send several messages along the line at once.
Signals were passed on by sight, so nothing had to be carried.
Operators worked in shifts, so the line could run day and night.
Messages were sent beside the railways by trained operators.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט **Because nothing physical had to travel** (כי שום דבר מוחשי לא היה צריך לעבור את הדרך) מסביר את המהירות: האותות עברו במבט, ולא היה צריך לשאת דבר (**nothing had to be carried**).

_The clue is **Because nothing physical had to travel**: signals were passed on by sight, so nothing had to be carried._

questionText: According to the passage, which of the following was one of the real advantages of the electric telegraph?

options.label: It used codebooks in which one sign could stand for a phrase.
It was faster, and this was the chief reason it took the towers' place.
It went on working after dark and whatever the weather was like.
It needed more workers along the line, so mistakes were caught sooner.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 4 היתרונות האמיתיים לא היו המהירות (**its real advantages lay elsewhere**), אלא למשל שהחוט פעל בלילה ובכל מזג אוויר (**worked at night and in any weather**).

_Speed was not the point: **its real advantages lay elsewhere**, for **a wire worked at night and in any weather**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "garble" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** העתקה רשלנית (**a single careless copy**) יוצרת טעות שעוברת הלאה (**where the mistake was made**), ולכן המילה **garble** פירושה לשבש, לערבל (**scramble**).

_**a single careless copy** creates a mistake that is passed on, so **garble** means scramble._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that, other things being equal, an optical telegraph line probably carried fewer messages

options.label: on clear days than on foggy or rainy ones
for government offices than for private citizens
after codebooks came into use than before
in the winter months than in the summer months

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הקו פעל רק באור יום (**It worked only in daylight**), והימים בחורף קצרים יותר, ולכן בחודשי החורף עברו פחות הודעות (**in the winter months**).

_The line **worked only in daylight**, and winter days are shorter, so it probably carried fewer messages in the winter months._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Blind tests suggest that famous old violins may sound no better than fine new ones, though the tests have their critics.
Several explanations, from varnish to dense wood, have been offered for the tone of old Italian violins.
Blind tests have shown that new violins sound better than the old ones, a result that even the defenders of the old instruments now accept.
In many fields, experts' judgments of quality often depend more on expectations than on the objects themselves.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בבדיקות עיוורות הנגנים לא הבחינו בעקביות בין ישן לחדש (**could not reliably tell**), אך יש טענות נגד (**trenchant objections**), ולכן: ייתכן שהישנים אינם עדיפים, אף שלבדיקות יש מבקרים (**the tests have their critics**).

_In blind tests players **could not reliably tell** old from new, yet defenders raised **trenchant objections**: old violins may sound no better, though the tests have critics._

questionText: What did the experiments with soloists find?

options.label: Most players preferred the old violins once they had played them for an hour.
Players needed several weeks to tell the old violins from the new ones.
Players could not dependably pick out which of the violins were the old ones.
Players could tell old from new by the feel of the instrument, but not by its sound.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 2 רוב הנגנים לא הצליחו להבחין באופן עקבי בין הישנים לחדשים (**could not reliably tell the old instruments from the new ones**), כלומר לא זיהו בעקביות את הישנים.

_Most soloists **could not reliably tell the old instruments from the new ones**, so they could not dependably pick out the old violins._

questionText: According to the passage, which of the following is one objection raised by defenders of the old violins?

options.label: The soloists chosen for the tests may have lacked experience with violins.
The tests may not have included the very best of the famous violins.
The audiences had been told beforehand which violin was which.
The tests went on for weeks, which left the players too tired to judge.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בפסקה 4 המגינים טוענים שהכינורות הישנים שעמדו לרשות הבודקים אולי לא היו המשובחים ביותר (**may not have been the finest examples**), כלומר ייתכן שבבדיקות לא נוגנו הכלים הטובים ביותר.

_Defenders argue that **the old violins available may not have been the finest examples**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "project" is closest in meaning to

options.label: sound sweet to the player's ear

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההסבר שבא אחריה, הצירוף **must be heard over a full orchestra in a large hall**, מראה שהמילה **project** כאן פירושה להגיע היטב למאזינים רחוקים (**carry well to distant listeners**).

_The phrase **must be heard over a full orchestra in a large hall** shows that **project** means carry well to distant listeners._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that the high prices paid for the old violins

options.label: are likely to fall now that the blind tests have been published
may owe something to reputation rather than to sound alone
show that buyers can hear differences that experts miss
probably reflect the cost of the rare wood used to make them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי הקטע חלק מהתהילה של הכינורות נמצא אצל המאזין (**may lie in the listener rather than in the wood**), ולכן המחיר הגבוה נובע אולי גם מהמוניטין ולא רק מהצליל (**owe something to reputation**).

_Part of their fame **may lie in the listener rather than in the wood**, so their high prices may owe something to reputation, not sound alone._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Cooks can tell when a pan is ready for searing meat by flicking water onto it and watching whether the drops skate.
A very hot surface can make a drop last longer by holding it up on vapor, which helps in some tasks and hinders others.
Water lasts longer on a hotter pan because the steam it gives off cools the metal to below the point at which water boils.
Liquids tend to behave in unexpected ways when they are heated, and scientists are still trying to explain why.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 2 מסבירה שכרית אדים (**a thin cushion**) מגינה על הטיפה ופסקה 4 מוסיפה תועלת ונזק, ולכן התשובה: משטח לוהט מאריך את חיי הטיפה בעזרת אדים, וזה מועיל או מזיק (**helps in some tasks and hinders others**).

_A **thin cushion** of vapor keeps drops alive on a very hot pan, and paragraph 4 adds that this helps cooks but is **the bane of metalworkers**._

questionText: According to the passage, why does a drop on a very hot pan take so long to disappear?

options.label: Its shiny surface sends back most of the heat that rises from the metal below.
It keeps sliding, so it rarely stays in one spot long enough to heat up.
Most of the water turns to vapor the moment the drop first lands.
A layer of vapor lets little of the metal's heat get through to the drop.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 2 האדים מעבירים חום גרוע הרבה יותר ממגע עם המתכת (הצירוף **vapor carries heat far less well**), ולכן שכבת האדים מעבירה לטיפה מעט חום (**lets little of the metal's heat get through**).

_The drop is shielded because **vapor carries heat far less well than direct contact with metal would**._

questionText: According to the passage, why do spilled drops of liquid nitrogen roll across a kitchen floor instead of spreading?

options.label: The tiles are far warmer than the point at which nitrogen boils.
The tiles are too smooth for the drops to spread out on them.
The nitrogen freezes the moment it touches the cold tiles.
Nitrogen needs a higher temperature than water does in order to boil.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** החנקן רותח בטמפרטורה של כמינוס 196 מעלות, ולכן אפילו רצפה רגילה לוהטת בשבילו (**even an ordinary kitchen floor is extremely hot**), כלומר האריחים חמים בהרבה מנקודת הרתיחה שלו.

_Nitrogen **boils at about minus 196 degrees Celsius**, so **even an ordinary kitchen floor is extremely hot** for it._

questionText: As used in the passage, the phrase "as such" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **as such** בא בתוך ניגוד: לא הטמפרטורה של המשטח עצמה אלא בכמה היא עולה על נקודת הרתיחה (הצירוף **how far it exceeds**), ולכן פירושו כשלעצמו (**considered in itself**).

_In **not the temperature of the surface as such but how far it exceeds**, the phrase sets the temperature in itself against the gap._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that if water flicked onto a pan hisses and vanishes at once, the pan

options.label: probably needs more heating before meat is seared in it
is probably too hot and should be left to cool before use
is already covered by a thin cushion of vapor

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 1 טיפות שרוחשות ונעלמות מעידות שהמחבת רק חמה (**merely hot**), ולפי פסקה 4 טיפות שמחליקות הן הסימן שהיא מוכנה, ולכן היא כנראה צריכה עוד חימום (**needs more heating**).

_Drops that **hiss and vanish** mean a pan that is **merely hot**, while **drops that skate** show it is ready, so it probably needs more heating._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Appearing in huge numbers protects the cicadas, and their prime-numbered cycles have been shown to keep them well clear of predators with shorter cycles.
Periodical cicadas may keep time by counting the yearly cycles of the trees on whose roots they feed.
Emerging in vast numbers at once protects the cicadas, but why their cycles run to a prime number of years is still debated.
Many animals rely on safety in numbers, which explains why their life cycles tend to follow a fixed rhythm.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 2 קובעת שההופעה ההמונית היא הגנה (**less a curiosity than a defense**) ופסקאות 3–4 מציגות השערות שנויות במחלוקת, ולכן התשובה: ההמונים מגינים, אבל אורך המחזור הראשוני עדיין שנוי במחלוקת (**is still debated**).

_Mass emergence is **less a curiosity than a defense**, but for the prime cycles **Neither idea has gone unchallenged**, so their length is still debated._

questionText: According to the passage, a cicada that came out of the ground a year before the rest of its brood would most likely

options.label: lose the protection that comes from appearing in vast numbers
run short of the root sap it needs before it could mate
mate with cicadas from a brood that follows a different cycle
escape the notice of predators that do not expect cicadas that year

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 2 אומרת שציקדה שיוצאת לבד או שנה מוקדם לא תיהנה מהגנה כזו (**would enjoy no such protection**), כלומר היא מאבדת את ההגנה שבהמונים (**lose the protection**).

_A cicada that emerged **alone, or a year early, would enjoy no such protection**, the protection of vast numbers._

questionText: According to the passage, one objection to the idea that prime cycles help the cicadas avoid predators is that

options.label: prime-numbered cycles are also common among insects that live above ground
broods of different lengths have often been seen emerging together in the same year
the cicadas keep time less precisely than the idea would require
the enemies the idea depends on have not been shown to exist

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 4 המבקרים מציינים שלא נמצא טורף בעל מחזור מתאים (**No predator with a matching multi-year cycle has been found**), כלומר לא הוכח שהאויב שההשערה נשענת עליו קיים.

_Critics note that **No predator with a matching multi-year cycle has been found**, so the enemy the idea needs is unproven._

questionText: As used in the passage, the phrase "gorge themselves" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **still** בצירוף **and still leave most of the brood untouched** (ובכל זאת משאירים את רוב הלהקה) מראה שהטורפים אוכלים הרבה, ולכן הצירוף **gorge themselves** פירושו לזלול כמה שאפשר (**eat greedily and heavily**).

_Predators **gorge themselves and still leave most of the brood untouched**: they eat as much as they can, yet most cicadas survive._

questionText: Why does the author mention a brood that appeared every twelve years?

options.label: To report that some broods of cicadas once followed a cycle that lasted for twelve years
To argue that a twelve-year cycle would help keep broods of different lengths from interbreeding
To explain why the numbers of many predators rise and fall at regular intervals of a few years
To show, by an imagined case, that a cycle that is not prime would meet enemies more frequently

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **would meet any enemy** (הייתה פוגשת כל אויב) מציג להקה דמיונית, והצירוף **whereas a seventeen-year brood** מעמיד מולה מחזור ראשוני, כדי להראות שמחזור לא ראשוני מביא יותר מפגשים עם אויבים.

_The twelve-year brood is imagined (**would meet any enemy**) and set against **a seventeen-year brood** to show what a cycle that is not prime would cost._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: Dust between the stars fails to explain the dark sky, since it would grow hot and glow almost as brightly as the stars.
The night sky is dark because the light of distant stars grows too faint to be seen from the Earth with the naked eye.
Simple everyday observations, rather than costly instruments, have settled most of the great questions about the origin of the universe.
Long a genuine puzzle, the dark night sky is now explained largely by the limited age of the universe and the speed of light.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקאות 1–2 מציגות חידה שההסברים הישנים לא פתרו ופסקה 3 מסבירה אותה, ולכן התשובה: החושך מוסבר בעיקר בגיל המוגבל של היקום (**the limited age of the universe**) ובמהירות האור.

_Paragraphs 1 and 2 build the puzzle, and paragraph 3 solves it: the universe **had a beginning** and **light travels at a finite speed**._

questionText: According to the passage, why does the faintness of distant stars fail to account for the dark sky?

options.label: Their light has not yet had time to reach the Earth, however bright the stars may be.
There are more of them at greater distances, which offsets the weaker light of each one.
Dust between the stars dims the light of nearby stars as much as that of distant ones.
Distant stars are generally larger and hotter than the stars that lie closer to the Earth.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 2 מספר הכוכבים גדל עם המרחק בדיוק בקצב שמפצה על החלשות האור (הצירוף **the rate needed to make up for that loss**), ולכן יש יותר כוכבים רחוקים, וזה מקזז את האור החלש (**offsets the weaker light**).

_The number of stars grows at **just the rate needed to make up for that loss**, so more distant stars offset each one's weaker light._

questionText: According to the passage, which of the following is one reason the night sky is dark?

options.label: Dust between the stars soaks up much of their light.
The light of distant stars is too faint to reach the Earth.
Stars eventually burn out and stop giving off light.
Light gradually loses speed on very long journeys through space.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בפסקה 3 ההסבר המקובל כולל גם את העובדה שכוכבים לא מאירים לנצח (**Stars, moreover, do not shine forever**), ולכן אחת הסיבות היא שכוכבים כבים בסופו של דבר ומפסיקים להפיץ אור.

_Paragraph 3 adds that **Stars, moreover, do not shine forever**, so stars that burn out help keep the sky dark._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "sketch" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפתרון הוצע במסה השערתית (**in a speculative essay**) בידי מי שלא היה אסטרונום (**not an astronomer**), ולכן המילה **sketch** פירושה להציג בקווים כלליים (**outline in broad terms**).

_A solution offered **in a speculative essay** by someone **not an astronomer** was only outlined in broad terms, not worked out in detail._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that the scientists who largely ignored the essay

options.label: had already reached the same conclusion through their own work
rejected it because it relied on dust between the stars
passed over an early version of the explanation accepted today
were probably right to doubt it, as later evidence showed

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **sketch this solution** מפנה להסבר המקובל היום בפסקה 3, ולכן המדענים שהתעלמו מהמסה החמיצו גרסה מוקדמת שלו (**passed over an early version**).

_The essay was **one of the first to sketch this solution**, the one **now generally accepted**, so the scientists who ignored it passed over an early version of it._

questionText: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: The old belief that ancient readers rarely read silently has been challenged, though reading aloud stayed common for social reasons.
Recent studies have shown that people in the ancient world read in silence just as often as we do today, so the older view was simply wrong.
Words in ancient texts ran together without spaces, so most readers had to sound them out in order to follow them.
Ancient authors preferred to hear their work performed because they distrusted readers who took in a text in silence.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 3 מערערת על התפיסה הישנה ופסקה 4 מייחסת את הקריאה בקול למנהג (**custom**), ולכן התשובה: התפיסה הישנה עורערה (**has been challenged**), אבל הקריאה בקול נשארה נפוצה מסיבות חברתיות.

_Paragraph 3 has **cast doubt on this picture**, and paragraph 4 traces reading aloud to custom, **less in necessity than in custom**._

questionText: According to the passage, what did some historians conclude from the way ancient books were written?

options.label: Copyists had made the texts difficult to read in silence on purpose.
Punctuation had been added to guide those who were reading aloud.
Readers would have had to voice the words to make sense of them.
Few people could afford to own the books that they wanted to read.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 2 היסטוריונים טענו שאת הדפים הללו כמעט אי אפשר להבין בלי להשמיע אותם (**could hardly be made sense of without being sounded out**), כלומר הקוראים נזקקו להשמיע את המילים (**voice the words**).

_Historians argued that such pages **could hardly be made sense of without being sounded out**, so readers had to voice the words._

questionText: According to the passage, what may the author of the famous account really have found surprising?

options.label: That a learned man could read with his voice and lips quite still
That a host read to himself while guests waited, leaving them out
That the page before him had no spaces between its words
That his visitors had been asked to read the text aloud in turn

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי פסקה 3 ייתכן שההפתעה לא הייתה מהקריאה השקטה עצמה, אלא ממארח שקרא בשקט בזמן שאורחיו חיכו (**a host who read silently while visitors waited**), כלומר מכך שהאורחים נשארו מחוץ לטקסט.

_The account may record surprise **not at silent reading itself but at a host who read silently while visitors waited**._

questionText: As used in the passage, the word "managed" is closest in meaning to
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **with little trouble** (בלי קושי רב) וההשוואה לקוראים שקולטים מילים במבט אחד (**take in familiar words at a glance**) מראים שהמילה **managed** פירושה כאן להתמודד היטב (**dealt well with**).

_**with little trouble** and the comparison with readers who **take in familiar words at a glance** show that **managed** means dealt well with._

questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that reading aloud in the ancient world

options.label: was a sign that a reader had not yet fully learned to read
often let people who never learned their letters enjoy a text
was needed chiefly to make sense of pages written without spaces
was usually done by authors presenting their own new work

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** פסקה 4 מונה בין הסיבות לקריאה בקול את העובדה שאנשים רבים לא ידעו קרוא וכתוב (**many people were unlettered**) ושספרות נהנו ממנה בחברה, ולכן הקריאה בקול אפשרה גם להם ליהנות מהטקסט (**enjoy a text**).

_Since **many people were unlettered** and literature **was often enjoyed in company**, reading aloud let those who could not read share in it._

questionText: Original: Before the swimming lesson starts, the children take a shower and put on their caps.

options.label: The children take a shower and take off their caps before they start the swimming lesson.
The children take a shower and put on their caps, and then the swimming lesson starts.
After the children take a shower and put on their caps, they swim in groups of four.
The children take a shower and put on their caps after the swimming lesson.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Before the swimming lesson starts** (לפני שהשיעור מתחיל) מציב את המקלחת ואת הכובעים לפני השיעור, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הסדר בעזרת הצירוף **and then the swimming lesson starts** (ואחר כך השיעור מתחיל).

_**Before the swimming lesson starts** puts the shower and the caps first, and the correct answer keeps this order with **and then the swimming lesson starts**._

questionText: Original: The soup was cooked by my father, and the bread was baked by my sister.

options.label: My father made the soup and the bread.
The soup was cooked for my father, and the bread was baked for my sister.
My father baked the bread, and my sister cooked the soup.
My father cooked the soup, and my sister baked the bread.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **by** (על ידי) מראה מי עשה את הפעולה, והתשובה הנכונה הופכת את המשפט לפעיל ושומרת על התפקידים בצירוף **My father cooked the soup** ובצירוף **my sister baked the bread**.

_**by** shows who did what, and the correct answer keeps the roles in the active voice: **My father cooked the soup**, **my sister baked the bread**._

questionText: Original: Ruth does not eat meat, and she does not drink milk either.

options.label: Ruth eats no meat and drinks no milk.
Ruth eats no meat, but she drinks milk.
Ruth does not eat meat, and her sister does not drink milk either.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **either** (גם לא) מצרפת שלילה שנייה לשלילה הראשונה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שתיהן בצירוף **eats no meat and drinks no milk** (לא אוכלת בשר ולא שותה חלב).

_**either** adds a second negative to the first one, and the correct answer keeps both with **eats no meat and drinks no milk**._

questionText: Original: The café near my school sells hot drinks in winter and cold drinks in summer.

options.label: In winter, the café near my school sells hot drinks.
The café near my school sells cold drinks in winter and hot drinks in summer.
In winter, the café near my school sells hot drinks, while in summer it sells cold drinks.
In winter, the café near my school sells hot drinks and soup, while in summer the café sells ice cream and cold drinks.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **hot drinks in winter** והצירוף **cold drinks in summer** מקשרים כל עונה לסוג המשקה שלה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שני הקשרים בעזרת המילה **while** (בעוד ש-).

_**hot drinks in winter** and **cold drinks in summer** link each season to its drinks, and the correct answer keeps both links with **while**._

questionText: Original: It was a little windy on Sunday, so Ella and her brother flew their kite in the park.

options.label: Ella and her brother flew their kite in the park on Sunday because there was a bit of wind.
It was a bit windy on Sunday, so Ella and her brother stayed at home and played games together.
Ella and her brother flew their kite on Sunday, so it was a little windy.
It was very windy on Sunday, so Ella and her brother flew their kite in the park.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (לכן) מראה שהרוח הקלה היא הסיבה להטסת העפיפון, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הקשר ועל הדרגה בעזרת המילה **because** (כי) והצירוף **a bit of wind** (קצת רוח).

_**so** makes the light wind the reason for flying the kite, and the correct answer keeps the link and the degree with **because** and **a bit of wind**._

questionText: Original: The train was late this morning because there was a problem with the signals.

options.label: The problem with the signals was caused by the late train this morning.
Tomorrow morning, a problem with the signals will make the train late.
A problem with the train made the signals late this morning.
A problem with the signals made the train late this morning.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי) מראה שהבעיה באיתות היא הסיבה לאיחור, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על הסיבה ועל התוצאה בעזרת הפועל **made** (גרם ל-).

_**because** makes the problem with the signals the reason for the delay, and the correct answer keeps reason and result with **made the train late**._

questionText: Original: Few of the students in my class have a pet, but most of them would like one.

options.label: A few of my classmates own a pet, while most of the others would like to have one.
Most of my classmates want a pet, but not many people in my class have one.
Most students in my class own a pet, but few of them want another one.
In my class, few students have a pet, and most of them do not want one.

explanation:

_**hardly any**, **most** and **a few** each apply to a different action, and the correct answer keeps them as **Almost none**, **the majority** and **a small number**._

questionText: Original: Although the village council replaced its old street lamps with LED lamps that use far less electricity, the lighting bill has not fallen, because the new lamps stay on for two extra hours each night.

options.label: Despite the new lamps staying on for two extra hours each night, the lighting bill has fallen, because the village council replaced its old street lamps with LED lamps that use far less electricity.

The lighting bill has not fallen, although the village council's new LED lamps use far less electricity than its old street lamps, because they stay on for two extra hours each night and cost more to install.

Despite swapping its old street lamps for LED lamps that consume much less electricity, the village council has seen no drop in its lighting bill, since the new lamps stay on two hours longer every night.
The village council's old street lamps need far less power than the new LED lamps, which is why the lighting bill has not fallen, even though the new lamps stay on for two extra hours each night.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **has not fallen** (לא ירד) מופיע בתשובה הנכונה כצירוף **has seen no drop in its lighting bill** (לא ראתה ירידה בחשבון), והסיבה נשמרת בצירוף **two hours longer every night**, בלי היפוך ובלי תוספת.

_**has not fallen** reappears as **has seen no drop in its lighting bill**, and the reason as **two hours longer every night**, with nothing reversed or added._

questionText: Original: Although nearly all of the people who signed up at the new gym in January planned to work out three times a week, only about a third of them were still going regularly by March.

options.label: Although only about a third of the people who signed up at the new gym in January planned to work out three times a week, nearly all of them were still going regularly by March.
Nearly all of the people who signed up at the new gym in January planned to work out three times a week, and by March about a third of them had stopped going regularly.
By March, only about one in three of those who had joined the new gym in January still went there regularly, though almost all had meant to exercise three times a week.
Around a third of those who signed up at the new gym in January went there three times a week until March, when most of them stopped.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **nearly all** (כמעט כולם) מתאר את מי שתכננו להתאמן, והצירוף **only about a third** (רק כשליש) את מי שעדיין הגיעו במרץ, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת כל כמות במקומה.

_**Nearly all** planned to train three times a week, but **only about a third** were still going by March; the correct answer keeps each amount with its group._

questionText: Original: Before the first postage stamps were introduced in Britain in 1840, the person who received a letter, rather than the sender, usually paid for it, so many letters were refused at the door.

options.label: Until postage stamps first appeared in Britain in 1840, letters were normally paid for by the people receiving them, not by those sending them, so many were turned away at the door.
Once the first postage stamps had been introduced in Britain in 1840, a letter was usually paid for by its recipient rather than its sender, so many letters were refused at the door.
Because many letters were being refused at the door, the person who received a letter in Britain, rather than the sender, usually paid for it until the first postage stamps appeared in 1840.
When the first postage stamps were introduced in Britain in 1840, many people at first refused them, since they were used to paying for letters on receiving them rather than on sending them.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Before** (לפני) שקולה כאן למילה **Until** (עד ש-): עד 1840 מי שקיבל מכתב שילם עליו, ובגלל זה (המילה **so**) מכתבים רבים נדחו בפתח הבית.

_**Before** 1840 works like **Until** 1840 here: the person receiving a letter paid for it, **so** many letters were refused at the door._

questionText: Original: The leisure center opened a second pool last spring, which attracted more evening swimmers, but its income barely rose because most of the newcomers used the free family sessions.

options.label: Opening a second pool last spring brought the leisure center more evening swimmers, but its income barely rose because most of the newcomers used the free family sessions, which the council now plans to charge for.
A second pool, opened at the leisure center last spring, drew more evening swimmers, yet most of the new arrivals used the free family sessions, so income hardly increased.
The second pool that opened last spring attracted more evening swimmers to the leisure center, although its income barely rose.
The leisure center offered free family sessions last spring, which attracted more evening swimmers, but its income barely rose until it opened a second pool.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט כולל ארבע יחידות: בריכה שנייה, יותר שחיינים בערב, הכנסה שכמעט לא עלתה (הצירוף **barely rose**) והסיבה (המילה **because**), והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על כולן ולא מוסיפה דבר.

_Four units: a second pool, more evening swimmers, income that **barely rose**, and the reason (**because** newcomers used free sessions); the correct answer keeps all four and adds nothing._

questionText: Original: Although the restaurant's new head chef was hired by its owners, she had been recommended to them by the kitchen staff, several of whom she had trained years earlier.

options.label: Although the restaurant's new head chef was hired by the kitchen staff, she had been recommended to them by its owners, several of whom she had trained years earlier.
The restaurant's owners hired the new head chef on the kitchen staff's advice, and in the years since she was hired, she has gone on to train several of them herself.
Although the head chef had trained several members of the kitchen staff years earlier, the owners of the restaurant took them on without first asking for her recommendation.
The kitchen staff, several of whom had been trained by the restaurant's new head chef years before, suggested her to its owners, though it was the owners who hired her.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **was hired by its owners** (נשכרה על ידי הבעלים) והצירוף **recommended to them by the kitchen staff** (הומלצה להם על ידי צוות המטבח) קובעים מי עשה מה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שני התפקידים.

_The chef **was hired by its owners** but **recommended to them by the kitchen staff**; the correct answer keeps both roles and the earlier training._

questionText: Original: Not until they had slept normally for two nights did the volunteers kept awake in the study regain their usual reaction times, even though most of them reported feeling fully alert after the first.

options.label: Although most of the volunteers kept awake in the study said they felt fully alert after one normal night's sleep, the group's reaction times recovered only after a second night.
The volunteers kept awake in the study were back to their usual reaction times after a single night's normal sleep, though most of them still felt listless until the second.
Even after two nights of normal sleep, the volunteers kept awake in the study had not regained their usual reaction times, though most of them reported feeling fully alert after the first.
Not until the majority of the volunteers reported feeling fully alert did the study let them sleep normally for two nights, after which their usual reaction times returned.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Not until** (רק אחרי ש-) אומר שזמני התגובה חזרו לרגיל רק אחרי שני לילות שינה, אף שרוב המתנדבים הרגישו ערניים כבר אחרי הלילה הראשון, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שני הזמנים.

_**Not until** two nights of normal sleep did reaction times recover, although most volunteers felt **fully alert after the first**; the correct answer keeps both times._

questionText: Original: In one study, people who doodled while listening to a dull phone message later recalled more of its details than those who simply listened, perhaps because doodling kept them from drifting into reverie.

options.label: One study showed that doodling while listening to a dull phone message makes people remember far more of its details, since it stops them from daydreaming.

Asked in advance to memorize a dull phone message, people in one study who doodled during the call later recalled more of its details than those who simply listened, perhaps because they were less prone to reverie.
In one study, people whose minds tended to drift into reverie doodled more while listening to a dull phone message, and later remembered less of what it said than those who simply listened.

Those who simply listened to a dull phone message in one study later remembered fewer of its details than people who doodled as they listened, possibly because doodling stopped their minds from wandering.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט זהיר: מחקר אחד (הצירוף **In one study**), זכרו יותר פרטים, וסיבה משוערת בלבד (המילה **perhaps**), והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על ההסתייגויות ולא מוסיפה דבר.

_The original is cautious (**In one study**, **perhaps because**); the correct answer keeps the comparison and the hedged reason without adding or strengthening anything._

questionText: Original: Hatched in the nest of a reed warbler, a young cuckoo pushes its foster parents' own eggs out of the nest, yet the warblers go on feeding the interloper for weeks.

options.label: A young reed warbler hatched in a cuckoo's nest pushes the cuckoo's own eggs out, and yet its foster parents keep feeding it for weeks.
For weeks, reed warblers go on feeding a young cuckoo that hatched in their nest, even though it has pushed their own eggs out of the nest.
A young cuckoo hatched in a reed warbler's nest is fed by the warblers for several weeks before it finally pushes their own eggs out of the nest.
Because the young cuckoo in their nest goes on feeding for weeks, the warblers push their own eggs out to make room for the interloper.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט הקוקייה הצעירה דוחפת החוצה את הביצים של הוריה המאמצים (הצירוף **foster parents' own eggs**), וציפורי הקנית ממשיכות להאכיל אותה (הצירוף **go on feeding the interloper**), והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על התפקידים.

_The young cuckoo pushes out its **foster parents' own eggs**, yet the warblers **go on feeding the interloper**; the correct answer keeps who does what and when._

questionText: Original: A female cod may release millions of eggs a season, yet seldom do more than a handful of her progeny reach adulthood, a fraction that is usually enough to keep the population stable.

options.label: A female cod may release millions of eggs a season, of which a sizable minority usually survive into adulthood, a share that is enough to keep the population stable.
A female cod may release millions of eggs a season, and although a mere handful of her progeny usually reach adulthood, so small a fraction is seldom enough to keep the population stable.
Only rarely do more than a few of the millions of eggs a female cod may produce a season become adults, yet that small share is generally enough to keep the population steady.
Seldom does a female cod reach adulthood, yet the handful that do may release millions of eggs a season, usually enough to keep the population stable.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **seldom** (לעתים רחוקות) והצירוף **more than a handful** (יותר מקומץ) אומרים שמעטים מאוד שורדים, והצירוף **usually enough** אומר שזה בכל זאת מספיק, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם.

_**Seldom do more than a handful** survive, yet that fraction is **usually enough**; the correct answer keeps the tiny number and its sufficiency._

questionText: Original: Far from revealing a slipshod writer, the typos people overlook in their own work stem largely from knowing what they meant to say, which leads the brain to read the intended words instead.

options.label: Typos missed in one's own texts are no mark of carelessness; they come mostly from knowing the intended meaning, so the brain sees the words meant, not those written.
People tend to overlook typos in their own work largely because they already know just what they intended to say, which leads the brain to read the intended words instead.
The typos people overlook in their own work are largely the sign of a slipshod writer, rather than of a brain that reads the words it was expecting.
Writers who know what they meant to say are far from slipshod, so their brains tend to make them miss the typos in other people's work rather than the ones in their own.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Far from revealing a slipshod writer** (רחוק מלהעיד על כותב רשלן) שולל רשלנות, והצירוף **stem largely from knowing what they meant to say** נותן את הסיבה האמיתית, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם.

_**Far from revealing a slipshod writer** rules out carelessness, and **stem largely from knowing what they meant to say** gives the real cause; the correct answer keeps both._

questionText: Original: Even when told outright that their pills contained no active ingredient, a good number of patients in some trials reported that their symptoms had eased, though measurable signs of the underlying malady seldom changed.

options.label: Even after learning that their pills held no active ingredient, many patients in some trials found that their symptoms had vanished, though objective signs of the illness itself seldom changed.
In some trials, quite a few patients said they felt better even after being openly informed that their pills were inactive, although objective measures of the disease itself rarely showed a change.

Even when told outright that their pills contained no active ingredient, most patients in the trials reported that their symptoms had eased, though measurable signs of the underlying malady seldom changed.

Patients in some trials who were told outright that their pills contained no active ingredient seldom reported that their symptoms had eased, although measurable signs of the underlying malady changed in a good number of them.

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הטענה במשפט מוגבלת: לא מעט מטופלים (הצירוף **a good number of patients**), רק בחלק מהניסויים (הצירוף **in some trials**), דיווחו על הקלה, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על ההיקף ועל הניגוד מול הסימנים המדידים.

_The original is limited (**a good number of patients**, **in some trials**, symptoms **had eased**); the correct answer keeps this scope and the contrast with signs that **seldom changed**._

questionText: My little brother is afraid of the dark, so he sleeps with a ________ on all night.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הילד פוחד מהחושך (**afraid of the dark**), ולכן הוא ישן עם משהו שדולק כל הלילה (**on all night**): מנורה (**lamp**).

_He is **afraid of the dark**, so he sleeps with something **on all night**: a **lamp**, which gives light._

questionText: My little sister is small, but she is very ________ and can carry her own bag.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** (אבל) מסמנת ניגוד לכך שהאחות קטנה (**small**), והיכולת לשאת תיק (**can carry her own bag**) מראה שהיא חזקה (**strong**).

_**But** signals a contrast with **small**, and being able to **carry her own bag** shows that she is **strong**._

questionText: My uncle is very ________ – he has a big house by the sea and three new cars.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההסבר שאחרי המקף, **he has a big house by the sea and three new cars** (יש לו בית גדול ליד הים ושלוש מכוניות חדשות), מראה שהדוד עשיר (**rich**).

_The explanation after the dash, **he has a big house by the sea and three new cars**, tells us that the uncle is **rich**._

questionText: She packed some warm ________ for the trip, such as a coat, two sweaters and a scarf.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** (כמו) מציג דוגמאות: מעיל, שני סוודרים וצעיף (**a coat, two sweaters and a scarf**), וכל אלה הם בגדים (**clothes**).

_The examples after **such as**, **a coat, two sweaters and a scarf**, are all things to wear: **clothes**._

questionText: My dentist told me to ________ my teeth twice a day.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפועל **brush** יוצר צירוף קבוע עם הביטוי **my teeth** (לצחצח שיניים), וזה מה שרופא שיניים (**My dentist**) מייעץ לעשות פעמיים ביום.

_The verb **brush** forms a fixed phrase with **my teeth**, which is what **My dentist** advises doing twice a day._

questionText: Dan climbed the ________ to pick apples from the top of the tree.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המטרה, **to pick apples from the top of the tree** (לקטוף תפוחים מראש העץ), מחייבת חפץ גבוה שאפשר לטפס עליו: סולם (**ladder**).

_To **pick apples from the top of the tree**, Dan needs something tall to climb: a **ladder**._

questionText: Last night, the children ________ happy birthday to my grandmother.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Last night** (אמש) מסמן זמן עבר, ולכן הפועל חייב להיות בצורת העבר: **sang** (הם שרו).

_**Last night** marks the past, so the verb must be in the past simple: **sang**._

questionText: Mia has a very high temperature and a bad cough, so she is ________ today.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (ולכן) מציגה תוצאה: חום גבוה ושיעול (**a very high temperature and a bad cough**) הם סימני מחלה, ולכן מיה חולה (**ill**).

_**So** introduces the result: **a very high temperature and a bad cough** are signs of sickness, so Mia is **ill**._

questionText: Lily felt ________ after spinning around ten times, so she sat down on the grass.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (ולכן) מחברת בין הסיבה **spinning around ten times** (סיבוב עשר פעמים) לבין ישיבה על הדשא: מי שמסתובבת כך מרגישה סחרחורת (**dizzy**).

_**So** links **spinning around ten times** to sitting down: after spinning like that a person feels **dizzy**._

questionText: The street is very ________, which means that two cars cannot pass each other.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **which means that** (כלומר) מסביר את המילה החסרה: **two cars cannot pass each other** (שתי מכוניות לא יכולות לחלוף זו על פני זו), ורחוב כזה הוא צר (**narrow**).

_The phrase **which means that** explains the blank: if **two cars cannot pass each other**, the street is **narrow**._

questionText: Many ________ live in our garden, such as ants, bees and flies.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** (כמו) מציג נמלים, דבורים וזבובים (**ants, bees and flies**), וכל אלה הם חרקים (**insects**).

_The examples after **such as**, **ants, bees and flies**, are all small animals with six legs: **insects**._

questionText: Look left and right before you ________ the street.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפועל **cross** יוצר צירוף קבוע עם הביטוי **the street** (לחצות את הרחוב), ולפני חציית רחוב מסתכלים שמאלה וימינה (**Look left and right**).

_The verb **cross** forms a fixed phrase with **the street**, and people **Look left and right** before crossing._

questionText: After losing every game, the players feel ________: they do not believe they can ever win.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הסיומת **-less** פירושה בלי: שחקנים שאינם מאמינים שינצחו אי פעם (**they do not believe they can ever win**) הם בלי תקווה, כלומר מיואשים (**hopeless**).

_The suffix **-less** means without: players who **do not believe they can ever win** are without hope, so they feel **hopeless**._

questionText: The magic show was ________, and the children clapped for a long time.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנושא **The magic show** הוא דבר שגורם להרגשה אצל אחרים, ולכן מתארים אותו בתואר **amazing** (מדהים) ולא בתואר **amazed** (נדהם).

_**The magic show** causes the feeling in others, so it is **amazing**; **amazed** describes the people who feel it._

questionText: When she reads the newspaper, my aunt puts on her ________ because she cannot see small letters.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** מי שאינה רואה אותיות קטנות (**she cannot see small letters**) כשהיא קוראת עיתון מרכיבה משקפיים (**glasses**).

_A person who **cannot see small letters** while reading the newspaper puts on **glasses**._

questionText: The film starts in ten minutes, so we must ________ to get there on time.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (ולכן) מחברת בין הסיבה **The film starts in ten minutes** (הסרט מתחיל בעוד עשר דקות) לבין מה שצריך לעשות כדי להגיע בזמן (**to get there on time**): למהר (**hurry**).

_The word **so** links **The film starts in ten minutes** to what we must do to arrive **on time**: **hurry**._

questionText: My bedroom is very ________: there are clothes, books and shoes all over the floor.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הנקודתיים בא הסבר: **clothes, books and shoes all over the floor** (בגדים, ספרים ונעליים בכל רחבי הרצפה), וחדר כזה הוא מבולגן (**messy**).

_The part after the colon explains the blank: **clothes, books and shoes all over the floor** means that the room is **messy**._

questionText: The shop sells beautiful ________, such as tables, chairs and beds.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** (כמו) מציג דוגמאות למילה החסרה: **tables, chairs and beds** (שולחנות, כיסאות ומיטות), והמילה שכוללת את כולן היא ריהוט (**furniture**).

_The phrase **such as** introduces examples of the blank: **tables, chairs and beds** are all **furniture**._

questionText: Dan learned how to ________ a knot in the rope before he hung the swing from the tree.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **knot** (קשר) יוצרת עם הפועל **tie** (לקשור) צירוף קבוע: אומרים **tie a knot** ולא **stretch a knot**, **fold a knot** או **bend a knot**.

_The noun **knot** goes with the verb **tie**: we say **tie a knot**, not **stretch**, **fold** or **bend** a knot._

questionText: The nurse put a ________ on my finger because it was bleeding.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **because** (כי) מסבירה למה האחות (**nurse**) שמה משהו על האצבע: **it was bleeding** (היא דיממה), ולכן היא שמה תחבושת (**bandage**) שמכסה את הפצע.

_The word **because** gives the reason: **it was bleeding**, so the nurse put a **bandage** on the finger._

questionText: Although the new manager seemed ________ when she arrived, she soon became the most popular person in the office.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** (למרות ש-) מסמנת ניגוד: מכיוון ש-**she soon became the most popular person** (היא הפכה במהרה לאדם הכי פופולרי), הרושם הראשון היה שלילי: **selfish** (אנוכית).

_**Although** signals contrast: since **she soon became the most popular person**, her first impression was negative, so she seemed **selfish**._

questionText: The new hiking boots are ________, that is, your feet stay dry even when you walk through heavy rain for hours.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **that is** (כלומר) מסביר את המילה החסרה: **your feet stay dry even when you walk through heavy rain** (הרגליים נשארות יבשות גם בגשם חזק), וזה פירוש המילה **waterproof** (אטום למים).

_The phrase **that is** introduces an explanation: if **your feet stay dry even when you walk through heavy rain**, the boots are **waterproof**._

questionText: Because it was ________ cold outside, the school canceled the sports day and kept all the children indoors.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **cold** (קר) יוצרת עם המילה **bitterly** את הצירוף הקבוע **bitterly cold** (קר מאוד), וההמשך **canceled the sports day** מתאים לקור עז.

_The word **cold** forms the fixed phrase **bitterly cold** (extremely cold), and the result **canceled the sports day** fits a severe cold._

questionText: Before you clean the toaster, you must ________ it, so that no electricity goes through it while you work.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המטרה **so that no electricity goes through it** (כדי שלא יעבור בו חשמל) מחייבת לנתק את הטוסטר, והתחילית **un-** (ביטול פעולה) עם המילה **plug** (תֶּקַע) נותנת **unplug** (לנתק מהחשמל).

_The purpose **so that no electricity goes through it** means the toaster must be disconnected: **un-** (undo) + **plug** = **unplug**._

questionText: Whereas the new reading room is full of students chatting at every table, the old library was so ________ that visitors whispered.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Whereas** (בעוד ש-) מציבה ניגוד: בחדר החדש התלמידים משוחחים (**chatting at every table**), ולכן הספרייה הישנה הייתה ההפך: **silent** (דוממת, ללא קול).

_**Whereas** sets up a contrast: the new room is full of students **chatting at every table**, so the old library was the opposite: **silent**._

questionText: Many dangerous sports require special ________, for example helmets, gloves and knee pads, which protect the body from injury.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **for example** (למשל) מציג דוגמאות למילה החסרה: **helmets, gloves and knee pads** (קסדות, כפפות ומגני ברכיים), והשם הכללי להן הוא ציוד (**equipment**).

_The phrase **for example** introduces examples of the blank: **helmets, gloves and knee pads** are all **equipment**._

questionText: Unless the bakery ________ more workers soon, it will not be able to serve all of its customers.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי **Unless** (אלא אם כן) באה צורת הווה פשוט גם כשהכוונה לעתיד, ולכן הצורה **hires** מתאימה, וההמשך **it will not be able** כבר מבטא את העתיד.

_After **Unless** we use the present simple even for the future, so **hires** fits; **it will not be able** already carries the future meaning._

questionText: The desks were in long rows, which made group work difficult, so the teacher decided to ________ them into small circles.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (ולכן) מראה שבגלל השורות הארוכות (**in long rows**) המורה החליטה לסדר את השולחנות מחדש, והתחילית **re-** (שוב, מחדש) עם המילה **arrange** (לסדר) נותנת **rearrange** (לסדר מחדש).

_The word **so** shows that because the desks were **in long rows**, the teacher put them in a new order: **re-** (again) + **arrange** = **rearrange**._

questionText: The jacket was half price, so it was a real ________ and I bought two of them.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **so** (ולכן) מחברת את המחיר הזול (**half price**, חצי מחיר) לתוצאה: זו הייתה עסקה משתלמת (**bargain**), ולכן קניתי שניים.

_The word **so** links **half price** to the result: it was a real **bargain** (a very good deal), so I bought two._

questionText: My grandfather is a ________ man – in other words, he rarely changes his mind, even when everyone disagrees with him.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **in other words** (במילים אחרות) מסביר את המילה החסרה: המשפט **he rarely changes his mind, even when everyone disagrees with him** מתאר אדם עיקש (**stubborn**).

_**In other words** explains the blank: a man who **rarely changes his mind, even when everyone disagrees with him**, is **stubborn**._

questionText: After months without rain, the stream behind our house became so ________ that the children could walk across it without getting their knees wet.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **so ... that** מסמן תוצאה: הילדים חצו את הנחל בלי שהברכיים נרטבו (**walk across it without getting their knees wet**), ולכן המים היו **shallow** (רדודים).

_**So ... that** introduces a result: the children could **walk across it without getting their knees wet**, so the stream was **shallow** (not deep)._

questionText: Many people feel ________ after a big meal, but a short walk in the fresh air usually wakes them up again.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** מעמידה מול התחושה החסרה הליכה שמעירה אנשים (**a short walk in the fresh air usually wakes them up again**), ולכן התחושה היא **drowsy** (מנומנם).

_**But** contrasts the missing feeling with a walk that **wakes them up again**, so the feeling is **drowsy** (half asleep)._

questionText: While Anna spends her salary as soon as she receives it, her brother is ________ and saves half of every month's pay.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **While** מעמידה את האח מול אנה, שמוציאה את המשכורת מיד (**spends her salary as soon as she receives it**), ולכן הוא **thrifty** (חסכן) וחוסך חצי ממנה.

_**While** contrasts the brother with Anna, who **spends her salary as soon as she receives it**, so he is **thrifty** (careful with money)._

questionText: The mushrooms sold at this market are ________, which means that people can eat them without any danger.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **which means** מגדיר את החסר: אפשר לאכול את הפטריות בלי סכנה (**people can eat them without any danger**), ולכן הן **edible** (ראויות למאכל).

_**Which means** defines the blank: **people can eat them without any danger**, so the mushrooms are **edible** (safe to eat)._

questionText: The small island is ________: its ground is so dry that almost nothing grows there, not even a single tree.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מציגות הסבר: האדמה יבשה כל כך שכמעט שום דבר אינו צומח בה (**almost nothing grows there**), ולכן האי הוא **barren** (עקר, חסר צמחייה).

_The colon introduces an explanation: **almost nothing grows there**, so the island is **barren** (without plants)._

questionText: Families on low incomes often struggle to pay for basic ________, such as food, housing and heating.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** מביא דוגמאות לחסר: אוכל, דיור וחימום (**food, housing and heating**) הם דברים הכרחיים, כלומר **necessities** (צרכי יסוד).

_**Such as** gives examples of the blank: **food, housing and heating** are things people must have, so they are **necessities** (basic needs)._

questionText: After the long walk, the scouts decided to ________ their tents beside the lake before it got dark.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפועל **pitch** יוצר עם המילים **their tents** את הצירוף הקבוע **pitch a tent** (להקים אוהל), ולכן הוא מתאים למה שחברי הקבוצה עושים ליד האגם (**beside the lake**); שאר הפעלים אינם נאמרים עם אוהל.

_**Pitch** forms the fixed phrase **pitch a tent** (set up a tent) with **their tents**, which fits what the scouts do **beside the lake**._

questionText: The company sells its products ________, in more than ninety countries on five continents.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **worldwide** בנויה מ-**world** (עולם) ו-**wide** (רחב), והיא מתאימה לפירוט שאחרי הפסיק: יותר מתשעים מדינות בחמש יבשות (**more than ninety countries on five continents**).

_**Worldwide** is **world** plus **wide** (everywhere), and it matches the detail after the comma: **more than ninety countries on five continents**._

questionText: Because the town's youth orchestra ________ entirely by local businesses, it can offer free lessons to every child.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** התזמורת אינה נותנת חסות לאיש אלא מקבלת אותה, והנותנים נזכרים אחרי המילה **by** (**by local businesses**), ולכן דרושה צורת סביל בהווה: **is sponsored** (נתמכת בחסות).

_The orchestra does not sponsor anyone; it receives support, and the givers follow **by** (**by local businesses**), so a present passive is needed: **is sponsored**._

questionText: The power went out on Friday night, and nobody opened the refrigerator for two days; as a result, most of the fresh food inside began to ________ in the warm kitchen.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **as a result** מסמן תוצאה: יומיים בלי חשמל ובמטבח חם (**in the warm kitchen**), ולכן האוכל הטרי התחיל להתקלקל, כלומר **spoil**.

_The phrase **as a result** introduces the consequence: two days without power in **the warm kitchen** make the fresh food begin to **spoil** (go bad)._

questionText: Although the new school was praised for its bright, modern classrooms, teachers complained that the supply of textbooks was ________, so students often had to share one book among three.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** מעמידה מול השבח על הכיתות תלונה של מורים, והמילה **so** מראה שתלמידים חולקים ספר אחד (**share one book among three**), ולכן האספקה הייתה **inadequate** (לא מספקת).
