_**Although** sets the teachers' complaint against the praise, and **so** shows that students **share one book among three**, so the supply was **inadequate** (not enough)._

questionText: Although the singer's first album was praised for its variety, her latest one is ________: that is, nearly every song uses the same rhythm and the same melody.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **that is** מסביר את החסר: כמעט כל שיר משתמש באותו קצב ובאותה מנגינה (**the same rhythm and the same melody**), ולכן האלבום הוא **repetitive** (חוזר על עצמו), בניגוד למגוון באלבום הראשון.

_**That is** explains the blank: **the same rhythm and the same melody** in nearly every song make the album **repetitive**, unlike the first one's **variety**._

questionText: Although some desserts, such as fruit salad and plain yogurt, are ________ for the body, others, such as chocolate cake and fried doughnuts, contain a great deal of sugar and fat.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמאות **fruit salad and plain yogurt** והניגוד עם קינוחים שיש בהם הרבה סוכר ושומן (**a great deal of sugar and fat**) מורים על התשובה **nutritious** (מזינים).

_The examples **fruit salad and plain yogurt**, set against desserts with **a great deal of sugar and fat**, point to **nutritious** (good for the body)._

questionText: Although the two scientists examined exactly the same data, they ________ it in opposite ways: one saw proof that the treatment worked, and the other saw proof that it failed.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** ההמשך אחרי הנקודתיים (**one saw proof that the treatment worked, and the other saw proof that it failed**) מראה שכל מדען הבין את אותם נתונים אחרת, כלומר **interpreted** (פירשו).

_After the colon, one scientist **saw proof that the treatment worked** and the other **saw proof that it failed**, so they **interpreted** (explained the meaning of) the same data differently._

questionText: Although paying by card is faster than counting out cash, its main ________ is that spending feels less real, so people often buy more than they planned.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** (למרות ש) פותחת ביתרון של תשלום בכרטיס, וההמשך **spending feels less real** מתאר בעיה, ולכן החסר הוא **drawback** (חיסרון, צד שלילי).

_**Although** opens with an advantage of paying by card, and **spending feels less real** describes a problem, so the blank is **drawback** (a downside)._

questionText: Although many people at first dismissed the microwave oven as a gimmick, families across the country soon ________ it as a quick way to heat a meal after a long day.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** והמילה **soon** מסמנות מעבר מדחייה של התנור (**dismissed the microwave oven as a gimmick**) לאימוץ שלו, ולכן המשפחות **embraced** (אימצו בהתלהבות) אותו.

_**Although** and **soon** mark a shift from rejection (**dismissed the microwave oven as a gimmick**) to acceptance, so families **embraced** (welcomed eagerly) it._

questionText: Although the review panel praised the proposal for its ambition, it also called it ________; that is, impossible to carry out with the money and staff available.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **that is** מגדיר את החסר: תוכנית שאי אפשר לבצע עם הכסף והצוות שיש (**impossible to carry out with the money and staff available**) היא **infeasible** (בלתי ניתנת לביצוע), בניגוד לשבח על השאפתנות.

_**That is** defines the blank: a plan **impossible to carry out with the money and staff available** is **infeasible**, which contrasts with the praise for its ambition._

questionText: Although the region now relies on tourism and software, its hills are still dotted with ________ of the old mining industry, such as rusted carts, stone wells and half-buried rails.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** מציג דוגמאות (**rusted carts, stone wells and half-buried rails**) שנותרו מתעשיית הכרייה (**mining industry**), והמילה **Although** מעמידה אותן מול כלכלת היום, ולכן החסר הוא **relics** (שרידים).

_**Such as** gives old leftovers (**rusted carts, stone wells and half-buried rails**), and **Although** contrasts them with today's economy, so the blank is **relics** (objects left from the past)._

questionText: Although the factory owner denied any wrongdoing, he went to great ________ to keep the inspectors away from the accounts.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **went to great lengths** (עשה מאמץ יוצא דופן) מתאים כאן: המילה **Although** מעמידה את הכחשת העוולה (**denied any wrongdoing**) מול המאמץ **to keep the inspectors away**.

_The fixed phrase **went to great lengths** (made an extreme effort) fits: **Although** sets his denial of wrongdoing (**denied any wrongdoing**) against his effort **to keep the inspectors away**._

questionText: Although Ms. Ruiz is usually calm in meetings, her sharp reply yesterday was completely ________, and several colleagues asked whether she was unwell.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** מעמידה את התגובה החדה מול ההתנהגות הרגועה הרגילה (**usually calm in meetings**), ולכן היא **uncharacteristic** (שאינה אופיינית לה), והשאלה אם היא חולה (**asked whether she was unwell**) מאשרת זאת.

_**Although** contrasts the sharp reply with her usual calm (**usually calm in meetings**), so it was **uncharacteristic** (not typical of her), and colleagues asking whether she was **unwell** confirms it._

questionText: Although safety inspectors had warned of the danger for years, the transport authority grew ________, assuming that nothing serious would ever happen.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הסוף **assuming that nothing serious would ever happen** מראה סיפוק עצמי ורשלנות, והמילה **Although** מעמידה אותו מול האזהרות של הפקחים (**had warned of the danger for years**), ולכן הרשות נעשתה **complacent** (שאננה).

_**Assuming that nothing serious would ever happen** shows careless self-satisfaction, set by **Although** against years of warnings (**had warned of the danger for years**), so the authority grew **complacent**._

questionText: Whereas the old city center is crowded from morning until midnight, the new suburbs are so ________ after dark that a resident can walk for ten minutes without meeting a single person.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Whereas** (ואילו) מעמידה את הפרברים מול מרכז העיר העמוס (**crowded from morning until midnight**), והתוצאה **without meeting a single person** מראה שהם ריקים מאדם, ולכן הם **deserted** (נטושים, ריקים).

_**Whereas** sets the suburbs against the **crowded** center, and **without meeting a single person** shows they are empty of people, so they are **deserted**._

questionText: Although the new can opener was advertised as 'effortless', customers found it ________: it took both hands and a great deal of force to turn the handle.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מסבירים את המילה החסרה: צריך שתי ידיים וכוח רב כדי לסובב את הידית (**it took both hands and a great deal of force to turn the handle**), וזה ההפך מן ההבטחה **effortless**, ולכן הפותחן הוא **clumsy** (מסורבל).

_The colon explains the blank: **it took both hands and a great deal of force to turn the handle**, the opposite of **effortless**, so it is **clumsy** (awkward)._

questionText: Although films often show medieval life as a world of rich nobles, most people were ordinary ________ who worked a small plot of land and usually gave part of each harvest to their lord.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Although** מעמידה עולם של אצילים עשירים (**rich nobles**) מול רוב האנשים, והפרטים **a small plot of land** ו-**part of each harvest to their lord** מגדירים אותם כאיכרים (**peasants**).

_**Although** contrasts **rich nobles** with most people, and **a small plot of land** and **part of each harvest to their lord** describe **peasants** (poor farmers)._

questionText: Although most household products are safe to keep in a cupboard, ________ substances, such as gasoline, paint thinner and some cleaning sprays, must be stored away from heat.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as** מביא דוגמאות (**gasoline, paint thinner and some cleaning sprays**), והסוף **must be stored away from heat** מגדיר את הקבוצה כחומרים **flammable** (דליקים).

_**Such as** gives examples (**gasoline, paint thinner and some cleaning sprays**), and **must be stored away from heat** defines the group as **flammable** (easily set on fire)._

questionText: Despite early complaints that the new playground next door would be unbearably noisy, most neighbors have grown ________ to the sound, and many no longer notice it at all.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Despite** והצירוף **no longer notice it at all** מראים שהתלונות הראשוניות נשכחו והשכנים התרגלו לרעש, ולכן התשובה **accustomed** (מורגל, רגיל).

_**Despite** the early complaints, many neighbors **no longer notice it at all**, so they have grown **accustomed** (used) to the sound._

questionText: Granted, starting school an hour later gives teenagers more time in bed, but if they simply go to sleep an hour later each night, the benefit is ________ by their new bedtimes.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **Granted** מודה ביתרון (**more time in bed**), והמילה **but** מציגה ניגוד: אם הנערים הולכים לישון מאוחר יותר, היתרון מתבטל, ולכן התשובה **neutralized** (מנוטרל, מבוטל).

_**Granted** admits a benefit, but teenagers who **go to sleep an hour later each night** lose it, so the benefit is **neutralized** (canceled out)._

questionText: Reports about rare illnesses are meant to reassure the public that the risk is small, but because their vivid details stay in the mind, such reports can actually ________ people's fear.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** והמילה **actually** מסמנות שהתוצאה הפוכה מהכוונה (**meant to reassure the public**), והסיבה **their vivid details stay in the mind** מראה שהפחד גדל, ולכן התשובה היא **magnify** (להגדיל, להעצים).

_**But** and **actually** reverse the intention (**meant to reassure the public**), and **their vivid details stay in the mind**, so the reports **magnify** (enlarge) the fear._

questionText: A childhood nickname often means little to the adult who carries it, yet it can be remarkably ________: even when the person has changed completely, old friends tend to keep using it for decades.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנקודתיים מסבירים את החסר: גם כשהאדם השתנה לגמרי (**even when the person has changed completely**), חברים ותיקים ממשיכים להשתמש בכינוי עשרות שנים, ולכן הכינוי הוא **persistent** (מתמיד, עמיד בפני שינוי).

_The colon explains the blank: even when the person **has changed completely**, old friends **keep using it for decades**, so the nickname is **persistent** (long-lasting)._

questionText: Unlike the old campus in the city center, the new campus, set in a salubrious valley, lacks basic ________, such as a café, a bank and a pharmacy.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **such as a café, a bank and a pharmacy** נותן דוגמאות לחסר, והמילה **Unlike** מראה שבקמפוס החדש חסר מה שיש בקמפוס הישן, ולכן התשובה היא **amenities** (מתקני נוחות ושירותי עזר).

_**Such as a café, a bank and a pharmacy** gives examples of what **Unlike** says the new campus lacks, so the word is **amenities** (useful facilities and services)._

questionText: Contrary to predictions that television would make speakers from disparate regions sound alike, regional accents have proved ________: young people in many towns proudly keep the sounds of their hometown.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Contrary to predictions** והנקודתיים (**proudly keep the sounds of their hometown**) מראים שהמבטאים אינם נעלמים, ולכן התשובה היא **resilient** (חסין, שורד).

_**Contrary to predictions** and the colon (**proudly keep the sounds of their hometown**) show that accents did not disappear, so they are **resilient** (able to survive)._

questionText: While a stand-up comedian can deliver a sardonic joke in plain words, a mime has no voice at all and must ________ the same joke through gestures and facial expressions.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **While** מעמידה קומיקאי שמוסר בדיחה במילים מול פנטומימאי שאין לו קול כלל (**has no voice at all**), ולכן הוא חייב להעביר (**convey**) את הבדיחה דרך תנועות והבעות פנים.

_**While** contrasts a comedian who uses plain words with a mime who **has no voice at all**, so the mime must **convey** (express) the joke through gestures and expressions._

questionText: Admittedly, volunteer fire crews are cheap to run, but they have a problem on weekdays: when an alarm sounds, many of the volunteers are ________ because they are at their jobs, far from the station.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **but** מציגה בעיה מול היתרון (**cheap to run**), והמשפט הסיבתי **they are at their jobs, far from the station** מסביר שהמתנדבים אינם נמצאים, ולכן התשובה היא **absent** (נעדרים).

_**But** introduces a problem against the advantage (**cheap to run**), and **they are at their jobs, far from the station** explains that many volunteers are **absent** (not there)._

questionText: The messaging app is convenient, yet its constant notifications can be distracting, so many users choose to ________ them during the working day.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילה **yet** מציגה ניגוד ליתרון (**convenient**), והמילה **so** מראה תוצאה של ההפרעה (**distracting**): המשתמשים בוחרים לכבות את ההתראות, ולכן התשובה היא **deactivate** (לבטל, לכבות).

_**Yet** contrasts the app's convenience with a problem (**distracting**), and **so** gives the result: users choose to turn the notifications off, that is, **deactivate** them._

questionText: Although doctors have advised people for years to eat less salt, the habit of adding it to every meal remains deeply ________ in many households.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף הקבוע **deeply ingrained** מתאר הרגל שהשתרש, והמילה **Although** מראה שההרגל נשאר למרות שנים של עצות (**doctors have advised people for years**), ולכן התשובה היא **ingrained** (מושרש).

_**Although** shows that the habit survives years of advice (**doctors have advised people for years**), and **deeply ingrained** is the fixed phrase for a habit that is hard to change._

questionText: Once pictured as a slow, clumsy creature, the reptile is now thought to have been highly ________, because the newly found skeleton has long legs and unusually light bones.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Once pictured as a slow, clumsy creature** מציג את התמונה הישנה, והמילה **now** עם הסיבה **long legs and unusually light bones** מראים תמונה הפוכה, ולכן הזוחל היה **agile** (זריז, קל תנועה).

_**Once pictured as a slow, clumsy creature** gives the old view, and **now** plus **long legs and unusually light bones** reverse it, so the reptile was **agile** (quick)._

questionText: Though blamed for the summer miasma that leaves Caribbean islanders coughing, dust blown across the Atlantic from the Sahara also ________ the Amazon rainforest, whose poor soils would otherwise lack phosphorus.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילים **Though** ו-**also** מסמנות שהאבק גם מועיל, והוא מספק זרחן שהקרקע הייתה חסרה בלעדיו (**would otherwise lack phosphorus**), ולכן התשובה היא **enriches** (מעשיר).

_**Though** and **also** signal a benefit, and soils that **would otherwise lack phosphorus** gain it from the dust, so the dust **enriches** (adds nutrients to) the rainforest._

questionText: Essays written by hand in a timed exam often contain small ________, such as a doubled 'the' or a dropped letter, which many graders forgive as signs of haste rather than of ignorance.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הדוגמה **a doubled 'the'** (מילה שהוכפלה) והדוגמה **a dropped letter** (אות שנשמטה) הן שני סוגים שונים של טעויות, ורק המילה **lapses** (שגיאות קטנות מהיסח הדעת) מכסה את שתיהן.

_**A doubled 'the'** adds a word and **a dropped letter** removes one, so only **lapses** (small slips of attention) covers both examples._

questionText: Decades of salt spray and winter gales have taken their ________ on the town's storied pier: its planks have rotted, its railings have rusted through, and last spring it was closed to visitors.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המילים **have taken their** שלפני החסר והמילה **on** שאחריו יוצרות רק עם המילה **toll** את הצירוף הקבוע **take a toll on** (לגבות מחיר כבד, לגרום נזק מצטבר).

_Only **toll** completes the fixed phrase take a toll on (cause gradual damage), which matches the planks that **have rotted** and the rusted railings._

questionText: After twenty summers of guiding tourists to the same waterfall, the ranger had grown ________: she still agreed with every glowing word in the guidebook, yet the roaring cascade no longer stirred her.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפקחית עדיין מסכימה עם כל מילת שבח (**still agreed with every glowing word**), אבל המפל כבר לא מרגש אותה (**no longer stirred her**), ולכן התשובה היא **jaded** (שהתרגשותו קהתה מרוב היכרות).

_She **still agreed with every glowing word**, yet the cascade **no longer stirred her**: twenty summers had made her **jaded** (dulled by overexposure)._

questionText: Asked whether the old house's roof had ever leaked, the real-estate agent ________ without a moment's hesitation, praising the sunny garden and the newly painted kitchen but never answering yes or no.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הסוכן דיבר בלי היסוס (**without a moment's hesitation**) אבל לא ענה על השאלה (**never answering yes or no**), ולכן התשובה היא **prevaricated** (התחמק, דיבר בעקיפין כדי לא לענות).

_He spoke **without a moment's hesitation** but dodged the question, **never answering yes or no**, so he **prevaricated** (spoke evasively)._

questionText: Far from breaking the supermarket's one-coupon-per-customer rule, the wily bargain hunters merely ________ it, sending a cousin, an aunt and a neighbor to the checkout with one coupon each.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף **Far from breaking** אומר שהם לא הפרו את הכלל אלא שלחו קרובי משפחה עם קופון לכל אחד, ולכן התשובה היא **sidestepped** (עקפו את הכלל בלי להפר אותו).

_**Far from breaking** the rule, they sent relatives **with one coupon each**, so they **sidestepped** it (got around it without breaking it)._

questionText: Why does the same side of the Moon always face the Earth?

options.label: The Earth spins once during each orbit the Moon makes
The Moon moves around the Earth much faster than it spins
The Moon completes one spin per trip around the Earth
The Moon does not spin, so one side is always fixed toward us

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט it turns exactly once in the time it takes to circle the Earth (הוא מסתובב פעם אחת בדיוק בזמן שלוקח לו להקיף את כדור הארץ), הסיבוב של הירח תואם את המסלול שלו, ולכן אותו צד תמיד פונה אלינו.

_The Moon turns exactly once in the time it takes to circle the Earth, so its spin and its orbit match and one side always faces us._

questionText: Which common assumption does the professor correct?

options.label: That mountaintops are made of the oldest rock on Earth
That shells can slowly harden into solid rock
That the ocean once climbed as high as the peaks
That huge waves once threw sea creatures onto high ground

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף But actually מופיע המשפט sea level never rose anywhere near that far (מפלס הים מעולם לא עלה כל כך גבוה), ולכן הפרופסור מתקן את ההנחה שהאוקיינוס כיסה פעם את ההרים.

_After But actually, he says sea level never rose anywhere near that far, which corrects the idea that the ocean once covered the peaks._

questionText: According to the professor, how did the shells end up high in the mountains?

options.label: The land was thrust upward as two plates collided
The sea slowly dried up and left the shells on high ground
The shells hardened into rock in the mud of a shallow sea
Powerful floods carried the shells up to the peaks

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט the land itself moved (הקרקע עצמה זזה) מוסבר בהמשך במשפט the crumpled land was pushed upward (האדמה המקומטת נדחפה כלפי מעלה), ולכן הצדפות עלו יחד עם הסלע.

_After the land itself moved, he explains that the crumpled land was pushed upward, so the shells rose together with the rock._

questionText: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.label: Competing theories on how dogs and people became partners
Why early hunters raised wolf pups and bred the tamest ones
How ancient bones reveal exactly when dogs split from wolves
How people first learned to domesticate many wild animals

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף two main explanations (שני הסברים עיקריים) והמשפט the origin of dogs remains unsettled (מקור הכלבים עדיין לא הוכרע) מראים שההרצאה עוסקת בהסברים מתחרים להתחלת הקשר בין האדם לכלב.

_The phrases two main explanations and the origin of dogs remains unsettled show that the lecture is about rival theories of how the partnership began._

questionText: What does the lecturer suggest about the two explanations?

options.label: Ancient bones probably favor the first explanation over the second
The second explanation is now accepted by most researchers
Each may describe part of what really happened
The two explanations may be too different to be combined

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט the truth combines both stories (האמת משלבת את שני הסיפורים), כל אחד משני ההסברים עשוי לתאר חלק ממה שקרה באמת.

_The lecturer says many researchers suspect that the truth combines both stories, so each explanation may describe part of what happened._

questionText: Why does ice float on liquid water?

options.label: Air trapped inside the ice lifts it up above the surface
Water gets denser as it freezes, just like most liquids do
Ice holds less material in the same space than liquid does
Ice forms at the surface, so it has no chance to sink

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט ice takes up more room than the same amount of liquid (קרח תופס יותר מקום מאותה כמות של נוזל), הקרח פחות צפוף מהמים הנוזליים, ולכן הוא צף.

_Since ice takes up more room than the same amount of liquid, it is less dense, so it floats._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what is the true cost of a choice?

options.label: What the single best rejected option was worth
The combined value of the options that were passed over
The money someone pays for the option they pick
The hours someone spends on the activity they pick

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט It is the value of the best alternative you give up (זהו הערך של החלופה הטובה ביותר שמוותרים עליה) מגדיר את העלות האמיתית, והמשפט the real cost is the next best thing you didn't choose חוזר על כך בסיכום.

_The lecturer defines the true cost as the value of the best alternative you give up, and repeats it as the next best thing you didn't choose._

questionText: How does the lecturer answer the objection that the idea makes everything sound expensive?

options.label: By admitting that the idea works for money but not for time
By saying it helps people weigh choices, not avoid them
By agreeing that people should avoid choices that have a cost
By claiming that the cost of a choice is mostly its money price

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המילה But מופיע המשפט the idea is a tool for comparing choices, not a reason to avoid them (הרעיון הוא כלי להשוואת בחירות ולא סיבה להימנע מהן), ולכן ההתנגדות נדחית.

_After But, the lecturer says the idea is a tool for comparing choices, not a reason to avoid them, which answers the objection._

questionText: What are the two students mainly doing?

options.label: Planning how to run a fair plant experiment
Arguing about how many plants their lab can afford to grow
Deciding which fertilizer will help bean plants grow best
Reviewing the results of an experiment they already finished

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף Control group, one variable, random placement (קבוצת ביקורת, משתנה אחד, שיבוץ אקראי) מסכם את מה שהם מתכננים: ניסוי הוגן.

_They are planning a fair test, as the summary Control group, one variable, random placement shows._

questionText: How does the man respond to the idea of a control group?

options.label: He supports it immediately and adds reasons of his own
He accepts it because their professor requires it
He rejects it throughout and keeps his own design
He objects at first but accepts it once she explains

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט Isn't it a waste? (האם זה לא בזבוז?) מראה התנגדות בתחילה, והמשפט I'm convinced (השתכנעתי) בסוף מראה שהוא קיבל את הרעיון אחרי ההסבר שלה.

_He first asks Isn't it a waste?, but after her explanation he says I'm convinced._

questionText: Why does the teaching assistant say the survey result is unreliable?

options.label: Too few students answered the survey
Those who replied were not typical of all students
The questions were worded to push students toward praising the library
Going online made students answer quickly and without much care

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המשפט Size isn't the issue (הגודל אינו הבעיה) בא המשפט mostly people who already use the library bothered to reply (בעיקר מי שכבר משתמשים בספרייה טרחו לענות), ולכן המשיבים אינם מייצגים את כל הסטודנטים.

_After Size isn't the issue, she explains that mostly people who already use the library bothered to reply, so the answers are biased._

questionText: How does the woman's view differ from the man's opening claim?

options.label: She thinks reformers used the press more cleverly than the authorities did
She sees the press as speeding up an upheaval that had other roots
She thinks the press had no influence on how ideas spread to readers
She thinks the pamphlets reached too few people to make a difference

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף a catalyst, not a cause (זרז ולא סיבה) והמשפט the fuel was already there (הדלק כבר היה שם) מראים שלדעתה הדפוס רק האיץ תסיסה שהיו לה שורשים אחרים.

_She calls the press a catalyst, not a cause and says the fuel was already there, so it only sped up an upheaval with other roots._

questionText: Why does the man say that authorities could not suppress ideas that spread fast?

options.label: To suggest that the authorities probably lost control before the press arrived
To admit that the press did not matter much in the end
To explain why pamphlets were cheap enough for ordinary readers
To suggest that fast spreading was significant in itself

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף But then מופיע המשפט maybe speed itself mattered (אולי המהירות עצמה הייתה חשובה), כלומר הגבר טוען שההתפשטות המהירה הייתה משמעותית כשלעצמה.

_After But then, he says maybe speed itself mattered, which means he thinks the fast spread was important in its own right._

questionText: What is the lecturer mainly explaining?

options.label: How water travels between the sea, the sky and the land
How rain slowly dissolves minerals out of the rocks on land
Why seawater keeps getting saltier as the years pass
How rivers and evaporation account for salty seawater

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט rivers deliver the minerals, and evaporation leaves the salt behind (נהרות מביאים את המינרלים וההתאדות משאירה את המלח) מסכם שההרצאה מסבירה את מליחות הים באמצעות נהרות והתאדות.

_The summary rivers deliver the minerals, and evaporation leaves the salt behind shows that the lecture explains the sea's saltiness through rivers and evaporation._

questionText: According to the lecturer, why does the sea not simply get saltier year after year?

options.label: Some minerals are removed by living things or by sinking
Each river carries so little that the sea hardly changes
Melting ice sends fresh water into the sea and dilutes it
Evaporation takes the salt out of the water

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המילים Not necessarily (לא בהכרח) המשפט Some of the minerals are used by living things or settle to the seafloor (חלק מהמינרלים נצרכים על ידי יצורים חיים או שוקעים לקרקעית הים) מסביר למה המליחות נשארת יציבה.

_After Not necessarily, she says Some of the minerals are used by living things or settle to the seafloor, so the saltiness stays roughly steady._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what turns a pidgin into a creole?

options.label: Children learn it from infancy as their home language
The traders who use it give it a richer grammar
Groups from different places adopt it for trade
Scholars write down its rules and teach them in schools

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המרצה עונה על השאלה what turns a pidgin into a creole? במילה Children ומסכמת שקריאולית היא פידג'ין שהפך לשפת אם (mother tongue).

_The lecturer answers what turns a pidgin into a creole? with Children and sums up that a creole has become someone's mother tongue._

questionText: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.label: How something noticed among farm workers led to a way of preventing disease
Why doctors finally gave up the older and riskier method of fighting smallpox
How farmers in the countryside protected their cows from catching smallpox
Why milkmaids were more likely than other workers to catch cowpox from cows

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המרצה פותח בצירוף not in a laboratory but on a farm ומסכם שמחלת פרות קלה יכולה להגן מפני מחלה אנושית קטלנית (a mild cow disease could protect people against a deadly human one).

_The talk begins not in a laboratory but on a farm and ends with the point that a mild cow disease could protect people against a deadly human one._

questionText: According to the lecturer, how was the country doctor's method different from the older defense?

options.label: It took material from a person who had a mild case of smallpox
It used a mild disease caught from cows rather than smallpox itself
It was first tried out on a large group of milkmaids in the countryside
It could be given safely by farm workers without a doctor present

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בשיטה הישנה השתמשו בחומר מפצע של אבעבועות שחורות (a smallpox sore), ואילו הרופא לקח חומר מפצע של אבעבועות הפרות (a cowpox sore), מחלה קלה שעוברת מפרות.

_The older defense used material from a smallpox sore, while the doctor took material from a cowpox sore, a mild illness passed on by cows._

questionText: By the end of the conversation, what is the man's view of the woman's explanation?

options.label: He rejects her arguments and still blames bad luck
He accepts her two arguments but adds that context can matter
He accepts her arguments and concludes that the field itself is broken
He agrees with her about journals but doubts what she says about samples

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הגבר מודה במשפט I'll grant you both points (אני מקבל את שתי הטענות), ומיד מסייג במשפט An effect might be real and still depend on the setting (אפקט יכול להיות אמיתי ועדיין להיות תלוי בהקשר).

_He says I'll grant you both points and then qualifies them: An effect might be real and still depend on the setting._

questionText: What conclusion do the two researchers reach?

options.label: A failed replication shows that the original study was probably wrong
Psychology should stop relying on studies that were run in other countries
Samples should be larger, and studies finding no effect should be published
Journals should publish fewer of the studies that report exciting new effects

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הגבר מסכם במשפט we need bigger samples, and we need to publish the studies that find nothing, too (מדגמים גדולים יותר ופרסום גם של מחקרים שלא מצאו דבר), והאישה מסכימה.

_He concludes we need bigger samples, and we need to publish the studies that find nothing, too, and she replies On that, we agree._

questionText: According to the lecturer, why did Renaissance painters adopt linear perspective?

options.label: To make clear which people in a scene were the most important
To make a painted surface look like a view into real space
To make the buildings in their scenes look larger and grander
To work faster by following one fixed rule in each painting

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המשפט Renaissance painters wanted something different המרצה מתאר חלון אל מרחב אמיתי (a window onto real space) ומסכם במשפט perspective let them create depth on a flat surface.

_After wanted something different, the lecturer says they wanted a window onto real space and sums up that perspective let them create depth on a flat surface._

questionText: Why does the professor mention the cells in the student's body?

options.label: To challenge his claim that new parts make a new thing
To show that his memories matter more than his body
To argue that he is no longer the person he was as a child
To explain why ships and living bodies change in different ways

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפרופסורית שואלת את השאלה Are you a different person from the child you once were? כדי לערער על הטענה it's simply not the same ship anymore (זו כבר לא אותה ספינה).

_She asks Are you a different person from the child you once were? to challenge his claim that it's simply not the same ship anymore._

questionText: What does the professor suggest about the ship puzzle at the end?

options.label: Philosophers now agree that the rebuilt ship is the real one
Since it has no clear answer, it is not really worth discussing
It can be settled once we know which of the planks are the oldest
Its value lies in making people ask what being the same means

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הפרופסורית אומרת במשפט The point isn't to settle it ומוסיפה שהמטרה היא לשאול מה פירוש להיות אותו דבר (what we really mean when we call something the same).

_She says The point isn't to settle it but to ask what we really mean when we call something the same._

questionText: What is the main point of the lecture?

options.label: Sea otters became rare in many areas because they were hunted for fur
An animal that is not plentiful can still hold its community together
Kelp forests depend more on water temperature than on any animal
The most numerous species in a habitat usually has the most influence

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המרצה מדגישה את המשפט Otters are not especially numerous ומסכמת שלמין מפתח יש השפעה גדולה בהרבה ממספרו (whose influence is far larger than its numbers would suggest).

_She stresses that Otters are not especially numerous and sums up a keystone species as an animal whose influence is far larger than its numbers would suggest._

questionText: According to the lecturer, why did kelp largely disappear in some areas?

options.label: Storms and warm water killed off the otters, letting urchins spread
With fewer otters to eat them, urchins multiplied and grazed it away
Hunters took the urchins as well, leaving the kelp with no defenders
Returning otters disturbed the kelp while diving for urchins

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המרצה מסבירה שהלוטרות אוכלות קיפודי ים, ולפי המשפט When otters were hunted almost to extinction for their fur, urchin numbers exploded הקיפודים התרבו ויער האצות נעלם.

_Otters eat urchins, so When otters were hunted almost to extinction for their fur, urchin numbers exploded, and the urchins stripped the kelp._

questionText: What does the lecturer suggest about the drivers' brains?

options.label: They were probably born with an unusual gift for remembering places
Learning the streets seems to have physically altered their brains
Their brains stayed fixed, but they learned to use them more efficiently
Their memory for places grew at the cost of other kinds of memory

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המרצה השינוי מופיע במהלך האימון עצמו (during training itself, not before), על השאלה אם נולדו כך הוא עונה בצירוף Probably not, ומסכם במשפט practice can physically reshape it (אימון יכול לשנות אותו פיזית).

_The change appears during training itself, not before, inborn talent gets a Probably not, and the lecturer concludes that practice can physically reshape it._

questionText: What is the main point of the lecture?

options.label: People in a crowd simply care less about strangers than people alone do
Each person in a crowd feels less responsible, not less concerned
A larger crowd usually means that help arrives more quickly
Pointing at one person is the main way to get a crowd to help

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המרצה מסכמת במשפט a crowd doesn't remove our concern; it spreads our sense of responsibility thin (הקהל לא מבטל את הדאגה אלא מפזר את תחושת האחריות).

_The lecturer sums up: a crowd doesn't remove our concern; it spreads our sense of responsibility thin._

questionText: According to the lecturer, which situation is likely to weaken the bystander effect?

options.label: The crowd is very large and is made up mostly of strangers
One onlooker is picked out and personally asked to get help
The person who fainted looks as if they are only slightly unwell
Each onlooker waits to see how worried the other people seem

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המרצה צעד אחד עוזר במיוחד: להצביע על אדם אחד ולבקש ממנו ישירות לקרוא לעזרה (pointing at a single person and asking them directly to call for help).

_One step seems to help a lot: pointing at a single person and asking them directly to call for help._

questionText: According to the woman, why does widening a road often fail to reduce traffic?

options.label: Faster trips lead people to drive more than they used to
Construction closes lanes for years and causes new jams
A growing population fills the extra lanes with new residents
Drivers avoid the new lanes because they must pay to use them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האישה מסבירה במשפט When a road gets faster, people change their behavior (כשהנסיעה בכביש מתקצרת, אנשים משנים את התנהגותם), ולמשל מי שנסע ברכבת מתחיל לנהוג (start driving).

_She explains that When a road gets faster, people change their behavior: train riders start driving and others make trips they used to skip._

questionText: How has the man's view changed by the end of the discussion?

options.label: He still thinks widening the highway would cut the morning jams
He now regards managing road use as more important than adding lanes
He now believes new roads cannot be justified even in growing regions
He now thinks buses alone can end the city's morning traffic problem

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הגבר מודה במשפט Then maybe I've been asking the wrong question ומסיק שהשאלה האמיתית היא איך מנהלים את הכביש (the real issue is how we manage it).

_He admits maybe I've been asking the wrong question and concludes that the real issue is how we manage it, not how much road we build._

questionText: What point does the woman add to the man's explanation?

options.label: The warm particles meet one another more often than cold ones
A larger share of the collisions carry enough energy to react
How often particles collide matters more than how hard they hit
Heating may loosen the bonds before the particles even meet

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף it can't be the whole story (זה לא כל ההסבר) היא אומרת את המשפט More of the collisions are energetic enough to actually break bonds, כלומר יותר התנגשויות חזקות מספיק כדי לשבור קשרים.

_After it can't be the whole story, she adds that More of the collisions are energetic enough to actually break bonds._

questionText: How does the man's view change during the discussion?

options.label: He drops his doubts and treats the planet as firmly established
He keeps arguing that a dip this small may be meaningless
He now favors a planet but still wants another test
He comes to think a dark spot on the star probably caused the dip

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט a regular repeat does make a planet the likeliest explanation (ההסבר הסביר ביותר) והמשפט I'd still want an independent check מראים שהוא משתכנע, אבל רק בחלקו.

_He concedes that a regular repeat does make a planet the likeliest explanation, yet adds I'd still want an independent check._

questionText: According to the woman, what makes the planet explanation convincing?

options.label: The dip was deeper than a dark spot on a star could produce
The star was also seen to wobble as the planet circled it
A single dip is enough when the star is otherwise steady
The dip recurred on a steady schedule, the same each time

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף But look at what the authors did היא מתארת ירידה באור הכוכב שחוזרת במרווחים סדירים לגמרי (at perfectly regular intervals), ומסכמת במשפט It's the repetition that makes the case.

_She stresses a dip seen at perfectly regular intervals with the same depth and shape, and sums up: It's the repetition that makes the case._

questionText: What is the main point of the lecture?

options.label: Equal steps trade pure intervals for the freedom to play in any key
Pure fifths work well as long as the player stays in one key
Equal steps won out because they make the intervals sound pure
Over time, listeners learned to hear slightly sour intervals as pure

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט equal tuning wasn't chosen because it's perfect והצירוף spreading a small error evenly (פיזור טעות קטנה באופן שווה) מראים שזו פשרה: מוותרים על טוהר המרווחים כדי לנגן בכל סולם.

_The lecturer says equal tuning wasn't chosen because it's perfect; it works by spreading a small error evenly so every key is usable._

questionText: Why does the lecturer mention singers and violinists?

options.label: To show that string players were the first to accept equal steps
To point out that keyboards, unlike them, cannot correct pitch
To suggest that pure intervals are easier to sing than to play
To explain why some musicians objected to the new tuning

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** מיד אחרי הזמר והכנר, שיכולים לתקן כל צליל, בא המשפט A keyboard can't; its pitches are fixed (הצלילים קבועים), ולכן הם מוזכרים כניגוד לקלידים.

_Right after singers and violinists comes A keyboard can't; its pitches are fixed, so they are mentioned as a contrast to keyboards._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what allows researchers to date a wooden beam?

options.label: Counting how many rings the beam contains from its center outward
Matching its order of thick and thin rings to a record
Comparing how wet or dry the wood itself has become
Measuring the beam's width against trees growing today

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף In short בא המשפט it's the sequence of wide and narrow rings, not simply their number, that dates the wood (הרצף של טבעות רחבות וצרות, ולא רק מספרן, הוא שמאפשר לתארך את העץ).

_After In short, she says it's the sequence of wide and narrow rings, not simply their number, that dates the wood._

questionText: What is the lecturer's main point?

options.label: Proportional voting tends to produce weak, short-lived governments
Voters prefer the large party closest to their own views
Counting rules can steer a country toward two main parties
Regional parties manage to win seats despite the voting rules

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט המסכם the rules of counting shape the number of parties (כללי הספירה קובעים את מספר המפלגות) מראה שהנושא הוא איך שיטת הבחירה דוחפת לשתי מפלגות גדולות.

_He sums up with the rules of counting shape the number of parties, after showing how support drifts to two large parties._

questionText: Why does the lecturer mention regional parties?

options.label: To give the clearest case of small parties losing out
To admit that the pattern he describes has exceptions
To suggest that proportional systems favor regional voters
To explain why voters desert small national parties

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט this is a tendency, not an iron law (זו נטייה, לא חוק ברזל) בא רגע לפני המפלגות האזוריות, ולכן הן מוזכרות כחריג לדפוס.

_He first says this is a tendency, not an iron law, then offers Regional parties, for instance as the exception._

questionText: How does the student's view change during the conversation?

options.label: She decides that early factory work may have left families poorer
She concludes that the wage figures she relied on were inaccurate
She sees that higher pay alone may not prove people lived better
She starts to doubt that living standards rose even in the long run

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט I suppose I was treating income as if it were the whole story (התייחסתי להכנסה כאילו היא כל הסיפור) מראה שהיא מבינה ששכר גבוה יותר לבדו אינו מוכיח רווחה.

_She admits I suppose I was treating income as if it were the whole story, so higher wages alone no longer settle the question for her._

questionText: What can be inferred about the professor's position?

options.label: He holds that ordinary families plainly grew poorer in those decades
He suspects the early gains were smaller than wages suggest
He considers height a more reliable guide than wages to well-being
He believes the long-run rise in living standards is still uncertain

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** השאלה Must they? והמשפט the gains in the first few decades look rather thin (הרווחים בעשורים הראשונים נראים דלים) מרמזים שהוא מפקפק בגודל השיפור המוקדם.

_His Must they? and the gains in the first few decades look rather thin imply doubt about the size of the early improvement._

questionText: According to the lecturer, why does the sky look blue?

options.label: The air itself has a faint blue color of its own
Air molecules spread blue light around more than red light
Sunlight contains more blue light than any other color
Most red light is soaked up by the air before it can reach our eyes

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** לפי המשפט they scatter short wavelengths, the blue end of the spectrum, far more strongly than long, red ones, מולקולות האוויר מפזרות אור כחול הרבה יותר מאור אדום.

_The molecules scatter short wavelengths, the blue end of the spectrum, far more strongly than long, red ones, so blue light reaches us from everywhere._

questionText: What does the man suggest about the evidence for a bilingual advantage?

options.label: Larger and more careful studies have disproved the effect
Published results may make the effect look stronger than it is
The effect shows up most clearly when the tasks are harder
Bilingual people may differ too much from one another to be studied

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט Studies that find no difference are less likely to get published והמשפט the record we see may flatter the hypothesis (מחמיא להשערה) מראים שהאפקט עשוי להיראות גדול מכפי שהוא באמת.

_He notes that Studies that find no difference are less likely to get published, so the record we see may flatter the hypothesis._

questionText: How does the woman's position change?

options.label: She concludes that the advantage is real but rather small
She stops believing that knowing two languages has real value
She shifts from accepting the claim to seeing it as unsettled
She keeps defending the claim by blaming tasks that are too easy

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** בסוף היא אומרת את המשפט Whether it trains some general thinking muscle is still open (השאלה עדיין פתוחה), אחרי שבהתחלה אמרה על הטענה את המילים it makes sense (זה הגיוני).

_She begins with it makes sense but ends with Whether it trains some general thinking muscle is still open._

questionText: What is the lecturer's main point?

options.label: Doctors resisted mainly because they were too proud to change
The resistance had understandable causes beyond mere stubbornness
The germ idea spread quickly once microscopes revealed tiny organisms
Physicians dismissed germs simply because no evidence for them existed

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי הצירוף to restate the point בא המשפט the resistance was not simple foolishness (ההתנגדות לא נבעה מטיפשות פשוטה), ושלושת הנימוקים שבהרצאה מראים שלהתנגדות היו מניעים מובנים.

_She rejects plain stubbornness as too easy and restates that the resistance was not simple foolishness, giving three sensible reasons._

questionText: Why does the lecturer mention that cleaning up filthy districts reduced illness?

options.label: To suggest that the older theory was largely correct in the end
To explain why the older theory seemed persuasive in its day
To show that physicians already accepted the germ idea
To illustrate how doctors first spotted the microscopic culprits

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף seemed to work והצירוף though for reasons the theory got wrong (מסיבות שהתיאוריה טעתה בהן) מראים שהדוגמה מסבירה למה התיאוריה הישנה שכנעה, ולא שהתיאוריה צדקה.

_The old view seemed to work, but the cleanup helped for reasons the theory got wrong, so the example explains its appeal, not its truth._

questionText: According to the view the lecturer presents, what makes a theory scientific?

options.label: It must rest on a large and growing body of supporting evidence
It must be open to being contradicted by evidence
It must be broad enough to account for whatever is observed
It must already have been contradicted by at least one observation before it is accepted

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט there must be some possible observation that would show it to be false והצירוף whether it could be refuted (האם אפשר להפריך אותה) מראים שתאוריה מדעית חייבת להיות פתוחה להפרכה.

_The lecturer says there must be some possible observation that would show it to be false; what matters is whether it could be refuted._

questionText: What is the main point of the lecture?

options.label: Saving by households is the main cause of most economic downturns
A household's wise decision can become harmful once it is widely copied
Families ought to spend more and save less whenever hard times are expected
Shops and firms respond to falling sales by cutting jobs and working hours

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפט הסיכום what is prudent for one family can, when everyone does it, deepen a downturn for all (מה שנבון למשפחה אחת עלול, כשכולם נוהגים כך, להעמיק את המיתון של כולם) מבטא את הרעיון המרכזי.

_The restatement what is prudent for one family can, when everyone does it, deepen a downturn for all gives the main point._

questionText: Why does the lecturer mention whether the extra savings are invested?

options.label: To suggest that most economists regard the paradox as mistaken
To indicate that the strength of the effect depends on other factors
To explain how a careful family should decide where to keep its extra savings
To show that investing, unlike saving, is what causes downturns

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט not every economist accepts the strongest form of this argument והצירוף much depends (הרבה תלוי) מראים שעוצמת האפקט תלויה בתנאים נוספים.

_He says not every economist accepts the strongest form of this argument and that much depends on investment, so the effect's strength varies._

questionText: How does the man's view change during the discussion?

options.label: He concludes that what the poet intended has no bearing on what a poem means
He comes to treat the poet's aims as evidence to weigh rather than the final word
He decides that each reader's own response is what defines a poem's meaning
He holds on to the view that the poet's letters should settle any dispute about meaning

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המשפט let me revise what I said הוא מכנה את כוונת המשורר בצירוף a strong clue (רמז חזק) ומודה במשפט it can't be the final test (זה לא המבחן הסופי).

_After let me revise what I said, he calls intention a strong clue but grants it can't be the final test._

questionText: What do the two speakers seem to agree on by the end?

options.label: The poet's intention should be the final test of any reading
The poem's own words should limit which readings are acceptable
A poem may fairly mean whatever a careful reader finds in it
A poet's letters and drafts are better evidence than the poem itself

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האישה אומרת במשפט they're wrong because the words on the page don't support them (פרשנויות כאלה שגויות כי הטקסט אינו תומך בהן), והגבר מסכם במשפט we're closer than we sounded.

_She says bad readings fail because the words on the page don't support them, and he concludes we're closer than we sounded._

questionText: What point do the speakers arrive at about the hospital ranking?

options.label: Survival rates may be too unreliable to compare hospitals in any way
The combined rate may reflect the patient mix more than the quality of care
The suburban hospital gives better care to patients who arrive seriously ill
Seriously ill patients should be sent to the hospital with the higher overall rate

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט the overall number may tell us more about who comes through the door than about the care itself מראה שהשיעור הכולל עשוי לשקף יותר את סוג המטופלים (מי נכנס בדלת) מאשר את איכות הטיפול.

_She concludes that the overall number may tell us more about who comes through the door than about the care itself._

questionText: Why does the professor mention that people invent or borrow words?

options.label: To argue that translating between languages rarely works well
To show why the strong version is hard to defend
To explain how the weaker version of the idea came about
To suggest that vocabulary matters more than grammar in shaping thought

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי המשפט If it were true, translation would be nearly impossible היא מוסיפה את המשפט people invent or borrow words all the time, כדי להראות שהגרסה החזקה לא מחזיקה מעמד.

_She says If it were true, translation would be nearly impossible, yet people invent or borrow words all the time._

questionText: What is the professor's view of the weaker version?

options.label: It shows that some languages leave speakers unable to tell certain colors apart
It has support from evidence that speakers notice things slightly differently
It is now rejected by most researchers, just like the strong version
It rests more on popular slogans than on the results of experiments

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף real but modest והמשפט they nudge attention rather than set limits (הם מכוונים את תשומת הלב ולא מציבים גבולות) מראים שהראיות מצביעות על הבדלים קטנים בלבד.

_She calls the effects real but modest and says they nudge attention rather than set limits._

questionText: What is the lecture mainly about?

options.label: Why drilling is still the most dependable way to study the deep Earth
How indirect clues revealed what lies at the center of the planet
How movements of molten metal deep inside the planet set off earthquakes
Why some kinds of earthquake wave do more damage at the surface than others

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפט הסיכום no one has seen the core; its structure was inferred from how waves bend, slow down, or vanish (המבנה הוסק מהתנהגות הגלים) מבטא את הרעיון המרכזי.

_The restatement no one has seen the core; its structure was inferred from how waves bend, slow down, or vanish gives the main idea._

questionText: What led scientists to conclude that part of the core is liquid?

options.label: Faint signals pointed to a smaller region at the very center
Waves that cannot cross liquid were missing on the planet's far side
Drilling eventually reached deep enough to bring up traces of molten metal
Earthquake waves of both kinds traveled faster through the molten metal

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט The other kind can travel only through solid rock והמשפט this second kind simply never showed up מראים שהיעדר הגלים בצד הרחוק העיד על נוזל.

_The second kind can travel only through solid rock, and on the far side it simply never showed up._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what has not yet been settled about these animals?

options.label: Whether these animals live much longer than most other species
Whether these animals avoid aging or merely decline too slowly to notice
Why the risk of dying rises steadily with age in most other animals, including humans
How these animals manage to switch off the process of aging

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט Researchers are unsure whether these animals truly stop aging or simply age too slowly for studies to detect מראה שהשאלה היא אם ההזדקנות נעדרת או רק איטית מאוד.

_The lecturer says Researchers are unsure whether these animals truly stop aging or simply age too slowly for studies to detect._

questionText: What is the lecturer's main point?

options.label: Fire played no part in the library's long decline
The library's loss was probably a slow process rather than a sudden event
The library was probably destroyed in a single night of fire
Its leading scholars left because the library's old scrolls had begun to crumble

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** משפט הסיכום less a single catastrophe than a long, quiet decline (לא אסון יחיד אלא דעיכה ארוכה ושקטה) מבטא את הרעיון המרכזי של ההרצאה.

_The lecturer sums up that it was less a single catastrophe than a long, quiet decline._

questionText: Why does the lecturer mention that papyrus scrolls had to be recopied?

options.label: To explain why fire spread so quickly through the library's shelves
To give one example of how the collection was lost through neglect
To show that ancient scholars valued copying above writing new works
To suggest that most of the lost books survived in later copies

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט unless they were recopied, they simply crumbled מופיע ברשימת הסיבות, ואחריו בא הצירוף wasn't destroyed so much as neglected (לא הושמדה אלא הוזנחה), ולכן הפרט על המגילות הוא דוגמה להזנחה.

_The point unless they were recopied, they simply crumbled supports his claim that the library wasn't destroyed so much as neglected._

questionText: How does the woman's position change during the conversation?

options.label: She drops her concern that a higher wage floor can reduce employment
She accepts the evidence on modest raises but still doubts large ones
She comes to believe that firms mainly cover the cost by raising their prices
She keeps insisting that even small increases will mainly hurt young, low-skilled workers

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט I'll admit that's more persuasive than I expected מראה שהשתכנעה, אבל על קפיצה גדולה היא אומרת את הצירוף could be a different story (עשוי להיות סיפור אחר).

_She finds the evidence more persuasive than I expected, yet says a large jump could be a different story._

questionText: What do the two speakers end up agreeing on?

options.label: A higher minimum wage has no real effect on the number of jobs
How much a raise affects jobs depends mostly on its size and setting
Comparisons of neighboring regions cannot settle questions about wages
Lower staff turnover largely makes up for the cost of paying more

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** האישה אומרת את המשפט The real question is how high, and where (השאלה האמיתית היא כמה גבוה והיכן), והגבר עונה במשפט On that, I think we agree.

_She says The real question is how high, and where, and he replies On that, I think we agree._

questionText: What is the lecturer's main point?

options.label: Experts often teach poorly because they put little effort into explaining
Mastering an idea can make a beginner's confusion hard to imagine
Beginners can follow more easily when experts skip the obvious steps
Experts gradually forget the difficult ideas they once worked to learn

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט it becomes remarkably hard to recall what it felt like not to understand it (קשה מאוד להיזכר איך זה לא להבין) מראה שדווקא הידע מקשה לראות את הרעיון דרך עיניו של מתחיל.

_Once we understand an idea, it becomes remarkably hard to recall what it felt like not to understand it, so the expert loses the beginner's view._

questionText: Why does the man mention a copied chess game?

options.label: To show that copies are usually easy to tell apart from originals
To suggest that a copied work can earn as much admiration as the original
To show that knowing how a result was produced can alter its worth
To argue that games and paintings should be judged by separate standards

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט The moves wouldn't change, but we'd stop admiring it as original play (המהלכים לא ישתנו, אבל נפסיק להעריך את המשחק כמקורי) מראה שערך התוצאה משתנה כשיודעים איך היא הושגה.

_He says The moves wouldn't change, but we'd stop admiring it as original play, so learning a result's origin changes its value._

questionText: How does the woman's position change during the discussion?

options.label: She grants that a forgery's history lowers its value but not its beauty
She abandons the view that a forgery can give real visual pleasure
She convinces the man that a painting's worth depends on how it looks
She begins to doubt that a skilled fake could really fool the art experts

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף because of what we know about it, not because of anything we see (בגלל מה שאנחנו יודעים עליו, לא בגלל מה שרואים) מראה שהאישה מסכימה שהזיוף מאבד מערכו, אך לא מיופיו.

_She concedes the chess point but keeps the visual pleasure, concluding the forgery loses value because of what we know about it, not because of anything we see._

questionText: According to the lecturer, what did the methods that eventually worked have in common?

options.label: Each relied on events that astronomers observed far beyond the Earth
Each used a moving part to block and release a beam of light
Each depended on observers with quicker reflexes than before
Each overcame how little time light needs to cross short distances

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט the real problem was one of scale (הבעיה הייתה בקנה המידה) והצירוף it stretched the distance, or it sliced time into pieces fine enough to measure מראים ששתי השיטות התגברו על זמן המעבר הזעיר של האור.

_The lecturer says the real problem was one of scale, and each method either stretched the distance or sliced time into pieces fine enough to measure._

questionText: What is the lecturer's view of the lantern test?

options.label: He dismisses it as a naive test that told scientists very little
He credits it with showing that light has a definite speed
He regards its failure to find a delay as revealing in itself
He values it mainly as a study of human reaction times

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף I'd call it a clue (אני קורא לזה רמז), שבא מיד אחרי הצירוף easy to call that a failure, מראה שלדעת המרצה עצם היעדר העיכוב לימד משהו על האור.

_Right after easy to call that a failure, he says I'd call it a clue: finding no delay was itself informative._

questionText: What is the lecturer's view of the proposal she describes?

options.label: It is an established limit whose exact size is still debated
It is a thought-provoking idea that has yet to be firmly shown
It has largely been abandoned by researchers in the field
It explains why the number of friends people have varies so much

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט the limit is best seen as an intriguing hypothesis, not an established law (עדיף לראות בגבול השערה מסקרנת ולא חוק מבוסס) מראה שהרעיון מעניין אך עדיין לא הוכח.

_She concludes that the limit is best seen as an intriguing hypothesis, not an established law: interesting, but not yet proven._

questionText: What is the main point of the lecture?

options.label: People judge harm by its manner as well as its extent
People settle such dilemmas mainly by counting how many are spared
Philosophers agree that the second choice is morally worse
People are more willing to cause harm when they act directly

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט our judgments seem to track not just how much harm occurs, but how it comes about (נראה שהשיפוט שלנו תלוי לא רק בכמות הנזק אלא גם באופן שבו נגרם) מסכם את ההרצאה: גם הדרך שבה נגרם הנזק חשובה, ולא רק היקפו.

_He restates that our judgments seem to track not just how much harm occurs, but how it comes about._

questionText: What does the lecturer suggest about people's reaction to the second case?

options.label: It is a gut feeling that careful thinkers ought to override
It may reflect a real moral difference rather than a mere error
It shows that the number of people affected has no place in moral reasoning
It may fade once people notice that the numbers are identical

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף I'm not so sure וההבחנה בין נזק שהוא תוצאת לוואי (a side effect) לבין שימוש באדם ככלי מראים שלדעת המרצה התגובה עשויה לשקף הבדל מוסרי אמיתי.

_He answers the glitch view with I'm not so sure and contrasts a side effect with a person used as a tool._

questionText: What is the woman's main argument?

options.label: Drought had little to do with the fall of the great palace societies
A lack of copper and tin was the main reason the palaces fell
Their reliance on one another let local shortages spread widely
The societies fell because dry spells were new to them

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** המשפט What had changed, I think, is how dependent they'd become on one another (מה שהשתנה הוא התלות ההדדית בין הממלכות) והמשפט Each failure made the next one more likely מראים שהתלות הפיצה את המחסור.

_She says What had changed, I think, is how dependent they'd become on one another, and Each failure made the next one more likely._

questionText: What position does the man hold by the end of the conversation?

options.label: Drought was a minor factor that historians have tended to overstate
Drought alone can explain why so many centers fell together
Trade links made these kingdoms more resilient to bad harvests
Drought began the crisis, but ties between societies spread it

explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הצירוף drought alone has trouble explaining (קשה להסביר זאת בבצורת בלבד) והשאלה Without the drought, would the chain have started at all? מראים שהגבר מקבל את ההסבר של רשת הקשרים, אך רואה בבצורת את נקודת ההתחלה.

_He grants that drought alone has trouble explaining the collapse, yet asks Without the drought, would the chain have started at all?_

questionText: My uncle ________ an alarm clock, because the birds outside his window wake him every morning.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הנושא My uncle הוא גוף שלישי יחיד, ולכן בשלילה בהווה באה הצורה doesn't ואחריה פועל בצורת הבסיס: doesn't need (לא צריך).

_My uncle is third person singular, so the negative is doesn't + base form: doesn't need._

**הסבר מלא:** בזמן present simple יוצרים שלילה בעזרת פועל העזר do, ועם נושא בגוף שלישי יחיד, כמו My uncle (הדוד שלי), משתמשים בצורה doesn't. אחרי הצורה doesn't בא הפועל בצורת הבסיס, בלי הסיומת ‎-s‎, ולכן כותבים doesn't need (לא צריך). במשפט חיובי הפועל מקבל את הסיומת ‎-s‎ (My uncle needs), אבל במשפט שלילי הסיומת עוברת לפועל העזר does. הכלל: he/she/it + doesn't + פועל בצורת הבסיס.

שיטה: מה בא אחרי המילה — מזהים קודם את הנושא My uncle, שדורש את הצורה doesn't, ואחרי הצורה doesn't בא תמיד פועל בצורת הבסיס, ולכן התשובה היא doesn't need.

_What follows the word: My uncle needs doesn't, and doesn't is always followed by the base form: doesn't need._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

don't need — הצורה don't need מתאימה לנושאים I, you, we ו-they, ואילו הנושא My uncle הוא גוף שלישי יחיד ודורש את הצורה doesn't.

_don't goes with I, you, we and they; My uncle is third person singular and needs doesn't._

doesn't needs — בצורה doesn't needs סימן הגוף השלישי מופיע פעמיים: עם הנושא My uncle הסיומת כבר נמצאת בצורה doesn't, ולכן הפועל need נשאר בצורת הבסיס.

_With My uncle, the -s is already in doesn't, so the verb after it stays in the base form need._

not needs — הצורה not needs מעתיקה את המבנה העברי "לא צריך", ואילו באנגלית השלילה של נושא כמו My uncle בזמן present simple נוצרת בעזרת פועל העזר doesn't ופועל בצורת הבסיס.

_not needs copies the Hebrew; in the present simple, My uncle needs the helper doesn't + base form._

_In the present simple, a negative with a third-person singular subject like My uncle uses doesn't + base form: doesn't need._

**תשובה סופית: doesn't need**

distractorExplanations.a:
הצורה don't need מתאימה לנושאים I, you, we ו-they, ואילו הנושא My uncle הוא גוף שלישי יחיד ודורש את הצורה doesn't.

don't goes with I, you, we and they; My uncle is third person singular and needs doesn't.
distractorExplanations.c:
בצורה doesn't needs סימן הגוף השלישי מופיע פעמיים: עם הנושא My uncle הסיומת כבר נמצאת בצורה doesn't, ולכן הפועל need נשאר בצורת הבסיס.

With My uncle, the -s is already in doesn't, so the verb after it stays in the base form need.
distractorExplanations.d:
הצורה not needs מעתיקה את המבנה העברי "לא צריך", ואילו באנגלית השלילה של נושא כמו My uncle בזמן present simple נוצרת בעזרת פועל העזר doesn't ופועל בצורת הבסיס.

not needs copies the Hebrew; in the present simple, My uncle needs the helper doesn't + base form.

questionText: In the 1940s, some of the first computers ________ as large as a room and weighed several tons.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הביטוי In the 1940s מציין עבר, והנושא some of the first computers הוא ברבים, ולכן צריך את הצורה were (היו).

_In the 1940s points to the past, and some of the first computers is plural, so the verb is were._

**הסבר מלא:** הביטוי In the 1940s (בשנות הארבעים) והפועל weighed בהמשך המשפט מראים שמדובר בעבר, ולכן צריך צורת עבר של הפועל be. בעבר יש לפועל be שתי צורות: הצורה was לנושא ביחיד (I, he, she, it) והצורה were לנושא ברבים ולגוף you. הנושא some of the first computers (חלק מהמחשבים הראשונים) הוא ברבים, ולכן התשובה היא were (היו). הכלל: קודם בודקים את הזמן, ואחר כך את המספר של הנושא.

שיטה: מילות זמן — מחפשים קודם את מילות הזמן: הביטוי In the 1940s והפועל weighed מצביעים על עבר, ואחר כך הנושא ברבים some of the first computers בוחר את הצורה were.

_Time markers: Find the time marker first: In the 1940s and weighed mean past; the plural subject then gives were._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

was — הצורה was היא צורת עבר נכונה, ואולם היא מתאימה רק לנושא ביחיד, ואילו הנושא some of the first computers הוא ברבים.

_was is past but singular; some of the first computers is plural._

are — הצורה are מתאימה לנושא ברבים, ואולם היא בזמן הווה, ואילו הביטוי In the 1940s והפועל weighed מדברים על עבר.

_are is present, but In the 1940s and weighed describe the past._

been — הצורה been היא הצורה השלישית (past participle), והיא באה רק אחרי פועל עזר כמו have, ולכן אינה יכולה לבוא לבדה אחרי הנושא some of the first computers.

_been needs a helper such as have; it cannot follow some of the first computers on its own._

_In the 1940s and weighed show the past, and some of the first computers is plural, so the past form of be is were._

**תשובה סופית: were**

distractorExplanations.a:
הצורה was היא צורת עבר נכונה, ואולם היא מתאימה רק לנושא ביחיד, ואילו הנושא some of the first computers הוא ברבים.

was is past but singular; some of the first computers is plural.
distractorExplanations.b:
הצורה are מתאימה לנושא ברבים, ואולם היא בזמן הווה, ואילו הביטוי In the 1940s והפועל weighed מדברים על עבר.

are is present, but In the 1940s and weighed describe the past.
distractorExplanations.d:
הצורה been היא הצורה השלישית (past participle), והיא באה רק אחרי פועל עזר כמו have, ולכן אינה יכולה לבוא לבדה אחרי הנושא some of the first computers.

been needs a helper such as have; it cannot follow some of the first computers on its own.

questionText: Last summer my grandparents ________ across Portugal by train and sent us a postcard from every city.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הביטוי Last summer מציין זמן שהסתיים, ולכן צריך את הזמן past simple, כלומר את הצורה traveled (נסעו, טיילו).

_Last summer is a finished time, so the verb must be past simple: traveled._

**הסבר מלא:** הביטוי Last summer (בקיץ שעבר) מציין זמן שהסתיים, ואחרי זמן כזה משתמשים בזמן past simple. גם הפועל sent בהמשך המשפט נמצא בזמן עבר, ולכן הצורה traveled (נסעו, טיילו) מתאימה לשני חלקי המשפט. הכלל: עם ביטויי זמן של עבר שהסתיים, כמו yesterday, last year או in 2010, משתמשים בזמן past simple ולא בזמן present perfect.

שיטה: מילות זמן — קודם מחפשים את מילות הזמן במשפט: הביטוי Last summer והפועל sent מצביעים על עבר שהסתיים, ולכן צריך את הצורה בזמן past simple, כלומר traveled.

_Time markers: Find the time marker first: Last summer and sent point to a finished past, so the answer is the past simple traveled._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

have traveled — הזמן present perfect בצורה have traveled מקשר את העבר להווה, ולכן אינו יכול לבוא עם זמן שהסתיים כמו Last summer.

_The present perfect have traveled cannot go with a finished time like Last summer._

travel — הצורה travel היא בזמן present simple, שמתאר הרגל בהווה, ואילו הביטוי Last summer והפועל sent מדברים על עבר.

_travel is present simple, but Last summer and sent describe the past._

are traveling — הצורה are traveling היא בזמן present continuous, שמתאר פעולה בהווה או תוכנית לעתיד, ולכן אינה מתאימה לביטוי Last summer, שמציין זמן שהסתיים.

_are traveling describes the present or a future plan, not something that happened Last summer._

_Last summer is a finished time and sent is past too, so the verb is past simple: traveled._

**תשובה סופית: traveled**

distractorExplanations.a:
הזמן present perfect בצורה have traveled מקשר את העבר להווה, ולכן אינו יכול לבוא עם זמן שהסתיים כמו Last summer.

The present perfect have traveled cannot go with a finished time like Last summer.
distractorExplanations.c:
הצורה travel היא בזמן present simple, שמתאר הרגל בהווה, ואילו הביטוי Last summer והפועל sent מדברים על עבר.

travel is present simple, but Last summer and sent describe the past.
distractorExplanations.d:
הצורה are traveling היא בזמן present continuous, שמתאר פעולה בהווה או תוכנית לעתיד, ולכן אינה מתאימה לביטוי Last summer, שמציין זמן שהסתיים.

are traveling describes the present or a future plan, not something that happened Last summer.

questionText: Right now, my older sister ________ a chocolate cake in the kitchen for tonight's dinner.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** הביטוי Right now מציין פעולה שקורית ממש עכשיו, ולכן צריך את הזמן present continuous: is baking (אופה עכשיו).

_Right now marks an action in progress, so the verb is present continuous: is baking._

**הסבר מלא:** הביטוי Right now (ממש עכשיו) מראה שהפעולה מתרחשת ברגע הדיבור, ולפעולה כזאת משתמשים בזמן present continuous: צורה של הפועל be ועוד פועל עם הסיומת ‎-ing‎. הנושא my older sister הוא ביחיד, ולכן כותבים is baking (אופה עכשיו). בעברית יש זמן הווה אחד, ולכן קל לבחור בזמן present simple, אבל הזמן הזה מתאר הרגל או עובדה קבועה, ולא עוגה אחת שנאפית ברגע זה. הכלל: לפעולה שמתרחשת ברגע הדיבור, עם ביטויים כמו right now ו-at the moment, משתמשים בזמן present continuous.

שיטה: מילות זמן — מחפשים את מילות הזמן: הביטוי Right now מסמן פעולה שמתרחשת עכשיו, ולכן בוחרים בזמן present continuous, כלומר בצורה is baking.

_Time markers: Spot the time marker: Right now signals an action in progress, so choose the present continuous is baking._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

bakes — הצורה bakes היא בזמן present simple, שמתאר הרגל או עובדה קבועה, ואילו הביטוי Right now מתאר פעולה אחת שמתרחשת ברגע זה.

_bakes is present simple, for habits and facts, but Right now describes one action in progress._

was baking — הצורה was baking היא בזמן past continuous, שמתאר פעולה שהתרחשה בעבר, ולכן אינה מתאימה לביטוי Right now.

_was baking is past, but Right now refers to the present moment._

bake — הצורה bake היא צורת הבסיס, ולכן אינה מתאימה לנושא ביחיד כמו my older sister, וגם אינה מתארת פעולה שמתרחשת עכשיו (Right now).

_bake does not agree with my older sister and does not show an action in progress._

_Right now shows an action happening at the moment of speaking, so we use the present continuous: is baking._

**תשובה סופית: is baking**

distractorExplanations.a:
הצורה bakes היא בזמן present simple, שמתאר הרגל או עובדה קבועה, ואילו הביטוי Right now מתאר פעולה אחת שמתרחשת ברגע זה.

bakes is present simple, for habits and facts, but Right now describes one action in progress.
distractorExplanations.b:
הצורה was baking היא בזמן past continuous, שמתאר פעולה שהתרחשה בעבר, ולכן אינה מתאימה לביטוי Right now.

was baking is past, but Right now refers to the present moment.
distractorExplanations.d:
הצורה bake היא צורת הבסיס, ולכן אינה מתאימה לנושא ביחיד כמו my older sister, וגם אינה מתארת פעולה שמתרחשת עכשיו (Right now).

bake does not agree with my older sister and does not show an action in progress.

questionText: ________ three small islands in the middle of the lake, and visitors can reach them by boat.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** אחרי החסר בא שם עצם ברבים, three small islands, ולכן צריך את הצירוף There are (יש), שמתאים לרבים.

_The noun after the blank, three small islands, is plural, so the answer is There are._

**הסבר מלא:** כדי לומר "יש" במובן של "נמצא במקום", משתמשים באנגלית בצירוף there is או בצירוף there are, ולא בפועל have. הבחירה ביניהם תלויה בשם העצם שבא אחריהם: לפני שם עצם ביחיד כותבים there is, ולפני שם עצם ברבים כותבים there are. כאן בא אחרי החסר הצירוף three small islands (שלושה איים קטנים), ולכן התשובה היא There are. הפועל have מציין שייכות ("יש לי"), ולכן הוא צריך נושא לפניו.

שיטה: מה בא אחרי המילה — מסתכלים על מה שבא אחרי החסר: הצירוף three small islands הוא ברבים, ולכן צריך את הצירוף There are ולא את הצירוף There is.

_What follows the word: Look at what follows the blank: three small islands is plural, so use There are._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

There is — הצירוף There is בא לפני שם עצם ביחיד, ואילו אחרי החסר בא שם עצם ברבים, three small islands.

_There is goes before a singular noun, but three small islands is plural._

Have — הפועל Have הוא תרגום מילולי של "יש", ואולם הוא מציין שייכות וצריך נושא, ולכן אינו יכול לפתוח משפט שמתאר מה נמצא במקום מסוים, כמו בצירוף in the middle of the lake.

_Have shows possession and needs a subject; to say what is in the middle of the lake, English uses there are._

There have — הצירוף There have מערבב את המבנה there are עם הפועל have, ולפני שם עצם כמו three small islands המבנה הנכון הוא המילה there ואחריה צורה של הפועל be.

_There have mixes two structures; before three small islands, English uses there + a form of be._

_To say that something exists somewhere, English uses there is + singular or there are + plural, not have; three small islands is plural, so the answer is There are._

**תשובה סופית: There are**

distractorExplanations.a:
הצירוף There is בא לפני שם עצם ביחיד, ואילו אחרי החסר בא שם עצם ברבים, three small islands.

There is goes before a singular noun, but three small islands is plural.
distractorExplanations.b:
הפועל Have הוא תרגום מילולי של "יש", ואולם הוא מציין שייכות וצריך נושא, ולכן אינו יכול לפתוח משפט שמתאר מה נמצא במקום מסוים, כמו בצירוף in the middle of the lake.

Have shows possession and needs a subject; to say what is in the middle of the lake, English uses there are.
distractorExplanations.c:
הצירוף There have מערבב את המבנה there are עם הפועל have, ולפני שם עצם כמו three small islands המבנה הנכון הוא המילה there ואחריה צורה של הפועל be.

There have mixes two structures; before three small islands, English uses there + a form of be.

questionText: A pet parrot ________ many words it hears at home, but it usually does not know their meaning.
explanation:
**הסבר קצר:** גם כשהנושא הוא A pet parrot (תוכי מחמד) בגוף שלישי יחיד, אחרי פועל העזר can בא פועל בצורת הבסיס, ולכן התשובה היא can repeat (יכול לחזור על).

_Even with a singular subject like A pet parrot, can is followed by the base form: can repeat._

**הסבר מלא:** המילה can (יכול) היא פועל עזר מודאלי, ואחריה בא תמיד פועל בצורת הבסיס, בלי המילה to ובלי הסיומות ‎-s‎ או ‎-ing‎. הנושא A pet parrot הוא בגוף שלישי יחיד, ולכן קל להוסיף את הסיומת ‎-s‎ כמו בפועל hears, אבל אחרי המילה can הפועל אינו משתנה. לכן כותבים can repeat (יכול לחזור על), בדיוק כמו בצירופים she can swim ו-it can fly.

שיטה: מה בא אחרי המילה — אחרי המילה can בא תמיד פועל בצורת הבסיס, ולכן פוסלים כל צורה שיש בה את המילה to או את הסיומת ‎-s‎, ונשארת הצורה can repeat.

_What follows the word: After can comes the base form, so drop every option with to or -s: can repeat._

**למה לא האפשרויות האחרות**

can repeats — הצורה can repeats מוסיפה את הסיומת ‎-s‎ בגלל הנושא A pet parrot, ואולם אחרי פועל העזר can הפועל נשאר בצורת הבסיס.

_A pet parrot is singular, but after can the verb stays in the base form, with no -s._
